blind_assessment: Sweet, richly nut-toned. Hazelnut, baking chocolate, pear, fresh-cut fir, brown sugar in aroma and cup. Sweet-toned structure with brisk acidity; crispy, satiny mouthfeel. The finish consolidates to hazelnut and baking chocolate with undertones of fresh-cut fir.
notes: Produced by Nelson Martinez, the Bayter Brothers, and their mother, Marta Bayter, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and flesh are removed from the beans before they are dried). Located in southwestern Colorado, Durango Coffee lays claim to a rich coffee history that dates to 1986. Its motto is “Tough Town, Great Coffee.” Visit www.durangocoffee.com or call 800-748-2275 for more information.
bottom_line: A friendly, accessible Colombia cup: sweet and nutty with pleasing chocolate tones throughout.

title: Colombia Bueasco Decaf
blind_assessment: Very sweet, crisply cocoa-toned. Date, cocoa powder, Meyer lemon zest, agave syrup, oak in aroma and cup. Pert acidity; lightly satiny mouthfeel. Cocoa-toned finish supported by Meyer lemon zest and oak.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers, entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Decaffeinated in Colombia using ethyl acetate, a solvent derived from sugar cane. Utopian Coffee is a specialty roaster based in Fort Wayne, Indiana. Visit www.utopiancoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A solid EA (ethyl acetate) Colombia decaf characterized by a cocoa throughline with bittersweet citrus zest undertones.

title: Colombia Buenavista Ataraxia Geisha
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. In the aroma, lush, chocolaty fruit (maraschino cherry, ripe orange) transforms to a bright, floral citrus in the cup, slightly drying but sweet. Co-taster John DiRuocco (94) felt that the entire package came together nicely, with “nice high notes balanced by chocolate undertones, acidity by body.” Ken had less conviction in regard to coherence, but he too characterized the mouthfeel as full and plush, the cup impressive, and seconded John’s 94. Both particularly praised the coffee in three parts milk, where lemon, chocolate and cherry tendencies played nicely.
notes: Produced at Finca Buenavista, entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic washed method, in which the whole coffee fruit is subjected to anaerobic fermentation, after which the skins and pulp are removed, the coffee is anaerobically fermented a second time, and washed before drying. Imported directly by Euphora Coffee. Euphora is a Taipei-based specialty coffee roaster with an active online community through which all sales are made. Visit www.euphoracoffeestudio.com for more information.
bottom_line: A fine espresso for those who enjoy paradox: intense yet balanced; bright yet full.

title: Colombia Buenos Aires Honey Process-Yellow Velvet Peach
blind_assessment: Fruit-toned, tropical. Strawberry-guava, freesia, ginseng, elm, cocoa nib in aroma and cup. Vibrantly sweet, juicy acidity; full, syrupy mouthfeel. Long, complex finish that leads with ginseng notes, followed by cocoa nib.
notes: Produced at Finca Buenos Aires, entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method, in which the whole fruit is fermented in an oxygen-free environment before drying, in this case, with the addition of peaches to the fermentation. Ingenuity Coffee Roastery is a specialty coffee roaster based in Changhua, Taiwan. Visit https://shopee.tw/etmax123 for more information.
bottom_line: A powerfully aromatic, flavor-saturated, experimentally processed Colombia cup that has been co-fermented with peaches.

title: Colombia Buesaco
blind_assessment: Crisply cocoa- and berry-toned. Raspberry, cocoa nib, brown sugar, hazelnut, fir in aroma and cup. Sweet-tart structure with brisk acidity; full, syrupy mouthfeel. The gently drying finish consolidates to notes of brown sugar and fir.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Old World Coffee Roasters is a specialty coffee roaster with cafes in Reno and Carson City, Nevada. Visit OldWorldCoffeeRoasters.com for more information.
bottom_line: An easygoing, cocoa-driven natural-processed Colombia with berry notes throughout, supported by suggestions of rich aromatic wood.

title: Colombia Buesaco
blind_assessment: High-toned, crisply sweet-tart. Tangerine zest, cocoa nib, apricot, cedar, freesia-like flowers in aroma and cup. Brightly sweet-tart structure with lively, juicy acidity; satiny-smooth mouthfeel. The resonant finish centered around notes of cocoa nib, tangerine zest and cedar.
notes: Produced from trees of the Caturra, Castillo and Colombia varieties of Arabica and processed by the wet, or washed, method. Oak & Bond is a specialty retail and wholesale coffee roaster based in Charlotte, North Carolina. The company’s name combines “oak,” a reference to its first coffee, a barrel-aged release, and “bond,” referring to the founders’ happy marriage. For more information, visit www.oakandbondcoffee.com.
bottom_line: A balanced, engaging, classic Colombia cup: bright, chocolaty, deeply sweet, richly vibrant.

title: Colombia Cafe Granja La Esperanza Sidra Natural
blind_assessment: Fruit-centered, chocolaty, balanced. Lychee, cocoa nib, lavender, nutmeg, sandalwood in aroma and cup. Sweetly savory with juicy acidity; round, viscous mouthfeel. Long, lingering, flavor-saturated finish with pretty notes of lychee and cocoa nib supported by lavender.
notes: Produced by Rigoberto Herrera of Granja La Esperanza, entirely of the Sidra variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Founded in 2013, modcup coffee focuses on fresh roasting and distinctive natural-processed coffees. Visit modcup.com for more information.
bottom_line: A spice-toned Colombia Sidra cup that evokes the tropics with its lyrical fruit tones throughout — juicy, vivacious, very sweet.

title: Colombia Cafe La Granja Pink Bourbon
blind_assessment: Elegant, berry-driven, chocolaty. Wild strawberry, cocoa nib, hop flowers, cedar, tangerine in aroma and cup. Delicately bright, juicy acidity; vibrant, silky mouthfeel. Crisply cocoa-toned, strawberry PopTart finish supported by tangerine.
notes: Produced by Rigoberto Herrera at Granja La Esperanza in Colombia, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method, in which the coffee is fermented in the whole fruit with limited access to oxygen before drying. Founded in 2013, modcup coffee focuses on fresh roasting and distinctive natural-processed coffees. This special release is available to members of modcup’s Deepcuts list. Visit modcup.com for more information.
bottom_line: A lovely anaerobic Colombia Pink Bourbon with a distinct strawberry throughline, whose nuances range from wild-forest berry to just toasted PopTart. A fun one!
coffee_origin: Caicedonia, Valle del Cauca Department, Colombia

title: Colombia Cafe La Granja Sudan Rume Natural
blind_assessment: Rich-toned, complex, compelling. Narcissus, black cherry, cardamom, dark chocolate, lemongrass in aroma and cup. Savory-sweet structure with winey acidity; syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Flavor-saturated finish led by narcissus and cardamom with undertones of black cherry.
notes: Comprised entirely of beans from the rare Sudan Rume, a presumably very old variety of Arabica originally selected from wild trees growing on the Boma Plateau of Sudan, close to the border with Ethiopia. Produced by Rigoberto Herrera at Granja La Esperanza in Colombia and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Founded in 2013, modcup coffee focuses on fresh roasting and distinctive natural-processed coffees. This special release is available to members of modcup’s Deepcuts list. Visit modcup.com for more information.
bottom_line: An enigmatic, very complex natural-processed Colombia Sudan Rume, rich and very sweet, complicated by spicy florals, deep chocolate, and sweet herbs.
coffee_origin: Caicedonia, Valle del Cauca Department, Colombia

title: Colombia Caldas Finca Villa Clara Supremo
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Richly sweet, crisply chocolaty. Dark chocolate, date, magnolia, oak, a hint of marjoram in aroma and small cup. Satiny mouthfeel; crisp, chocolaty finish. In cappuccino-scaled milk, deep chocolate notes are further animated, as are magnolia-like florals.
notes: Produced by Carito Mejía of Finca Villa Clara from trees of the Caturra and Bourbon varieties of Arabica and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and flesh are removed from the beans before they are dried). CofFeeling Coffee is based in Kaohsiung City in southern Taiwan. Visit www.coffeelingcafe.com or call +886-7-285-5300 for more information.
bottom_line: A classic Colombia coffee, deep-toned and chocolaty, roasted for espresso. Particularly floral and rich in milk.

title: Colombia Caldas Laderas del Tapias
blind_assessment: Rich, deep, yet delicate. Tangerine, rose-like flowers, fresh-cut cedar, roasted cacao nib in aroma and cup. Lively, levitating acidity; light but silky mouthfeel. Flavor consolidates in a sweetly crisp finish.
notes: Established in the first decade of the twentieth-century, Finca Laderas del Tapias devotes forty-percent of its arable land to protected forest and is in the process of becoming Rainforest Alliance certified. Victrola is a small-batch, hands-on roaster with a passionate commitment to quality and distinctiveness. Visit www.victrolacoffee.com or call 206-624-1725 for more information.

title: Colombia Caldas Twilight Geisha Natural
blind_assessment: High-toned, sweetly tart. Raspberry, hazelnut, amber, cocoa nib, freesia in aroma and cup. Crisp, citrusy acidity; full, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Exceptionally resonant, lingering finish that carries over all the aroma and flavor notes from the cup.
notes: Comprised entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). 1980 Cafe is a Tainan City, Taiwan-based specialty coffee roaster. Visit www.1980cafetw.com for more information.
bottom_line: A berry-driven natural Colombia with undertones of amber and cocoa nib supported by spice-toned florals.

title: Colombia Calderon Honey
blind_assessment: Complex, spice-toned, floral. Ginger blossom, candied violet, clove, pomegranate, pink grapefruit zest in aroma and cup. Balanced, juicy acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Long, resonant, richly aromatic finish.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 11 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 30 Coffees of 2023. Produced by Luis Calderon of Finca Betulia, from trees of the Castillo, Colombia and Red Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic honey method, in which ripe cherries undergo a meticulous fermentation process in oxygen-free bags for 24-48 hours. Then the fruit skin is removed and the beans are fermented again for an additional 48 hours in closed containers. The beans then undergo precise mechanical drying, with careful attention paid to controlling Brix degrees, temperature, and pH levels. Revel Coffee is a micro-roaster located in Billings, Montana. Its motto: “Quality is paramount – a difference you can revel in.” Visit www.revelcoffee.com or call 406-534-9621 for more information.
bottom_line: An ethereally sweet, immersively rich-toned anaerobic Colombia with complex spice notes that enliven the cup.

title: Colombia Camilio Torres
blind_assessment: Rich, round, deep. Roasted nut, dusk flowers, cocoaish dark chocolate, melon-like fruit with a hint of citrus in aroma and cup. Wine-toned acidity; silky mouthfeel. The dry chocolate and melon suggestions carry into a long, resonant finish.
notes: Produced by members of the Camilio Torres cooperative, near the village of El Parasio, in the Huila coffee growing region. Temple Coffee is a quality-focused retail and wholesale specialty roaster active in Sacramento, California since 2005. Committed to sourcing, roasting and brewing the finest coffees, Temple features coffee from distinguished single estates and cooperatives around the world. Visit www.templecoffee.com or call 916-601-5363 for more information.

title: Colombia Camp Hermoso Sidra Washed
blind_assessment: Complex, floral- and fruit-toned. Raspberry, jasmine, wild honey, pink grapefruit, cocoa nib in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart structure with juicy acidity; silky, buoyant mouthfeel. Finish is long and resonant, carrying through fruit and floral sweetness supported by a quiet cocoa undercurrent.
notes: Produced by Edwin Noreña, entirely of the Sidra variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Bear Lake Coffee Co., a B Corp-certified coffeehouse and roastery located in Barronett, Wisconsin, is committed to sustainability through its Coffee with a Purpose™ initiative, which ensures that farmers receive compensation well above the Fairtrade Premium for their exceptional small-batch coffee. Visit www.bearlakecoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A standout washed Sidra: vibrant yet balanced, layering berry, citrus, and floral top notes over a deep cocoa foundation.

title: Colombia Campo Hermoso Pink Bourbon Washed
blind_assessment: Crisply sweet, fruit- and spice-driven. Red currant, blood orange, cocoa, cinnamon, tea rose in aroma and cup. Brightly sweet-tart structure with bright acidity; plush, satiny mouthfeel. Finish is clean and gently persistent, with fruit and spice lingering alongside distinct cocoa notes.
notes: Produced by Edwin Noreña, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Bear Lake Coffee Co., a B Corp-certified coffeehouse and roastery located in Barronett, Wisconsin, is committed to sustainability through its Coffee with a Purpose™ initiative, which ensures that farmers receive compensation well above the Fairtrade Premium for their exceptional small-batch coffee. Visit www.bearlakecoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: An elegant washed Pink Bourbon, animated by vivid fruit and floral tones and lifted by spice complexity and cocoa depth.

title: Colombia Cardona Natural
blind_assessment: Richly fruit-toned, sweetly fermenty. Raspberry coulis, chocolate fudge, wine barrel, narcissus, tangerine zest in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart with vibrant, juicy acidity; very full, syrupy mouthfeel. The fragrant finish suggests a barrel room full of red wine in process.
notes: Produced by Andres Cardona of Villa Lucia Farm from trees of the Castillo and Colombia varieties of Arabica and processed by the natural method. Nostalgia Coffee Roasters was founded by Taylor Fields in 2018 as a mobile café; since it has added specialty roasting and internet retailing of select fine coffees. Visit www.nostalgiacoffeeroasters.com for more information.
bottom_line: An attractively fruit-toned, natural-processed Colombia with a winey aroma and flavor, supported by notes of rich chocolate and sweet florals.

title: Colombia Carmen Montoya Chiroso
blind_assessment: Brightly sweet-tart, balanced. Nectarine, almond butter, tangerine, fresh-cut oak, bay leaf in aroma and cup. Sparkling acidity; crisp, satiny mouthfeel. FInish consolidates to notes of nectarine and bay leaf.
notes: Produced by Carmen Montoya, entirely of the Chiroso variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Big Shoulders Coffee is a Chicago artisan roaster that emphasizes a fresh-roasted, no-nonsense approach to fine coffee. Visit www.bigshoulderscoffee.com or call 312-846-1439 for more information.
bottom_line: A pretty, stone fruit-driven cup with sweet nut and complex citrus tones throughout.

title: Colombia Castillo Fruit Maceration Series (Grape)
blind_assessment: Candy-like, chocolaty. Jolly Roger candy, baking chocolate, bay leaf, crisped rice, cedar in aroma and cup. Tart-leaning structure with brisk acidity; full, satiny mouthfeel. Crisply tart finish with fruit and aromatic wood impulses.
notes: Produced by Jairo Arcila and Cofinet of Finca Santa Monica entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by an experimental fruit maceration process in which the whole fruit is first fermented in an anaerobic (limited oxygen) environment with wine yeasts and macerated fruit. After fermentation, the coffee cherries are pulped and placed to dry on raised beds with macerated fruits until the ideal moisture content is achieved. Founded in 2013, modcup coffee focuses on fresh roasting and distinctive natural-processed coffees. Visit modcup.com for more information.
bottom_line: A very sweet experimental Colombia cup that suggests the flavor of certain hard candies, complicated by a pleasing tartness and crisp, bracing chocolate.

title: Colombia Castillo Fruit Maceration Series (Passionfruit)
blind_assessment: Powerfully aromatic, fruit-centered. Passionfruit, lychee, ginger flower, almond brittle, kumquat in aroma and cup. Sweet-tart structure with apple-toned, malic acidity; full, syrupy mouthfeel. Exceptionally harmonious and integrated finish into the far long.
notes: Produced by Jairo Arcila and Cofinet of Finca Santa Monica entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by an experimental fruit maceration process in which the whole fruit is first fermented in an anaerobic (limited oxygen) environment with wine yeasts and macerated fruit. After fermentation, the coffee cherries are pulped and placed to dry on raised beds with macerated fruits until the ideal moisture content is achieved. Founded in 2013, modcup coffee focuses on fresh roasting and distinctive natural-processed coffees. Visit modcup.com for more information.
bottom_line: High-toned, explicitly and cleanly fruit-forward, leading with notes of passionfruit and lychee — tropics in a cup.

title: Colombia Castillo Fruit Maceration Series (Peach)
blind_assessment: Elegantly floral, richly sweet. White peach, lilac, cocoa nib, lemon-thyme, oak in aroma and cup. Sweet-tart structure with vivacious, juicy acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Gently fruit-driven finish with notes of lemon-thyme and oak.
notes: Produced by Jairo Arcila and Cofinet of Finca Santa Monica entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by an experimental fruit maceration process in which the whole fruit is first fermented in an anaerobic (limited oxygen) environment with wine yeasts and macerated fruit. After fermentation, the coffee cherries are pulped and placed to dry on raised beds with macerated fruits until the ideal moisture content is achieved. Founded in 2013, modcup coffee focuses on fresh roasting and distinctive natural-processed coffees. Visit modcup.com for more information.
bottom_line: A fruit-forward, experimentally processed Colombia fermented with macerated peaches, a method that amplifies the stone fruit inclinations of the cup.

title: Colombia Castillo Fruit Maceration Series (Strawberry)
blind_assessment: Sweetly tart, delicately bright. Berry melange, narcissus, cocoa nib, amber, agave syrup in aroma and cup. Brightly tart with brisk acidity; creamy, viscous mouthfeel. The long, resonant finish is flavor-saturated, balanced and complex.
notes: Produced by Jairo Arcila and Cofinet of Finca Santa Monica entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by an experimental fruit maceration process in which the whole fruit is first fermented in an anaerobic (limited oxygen) environment with wine yeasts and macerated fruit. After fermentation, the coffee cherries are pulped and placed to dry on raised beds with macerated fruits until the ideal moisture content is achieved. Founded in 2013, modcup coffee focuses on fresh roasting and distinctive natural-processed coffees. Visit modcup.com for more information.
bottom_line: While the co-fermentation with strawberries is not obvious in the cup, there’s an overt berry throughline here that isn’t afraid to take over — an invocation of summer desserts.

title: Colombia Castillo Special Fermentation Washed Fruit of Taiwan
blind_assessment: High-toned, tangy. Cocoa powder, peach kefir, jasmine, lychee, almond. Tartly sweet, roundly savory; full, plush mouthfeel. Rich-toned finish centered around notes of cocoa powder and peach kefir.
notes: Part of the Winemaker Green Coffee Series jointly developed by Bean Super and local wineries in Taiwan, this Colombia Castillo is anaerobically fermented with the addition of Taiwanese fruits, including grape pulp, to the fermentation. Riika Cafe is a specialty coffee roaster based in New Taipei City, Taiwan. For more information, visit instagram.com/riikacafe or email riikacafe@gmail.com.
bottom_line: A tangy, stonefruit-driven anaerobic Colombia supported by pretty floral and rich almond notes.

title: Colombia Caturra Anaerobic Natural
blind_assessment: Deeply sweet-savory. Watermelon candy (Jolly Rancher), chocolate fudge, oregano, cedar, hint of teriyaki sauce in aroma and cup. Savory-leaning structure with brisk acidity; lightly satiny mouthfeel. Salty, chocolaty finish.
notes: Produced by the Bayter Brothers of El Vergel Estate entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method (fermented in the whole fruit in a hermetically sealed vessel). Cafe Kreyol is a roaster in Manassas, Virginia with the mission of creating sustainable employment by way of specialty coffee. Visit www.cafekreyol.com or call 571-719-7018 for more information.
bottom_line: Almost dessert-like in its sweetness, this anaerobically processed Caturra exhibits candy-like aromas and flavors with a savory edge.

title: Colombia Caturra Chiroso
blind_assessment: Crisply sweet, balanced. Goji berry, mandarin, freesia, thyme, cocoa nib in aroma and cup. Briskly sweet acidity; lightly satiny, very smooth mouthfeel. Cocoa-toned finish with notes of freesia and thyme.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers in the Argentina and Pitalito Municipalities, entirely of the Chiroso variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Speedwell Coffee, based in Plymouth, Massachusetts, is a wholesale and retail specialty roaster particularly dedicated to offering attractive coffee subscription plans. For more information, visit www.speedwellcoffee.com.
bottom_line: Notes of spice-toned florals and cocoa nib carry this understated Colombia Chiroso that’s satisfying in its balance.

title: Colombia Cauca At’e
blind_assessment: High-toned, richly sweet, delicately tart. Apple blossom, pomegranate, toffee, narcissus, cedar in aroma and cup. Sweet-tart structure with juicy, vibrant acidity; syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Resonant finish consolidates to toffee and cedar with a hint of narcissus-like flowers in the long.
notes: Available for delivery in the San Francisco Bay Area; no mail order. Produced entirely of the Colombia and Caturra varieties of Arabica and processed by the wet, or washed, method. Founded by roaster Keith Gehrke in 2015, States Coffee is a single-location community-focused coffee shop in downtown Martinez, California, featuring coffee roasted in-house and artisan baked goods. Visit www.statescoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A bright, lively Colombia cup with tart fruit, sweet floral, and deep toffee notes throughout — elegantly structured.

title: Colombia Cauca Castillo K-01
blind_assessment: Richly spiced-toned, elegantly aromatic. Ginger blossom, nutmeg, lavender, lemon verbena, baking chocolate in aroma and cup. Malic (apple-like) acidity; silky, viscous mouthfeel. Spice-toned finish into the long.
notes: Produced by Diego Bermudez of Finca El Paraiso, entirely of the Castillo K-01 variety of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic washed method, in which the fermentation step occurs in a hermetically sealed vessel (and includes the addition of alcohols yeasts) before the beans are washed and dried. Jaunt Coffee Roasters is a San Diego-based roaster and café with an extensive coffee and food menu. Visit www.jauntcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: An herbal tea-like aromatic profile with notes of baking spices and sweet florals characterizes this inviting, double-anaerobic Colombia.

title: Colombia Cauca Castillo YN-05
blind_assessment: Very sweet, complexly fruit-forward. Red plum, mango, freesia, cocoa nib, nougat in aroma and cup. Sparkling acidity; crisp, satiny mouthfeel. Cocoa-toned, fruity finish.
notes: Produced by Diego Bermudez of Finca El Paraiso, entirely of the Castillo YN-05 variety of Arabica, and processed by a complexly detailed version of the double-anaerobic method (sealed-tank fermentation of the whole fruit with the addition of yellow-fruit yeast, removal of skin and pulp, and a second fermentation of the beans shut in the tank with the removed skin and pulp). Additional processing nuance includes a thermal shock wash (soaking the whole fruit in hot water for 30 seconds, then cold water for 30 seconds) to reduce astringency. Jaunt Coffee Roasters is a San Diego-based roaster and café with an extensive coffee and food menu. Visit www.jauntcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A very sweet, very clean anaerobic cup fermented with yellow-fruit yeast for a subtle yet distinctive brightness.

title: Colombia Cauca El Paraiso
blind_assessment: Lyrically sweet, juicy, elegantly bright. Strawberry guava, coconut, hop flowers, narcissus, lemon balm in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart with juicy, tantalizing acidity; delicate, very silky mouthfeel. Resonant, long, flavor-saturated finish.
notes: SOT Coffee Roaster, based in Osaka, Japan, is a Swedish-style roaster with a self-described “aggressively light” roasting style. This coffee was produced by Diego Samuel Bermudez Tapia of the Castillo, Caturra and Colombia varieties of Arabica and processed by a “double-anaerobic method” (subject to oxygen-restricted fermentation first in the whole fruit, then, after skins are removed, in the fruit flesh). For more information, visit www.sotcoffee.com.
bottom_line: An exquisitely refined ultra-light-roasted coffee from Japan, all fruit and flowers, at turns delicate and mysterious, and consistently confident and engaging.

title: Colombia Cauca Finca EI Paraiso 92 Pink Bourbon
blind_assessment: Brightly sweet, deeply fruit- and cocoa-toned. Raspberry jam, dark chocolate, thyme, peach, frankincense in aroma and cup. Balanced, vibrant acidity;very silky, very smooth mouthfeel. Jammy cocoa-toned finish.
notes: Produced by Wilton Benitez of Granja Paraiso 92, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the thermal shock method, in which the coffee fruit, after having been first sanitized with ozone, undergoes two stages of fermentation. First, the whole cherries are submerged under water for 48 hours, then the beans are pulped and fermented with a strain of Lactobacillus for 24 hours. After fermentation, the beans are given a “thermal shock” using hot and cold rinses to help the beans absorb the fermentation metabolites and halt any further fermentation. Afterward, the washed parchment coffee is rapidly dried with an in-house designed Eco-Enigma dehumidifying dryer to avoid over-oxidation or continued fermentation. Bargain Cafe is a specialty coffee roaster in Taitung, Taiwan. Visit www.bargain-cafe.com for more information.
bottom_line: A nuanced, complex, invitingly rich Colombia anaerobic Pink Bourbon with grace, depth and balance.

title: Colombia Cauca Finca El Paraiso Double Anaerobic Flor Lichi
blind_assessment: Tropical fruit-toned. Mango, orange zest, dark chocolate, marjoram, oak in aroma and cup. Very sweet structure with brisk acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Chocolaty, fruity finish.
notes: Produced by Diego Bermudez of Finca al Paraiso, from trees of the Castillo, Colombia and Caturra varieties of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobi washed method, in which the coffee fruit, after having been first sanitized with ozone, undergoes two stages of fermentation. First, the whole cherries are submerged under water for 48 hours, then the beans are pulped and fermented with a strain of Lactobacillus for 24 hours. After fermentation, the beans are given a “thermal shock” using hot and cold rinses to help the beans absorb the fermentation metabolites and halt any further fermentation. Afterward, the washed parchment coffee is rapidly dried with an in-house designed Eco-Enigma dehumidifying dryer to avoid over-oxidation or continued fermentation. Lee Dong Coffee is a specialty coffee roaster and cafe in Taichung, Taiwan. Visit www.facebook.com/LiDongcoffee/ for more information.
bottom_line: A tropically fruity anaerobic Colombia with undertones of dark chocolate throughout.

title: Colombia Cauca Finca El Paraiso Double-Anaerobic Flor Lychee
blind_assessment: Resonantly floral, fruit-driven. Narcissus, pomegranate, amber, dark chocolate in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart structure with gently bright, fruity acidity; lively, viscous mouthfeel. The rich, concentrated finish centers around notes of pomegranate and dark chocolate with lush undertones of amber.
notes: Produced by Diego Bermudez entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic washed method, in which the fermentation step occurs in a hermetically sealed vessel before the beans are washed and dried. JYL Cafe is a specialty coffee roaster and cafe in Changhua, Taiwan. Visit https://line.me/ti/p/5YHFz4U0tW for more information.
bottom_line: This Colombia anaerobic offers and unrestrained experience of sweet-tart fruit and rich florals that play off each other in synergistic harmony.

title: Colombia Cauca Finca El Paraiso Rose Tea
blind_assessment: Richly aromatic, gently tart. Tamarind, magnolia, oak, pistachio, pink grapefruit zest in aroma and cup. Sweetly tarty structure with gently brisk acidity; crisp, satiny mouthfeel. Gently drying finish centered around notes of tamarind and oak with pistachio undertones.
notes: Produced by Diego Bermudez entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic washed method, in which the fermentation step occurs in a hermetically sealed vessel before the beans are washed and dried. Rubasse Coffee Roaster is a specialty roaster based in New Taipei City, Taiwan. Visit rubasseroasters.com/ for more information.
bottom_line: A Colombia anaerobic with tart fruit notes at the top of the profile and richly sweet floral undertones.

title: Colombia Cauca Granja Paraiso 92 – Pink Bourbon
blind_assessment: Exuberant yet coherent anaerobic. Butterscotch, blueberry, cocoa, lilac, candycap mushroom in aroma and cup. Sweet, tart and savory impulses balance in a richly expressive structure. Plush, lightly syrupy mouthfeel. Fruit notes consolidate in a long though quiet finish.
notes: Produced by Wilton Benitez of Finca El Paraíso entirely of the rare Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by a complexly detailed version of the double-anaerobic method (sealed-tank fermentation of the whole fruit with the addition of brewer’s yeast, removal of skin and pulp, and a second fermentation of the beans shut in the tank with the removed skin and pulp). Additional processing nuance includes a thermal shock wash (soaking the whole fruit in hot water for 30 seconds, then cold water for 30 seconds) to reduce astringency. Reprise Coffee is a quality-oriented small-batch roaster and café located in Lake Forest, Illinois, north of Chicago. Visit repriseroasters.com for more information.
bottom_line: A fruit-forward but balanced, tangy-rich rendition of the anaerobic style.

title: Colombia Cauca Lusitania Geisha Washed
blind_assessment: Bright, balanced, floral-toned. Star jasmine, guava nectar, almond nougat, bay leaf, blood orange in aroma and cup. Vibrant, sparkling acidity; very silky, lively mouthfeel. Notes of star jasmine and cocoa nib commingle in the finish.
notes: Produced by Consuelo Marín and Javier Macias of Finca Lusitania, entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Buon Caffe is a specialty coffee roaster and cafe in Taipei, Taiwan. Visit www.buoncaffe.com.tw for more information.
bottom_line: With tropical florals on the nose and tropical fruit on the palate, this meticulous Colombia Geisha delivers complex sweetness and depth while remaining even-keeled throughout the profile.

title: Colombia Cauca Paraiso 92 Double-Anaerobic P-07
blind_assessment: Explosively aromatic, fruit-saturated and confectionary. Strawberry, passionfruit, blood orange, tea rose and vanilla fudge in aroma and cup. Vibrant, juicy acidity; plush, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. The finish is intensely rich and aromatic, with concentrated notes of strawberry, rose and vanilla fudge.
notes: This coffee earned Finalist recognition in the Experimental category, International division, of the inaugural Kenneth Davids Cup. Produced by Wilton Benitez of Granja Paraiso 92, and processed by the double-anaerobic thermal shock method, in which the coffee fruit, after having been first sanitized with ozone, undergoes two stages of fermentation. First, the whole cherries are submerged under water for 48 hours, then the beans are pulped and fermented with a strain of Lactobacillus for 24 hours. Lastly, this lot also underwent ultrasound treatment, in which the enzymatic hydrolysis process breaks down complex sugars to generate a high concentration of simple sugars. Cozy House Coffee is a Taiwan-based specialty coffee roaster and an SCA Authorized Trainer (AST). For more information, visit shop.cozyhousecoffee.com.
bottom_line: A dramatically expressive anaerobic whose elaborate processing drives intense fruit, florals and confectionary sweetness while maintaining transparent clarity and structure.

title: Colombia Cauca Paraiso 92 Orange Bourbon Double-Anaerobic P17
blind_assessment: Intensely aromatic, fruit-saturated and confectionary. Mandarin, red guava, yellow peach, orange blossom and chocolate fudge in aroma and cup. Vibrant, juicy-bright acidity; viscous, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. The finish is exceptionally persistent and aromatic, with mandarin, orange blossom and chocolate fudge notes.
notes: This coffee earned Finalist recognition in the Experimental category, International division, of the inaugural Kenneth Davids Cup. Produced by Wilton Benitez of Granja Paraiso 92, entirely of the Orange Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic thermal shock method, in which the coffee fruit, after having been first sanitized with ozone, undergoes two stages of fermentation. First, the whole cherries are submerged under water for 48 hours, then the beans are pulped and fermented with a strain of Lactobacillus for 24 hours. Lastly, this lot also underwent ultrasound treatment, in which the enzymatic hydrolysis process breaks down complex sugars to generate a high concentration of simple sugars. OLI Cafe Roaster is a specialty coffee roaster based in Taichung Dali, Taiwan. Visit OLI Cafe's LinkTree for more information.
bottom_line: A fruit bomb of an Orange Bourbon in which double-anaerobic processing intensifies the variety’s citrus and tropical-fruit character, while florals and deep chocolate sweetness bring complexity and ballast.

title: Colombia Cauca Paraiso 92 Striped Bourbon Double-Anaerobic Thermal Shock P19
blind_assessment: Opulently aromatic, tangy-sweet and spice-laced. Pomegranate, tamarind, ruby grapefruit, wisteria and cinnamon bark in aroma and cup. Bright, electric acidity; full, satiny-smooth mouthfeel. The finish is expansive and complex, with notes of pomegranate, tamarind and cinnamon bark.
notes: This coffee earned Finalist recognition in the Experimental category, International division, of the inaugural Kenneth Davids Cup. Produced by Wilton Benitez of Granja Paraiso 92, entirely of the Striped Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic thermal shock method, in which the coffee fruit, after having been first sanitized with ozone, undergoes two stages of fermentation. First, the whole cherries are submerged under water for 48 hours, then the beans are pulped and fermented with a strain of Lactobacillus for 24 hours. Lastly, this lot also underwent ultrasound treatment, in which the enzymatic hydrolysis process breaks down complex sugars to generate a high concentration of simple sugars. Lean Coffee Roasters is a specialty coffee roaster and cafe in Taiching, Taiwan. Visit Lean Coffee’s Facebook for more information.
bottom_line: A riveting Striped Bourbon whose elaborate processing produces an unusual tension between tart red fruit, citrus, florals and warm spice, with striking intensity and definition.

roaster: La Golondrina by Counter Culture Coffee
title: Colombia Cauca, Special Micro-Lot Selection Juvenal Penna
blind_assessment: Sweet-toned, quietly complex aroma: cherryish, chocolate-toned fruit with a hint of herby cedar. In the cup softly acidy and richly and exquisitely balanced, with the fruit taking on a distinct black cherry character. A coffee whose excellence ultimately lies in its suave authority and completeness.
notes: La Golondrina represents a coffee partnership between Counter Culture's green buyer and roastmaster Peter Guiliano and Colombians Alejandro Cadena and Giancarlo Gianetti to together identify, encourage and promote through paying high premiums exceptional coffees produced by small farmers in the Inza region of Cauca Department, including this one produced by farmer Juvenal Penna. The founders named their project La Golondrina or "The Swallow" because the swallow is symbol of communication between people separated by distance and borders. Counter Culture Coffee is a small-batch wholesale specialty roaster with an informative and lively website, a commitment to fine coffee and youthful, enthusiastic leadership. Visit www.counterculturecoffee.com or call 888-238-5282 for more information.

title: Colombia Cauca
blind_assessment: Softly tart, nut-toned. Roasted cacao-nib, hazelnut, tea rose, blood orange in aroma and cup. Crisply sweet, juicy acidity; satiny, lively mouthfeel. Flavor persists, delicately but sweetly, in a clean, satisfying finish.
notes: Some of Colombia’s most admired coffees are produced in the southwestern Department of Cauca. Founded in 1990, Lexington Coffee is an award-winning artisan roasting company based in Virginia. Lexington’s focus on fresh, flavorful and sustainable coffee is reflected in its motto, “Fresh, Flavorful & Fair.” Visit www.lexingtoncoffee.com or call 800-322-6505 for more information.
coffee_origin: Valle de Cauca Department, southwestern Colombia.

title: Colombia Cerro Azul Enano
blind_assessment: Delicate in the nose, syrupy in the cup, quietly complex throughout. Honey, distinct dark chocolate, lemon zest, peach, violet in aroma and cup. Richly and complexly expressed acidity; full, lightly syrupy mouthfeel. A mildly drying but long and resonant finish, with pleasing hints of the peach and violet persisting.
notes: The unpredictability of coffee is confirmed once again with this striking sample, produced from trees that are apparently a spontaneous hybrid involving the famous Gesha (also Geisha) variety of Arabica. The producers Granja la Esperanza brought Gesha plant material from Panama, where this celebrated variety was first rediscovered, to Colombia, where they established it on their farm Cerro Azul. Some of the trees proved not to resemble the trees of the classic Gesha, however; they grew smaller and denser. The producers have given the name “Enano” or dwarf to this apparent hybrid of Gesha. Based on the slim evidence of the two samples of the Enano we have tested at Coffee Review, the result in the cup is a profile similar to the finest examples of bonafide Gesha, though perhaps a bit less intense in its Geshaness. Founded in 1995, Equator Coffees & Teas is a women-owned wholesale coffee roasting company with web-based retail and two recently-established cafés plus more on the way. Equator focuses on sustainability in coffee sourcing and business practices. Visit www.equatorcoffees.com or call 800-809-7687 for more information.
coffee_origin: Valle del Cauca growing region, Colombia.

title: Colombia Cerro Azul Enano
blind_assessment: Elegantly fruit- and cocoa-toned. Strawberry guava, cocoa nib, cane sugar, tea rose, cedar in aroma and cup. Delicately sweet structure with gently bright acidity; crisp, syrupy mouthfeel. A resonant finish centers around notes of cocoa nib and tea rose.
notes: Produced at Finca Cerro Azul (also owners of Granja La Esperanza), entirely of the Enano (dwarf Geisha) variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and flesh are removed from the beans before they are dried). Founded in 1995 by Brooke McDonnell and Helen Russell, Equator Coffees operates retail stores in the San Francisco Bay Area and southern California and provides coffee to hundreds of wholesale accounts. Visit www.equatorcoffees.com or call 800-809-7687 for more information.
bottom_line: This rare Enano (dwarf Geisha) excites with high-toned fruit, crisp cocoa, and rich floral notes throughout.
coffee_origin: Trujillo, Valle del Cauca Department, Colombia

title: Colombia Cerro Azul Enano
blind_assessment: Intensely floral, deeply complex. Rose- and lavender-like flowers, honey, cacao nib, apricot, a delicate hint of cashew in aroma and cup. Gently buoyant, lively acidity, light but very silky mouthfeel. Lavender and cashew in particular persist in a sweet-toned, balanced finish.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the #28 coffee in the Coffee Review Top 30 Coffees of 2014. The unpredictability of coffee is confirmed once again with this striking sample, produced from trees that are apparently a spontaneous hybrid involving the famous Gesha (also Geisha) variety of Arabica. The producers Granja la Esperanza brought Gesha plant material from Panama, where this celebrated variety was first rediscovered, to Colombia, where they established it on their farm Cerro Azul. Some of the trees proved not to resemble the trees of the classic Gesha, however; they grew smaller and denser. The producers have given the name “Enano” or dwarf to this apparent hybrid of Gesha. Based on the slim evidence of this single sample of the Enano, the result in the cup is a profile similar to the finest examples of bonafide Gesha, though perhaps a bit less intense in its Geshaness. Founded in 1995, Equator Coffees & Teas is a women-owned wholesale coffee roasting company with web-based retail and two recently-established cafés plus more on the way. Equator focuses on sustainability in coffee sourcing and business practices. Visit www.equatorcoffees.com or call 800-809-7687 for more information.
coffee_origin: Valle del Cauca growing region, Colombia.

title: Colombia Cerro Azul Geisha
blind_assessment: Richly aromatic, chocolaty, fruit-toned. Dark chocolate, dried mango, honeysuckle, wine barrel, marjoram in aroma and cup. Richly sweet structure with winey acidity; plush, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. The long, lingering finish centers around notes of dark chocolate and spicy florals.
notes: Produced by Rigoberto Herrera of Granja La Esperanza entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (sun-dried in the whole fruit). Bird Rock Coffee Roasters is a retailer and wholesaler focused on organic and socially responsible coffees; it was named the “2012 Micro-Roaster of the Year” by Roast Magazine. Visit www.birdrockcoffee.com or call 858-551-1707 for more information.
bottom_line: A trifecta of fruit, chocolate and flowers, both levitatingly sweet and structurally grounded.
coffee_origin: Trujillo, Valle del Cauca Department, Colombia

title: Colombia Cerro Azul Geisha
blind_assessment: Intense yet delicate; crisp, graceful. A tightly layered, utterly pleasing fusion of lavender-like flowers, roasted cacao nib and a hint of blood orange carries with clarity and consistency from aroma through finish. Lyrical, animated acidity; light but silky, lively mouthfeel. The finish never seems to stop; the floral-cacao-citrus notes ring on and on.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the #25 coffee in the Coffee Review Top 30 Coffees of 2014. Produced from trees of the rare Ethiopia-derived botanical variety Gesha (also spelled Geisha). Gesha was planted on the Granja La Esperanza farms as part of a ten-year project to improve coffee quality and to introduce new botanical varietals to Colombia; Cerro Azul is one of those farms. With its generally elongated beans and distinctive floral and chocolate cup, the Gesha variety continues to distinguish itself as one of the world's most unique coffees. Tony’s Coffee has been roasting in Bellingham, Washington since 1971. Visit www.tonyscoffee.com or call 800-448-8804 for more information.
coffee_origin: Valle del Cauca growing region, Colombia.

title: Colombia Chachagüí Mild Roast
blind_assessment: Chocolaty-sweet, fruit-forward. Baking chocolate, red grape, pink peppercorn, freesia, oak in aroma and cup. Gentle, round acidity; plush, creamy mouthfeel. Chocolaty finish with undertones of pink peppercorn.
notes: Produced by the Guerrero, Sepulveda and Trejos families, from trees of the Castillo, Caturra and Colombia varieties of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Rusty Dog Coffee is a Madison, Wisconsin-based specialty coffee roaster. Visit www.rustydogcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: Crisp chocolate and sweet-tart fruit notes are front and center in this cleanly natural-processed Colombia cup with spicy floral notes throughout.

title: Colombia Chachagüí Mild Roast
blind_assessment: Sweetly spice-toned, delicately aromatic. Ginger blossom, clove, narcissus, cocoa nib, goji berry in aroma and cup. Gently bright, balanced acidity; vibrant, silky mouthfeel. Crisp, cocoa-toned finish supported by notes of ginger blossom and clove.
notes: Produced by the Guerrero, Sepulveda and Trejos families, from trees of the Castillo, Caturra and Colombia varieties of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Rusty Dog Coffee is a Madison, Wisconsin-based specialty coffee roaster. Visit www.rustydogcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: An enigmatic, complex, natural-processed Colombia driven by notes of warming spices with floral and cocoa tones throughout the profile.

title: Colombia Chili Bourbon
blind_assessment: Sweetly spice-toned, uniquely composed. Szechuan peppercorn, lemon balm, dark chocolate, lavender, date in aroma and cup. Winy acidity; crisp, syrupy mouthful. Chocolaty, spice-toned finish.
notes: Produced by Edwin Noreña of Finca Campo Hermoso, entirely of the Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the carbonic maceration method, as follows: The whole fruit is co-fermented with aji chili must in oxygen-free containers for 96 hours. The fruit is then semi-washed (some of the fruit flesh is left on the bean), then returned to the carbonic fermentation tanks and re-infused with fresh aji chili must for an additional 48 hours. After the secondary carbonic fermentation, the coffee is dried on raised beds for 22 days and then set in a relative humidity-controlled warehouse for a final eight days of repose. Barrington Coffee is an artisan roaster dedicated to elite coffees, fresh delivery, and roasting that foregrounds the coffee and not the roast. Visit www.barringtoncoffee.com or call 800-528-0998 for more information.
bottom_line: A wild ride of a coffee with distinct notes of peppercorn (the coffee was co-fermented with aji chili) that’s also a fruity and fun carbonic-macerated cup.

title: Colombia Chiroso Caturra Washed
blind_assessment: Floral-toned, super-sweet. Wisteria, cocoa nib, rambutan, black sage, salted caramel in aroma and cup. Malic (apple-like) acidity; plush, viscous mouthfeel. Concentrated finish that carries through on the promise of the cup.
notes: Produced at Finca Granito de Oro, entirely of the Caturra Chiroso variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Founded in 2013, modcup coffee focuses on fresh roasting and distinctive natural-processed coffees. Visit modcup.com for more information.
bottom_line: A decadently sweet, richly perfumed Colombia from a lesser-known variety — confident, high-toned, floral and deep.

title: Colombia Chiroso Natural
blind_assessment: Crisply sweet-tart, high-toned. Meyer lemon zest, cocoa nib, hazelnut, dried hibiscus flower, marjoram in aroma and cup. Bright, tart-leaning structure with juicy acidity; delicate, silky mouthfeel. Citrusy finish supported by tart florals and cocoa nib.
notes: Produced by Wilson Roldan entirely of the Chiroso variety of Arabica and processed by the natural method (beans are dried in the whole fruit). Paradise Roasters specializes in micro-lot Arabica and Robusta coffees from Asia and other emerging origins. The company prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.
bottom_line: A vibrantly rich Colombia cup from the rare Chiroso variety of Arabica, grown only in parts of Colombia and offered by Paradise for the first time.

title: Colombia Cumbarco Lot 397
blind_assessment: Crisply chocolaty, richly nut-toned. Baking chocolate, almond butter, plum, cedar, maple syrup in aroma and cup. Sweet structure with juicy acidity; velvety mouthfeel. The flavorful finish leads with notes of baking chocolate and almond with hints of plum.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers surrounding the famous Café La Granja La Esperanza farm from trees of the Caturra, Castillo and Colombia varieties of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method at La Granja. modcup coffee, founded in 2013, focuses on fresh roasting and distinctive natural-processed coffees. Visit modcup.com for more information.
bottom_line: A classic washed Colombia cup with crisp stonefruit notes, balanced acidity, a richly sweet structure.
coffee_origin: Caicedonia, Valle de Cauca Department, Colombia

title: Colombia Cup of Excellence 2011 First Place Winner
blind_assessment: Bright, high-toned complexity: sweet, rose-like floral notes, milk chocolate, lemony cherry, a hint of pungent fir. Rich, zesty acidity; lightly syrupy mouthfeel. The finish is deep and long with echoes of flowers and chocolate.
notes: The Cup of Excellence is the most esteemed competition for green coffees from a given country of origin; this was the first prize winner from the Colombia 2011 competition chosen by a select group of national and international cuppers. From Arnulfo Leguizamo’s Primavera farm and Rainforest Alliance certified, meaning it was produced following sustainable ecological and socio-economic criteria developed by the Sustainable Agricultural Network, a coalition of independent, environment-focused non-governmental organizations. Paradise Roasters prides itself on roasting and shipping coffee only after orders are placed. Its metaphoric mission is to bring some paradisiacal warmth from the coffee-growing south to the cool environs of Minnesota. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.
coffee_origin: San Agustín growing region, Huila Department, southern Colombia

title: Colombia Cup of Excellence Lot #8 Hato Viejo
blind_assessment: Very sweet-toned aroma with orange and pipe-tobacco notes. In the cup rich, wine-like acidity, syrupy mouthfeel, and a delicate yet rich structure with continued orange and fresh pipe-tobacco notes. Rich, long, sweet finish.
notes: A prize winner in the 2006 Colombia Second Harvest Cup of Excellence competition, where as a green (unroasted) coffee it placed eighth out of hundreds of entries, attracting a score of 88.65 from an international jury. Produced from trees of the caturra variety at an impressive elevation of approximately 6,000 feet by farmer Alvaro Flavio Ortega. Torreo Coffee Roasters is a Philadelphia-based small-batch artisan roasting company specializing in high-end coffees brought to light to medium roast levels designed to foreground the character of the green coffees. Visit www.torreo.com or call 888-286-7736 for more information.

title: Colombia Daniel Ortega
blind_assessment: Subtly complex, richly spice-toned. Brown sugar, apple blossom, date, allspice, fresh pipe tobacco in aroma and cup. Bright, vibrant, balanced in structure; crisp, velvety-smooth mouthfeel. The flavor-saturated finish leads with sweet floral and fruit tones in the short modulating to tobacco and spice in the long.
notes: Produced by Daniel Ortega of Finca Buenos Aires from trees of the Caturra and Castillo varieties of Arabica. Processed by the wet or washed method (fruit skin and pulp are removed before drying). Branch Street Coffee Roasters is a small-batch specialty coffee roaster in Youngstown, Ohio. Under the careful eye of owner/roaster Matthew Campbell, each coffee is individually profiled and cupped to ensure peak flavor and consistency.Visit www.branchstreetcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A rich, complex, rather atypical Colombia coffee that deepens as you linger with the cup: bright but resonant, deeply spice-toned.

title: Colombia Dark Roast Decaf
blind_assessment: Dominated by a low-toned but richly intense fruit complex that in the aroma clearly and pleasurably reads as semi-sweet chocolate. In the cup turns toward something less chocolate and more cherry perhaps, with a little pungent lean toward Mediterranean herbs. Full-bodied and deeply dimensioned throughout.
notes: No decaffeination method is noted on the package, which probably means this Colombia was decaffeinated by the conventional or direct solvent method. CC's Coffee is the upscale specialty line of Community Coffee, a distinguished family-owned coffee company founded in 1919. Visit www.cc-coffee.com or call 800-535-9149 for more information.

title: Colombia Dark Roast Decaf
blind_assessment: Wonderfully robust balance of sweet, roasty, and roundly acidy tones, with sweetness in the ascendancy. Some fruity complication, but the main appeal is pure, classic Latin-America coffee expression. The dark roast rounds and sweetens the acidity but leaves little bitterness behind.
notes: This very characteristic Colombia was decaffeinated by the conventional or direct solvent method. CC's Coffee is the upscale specialty line of Community Coffee, a distinguished family-owned coffee company founded in 1919. Visit www.cc-coffee.com or call 800-800-535-9149 for more info.

title: Colombia David Gomez 100% Caturra
blind_assessment: Crisply sweet, spice-toned. Dried papaya, caramel, tangerine zest, pink-peppercorn, vanilla in aroma and cup. High-toned, sweetly tart in structure with juicy, bright acidity; lean, though satiny-smooth mouthfeel. The resonant, richly drying finish is laden with sweet notes of caramel and papaya in the short, turning more savory-leaning in the long, with hints of pink peppercorn wrapped in vanilla.
notes: Produced by David Gomez of of El Balso Farm entirely from trees of the Caturra variety of Arabica. Like almost all Colombia coffees, this coffee is wet-processed or “washed,” meaning the fruit skin and pulp were removed from the beans immediately after harvesting and before drying. Huila is one of Colombia’s most respected coffee-growing regions. Husband and wife team Samantha and Weston Nawrocki founded Manzanita Roasting on their family’s 127-year-old winery in San Diego. Committed to quality direct-trade sourcing and skillful roasting, they are happy to be a part of what they call San Diego’s new “coffee frontier.” Visit www.manzanitaroasting.com for more information.
bottom_line: Engaging Colombia cup with impressively juicy, bright acidity and zesty, spice-toned aromatics.

title: Colombia Decaf Granja Paraiso 92
blind_assessment: Jammy, chocolaty. Milk chocolate, blackberry jam, violet, thyme, oak in aroma and cup. Briskly sweet acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Chocolaty, fruity finish into the long.
notes: Produced by Wilton Benitez of Granja Paraiso 92, entirely of the Red Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed anaerobic method, in which in which, after skin and pulp removal, fermentation takes place in a hermetically sealed vessel before the beans are de-pulped and dried. Decaffeinated in Colombia using ethyl acetate, a solvent derived from sugar cane. Kakalove Café is a nano-roaster located in the small city of Chia-Yi in Taiwan that strives to procure and roast the finest quality coffee. Visit www.kakalovecafe.com.tw or email kahiyuho@gmail.com for more information.
bottom_line: We couldn’t tell this was decaf in a blind cupping — it’s chocolaty, syrupy, deep-toned and rich.

title: Colombia Decaf Natural
blind_assessment: Sweet, brightly herb- and fragrantly floral-toned. Goji berry, cacao-nib, narcissus, fresh-cut cedar in aroma and cup. Sweet, delicately savory structure; satiny mouthfeel. Crisp, berryish, cocoa-toned finish.
notes: Produced entirely from trees of the Caturra variety of Arabica and processed by the natural (dried in the whole fruit) method at Finca Clara in a coffee-growing region designated as a UNESCO World Heritage site. Decaffeinated in Colombia by the ethyl acetate (EA) method. Kakalove Café is a nano-roaster located in the small city of Chia-Yi in Taiwan that strives to procure and roast the finest quality coffee. Visit www.kakalovecafe.com.tw or email kahiyuho@gmail.com for more information.
bottom_line: Complex herb-toned flowers and savory-sweet structure drive an intriguing original decaf cup.

title: Colombia Diofanor Ruiz
blind_assessment: Crisply sweet-tart, fruit-toned. Vanilla yogurt, Ibarra chocolate (chocolate with cinnamon), gardenia, amber, date in aroma and cup. Rich, sweetly tart structure with bright, tangy acidity; syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Resonant, flavor-laden, long finish.
notes: Produced by Diofanor Ruiz of Buenavista Farm entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Plat Coffee is a specialty roaster and café in Hong Kong. For more information, visit www.platcoffee.com.
bottom_line: A uniquely composed natural-processed coffee with unusual yogurt-like nuance layered with chocolate, fruit and floral suggestions.

title: Colombia Don Correa Gesha
blind_assessment: Elegantly fruit-forward, delicately juicy. Strawberry guava, malted milk balls, freesia-like flowers, pink peppercorn, marjoram in aroma and cup. Balanced, sweet-tart structure with gently bright acidity; plump, satiny mouthfeel. Crisp, sweet finish centered on suggestions of freesia and pink peppercorn.
notes: Produced by José Giraldo and Jorge Correa of Finca San Juan entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural carbonic maceration method, which involves fermenting whole coffee fruit inside a sealed container that has been flushed with CO2, then drying the coffee, still in the whole fruit. Founded in 1990, Roadmap CoffeeWorks, formerly Lexington Coffee Roasters, is an award-winning artisan roasting company based in Lexington, Virginia. Roadmap CoffeeWorks focuses on producing fresh, distinctive and sustainable coffees. Visit www.roadmapcoffeeworks.com or call 800-322-6505 for more information.
bottom_line: A deep, subtly invigorating carbonic-macerated Colombia Geisha cup with notes of tropical fruit and spicy flowers, complicated by a sweet herbaceousness.

title: Colombia Don Ruiz Anaerobic
blind_assessment: Elegantly fruit-toned, very juicy. Ripe peach, dark chocolate, blueberry jam, almond butter, a hint of wine barrel in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart structure with bright, malic acidity; very smooth, syrupy mouthfeel. Integrated, harmonious, long finish.
notes: Produced by José Giraldo and Jorge Correa and processed by the anaerobic ferment method at “La Clarita” drying station in Quindío. Founded in 1990, Roadmap CoffeeWorks, formerly Lexington Coffee Roasters, is an award-winning artisan roasting company based in Lexington, Virginia. Roadmap CoffeeWorks focuses on producing fresh, distinctive and sustainable coffees. Visit www.roadmapcoffeeworks.com or call 800-322-6505 for more information.
bottom_line: A fruit bomb, but a sophisticated one — balanced, inviting, confidently bright — also delicious cold.

title: Colombia Double Anaerobic Washed Los Nogales Yellow Bourbon
blind_assessment: Fruit-driven, subtly lactic. Grape jelly, pineapple kefir, dark chocolate, amber, salted caramel in aroma and cup. Tangy acidity; creamy-smooth mouthfeel. The lactic-leaning finish gets ballast from dark chocolate notes.
notes: Produced at Finca Los Nogales, entirely of the Yellow Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed anaerobic method, in which the fermentation step occurs in a hermetically sealed vessel before the beans are washed and dried. Kakalove Café is a nano-roaster located in the small city of Chia-Yi in Taiwan that strives to procure and roast the finest quality coffee. Visit www.kakalovecafe.com.tw or email kahiyuho@gmail.com for more information.
bottom_line: A uniquely composed anaerobic washed cup with rich chocolate and salted caramel notes juxtaposed with a sweet-tart lactic tang that is remarkably integrated.

title: Colombia Edison Argote SL 28 Advanced Natural
blind_assessment: Vibrant, fruit-forward. Pink guava, raspberry liqueur and blood orange, supported by cocoa nib and chamomile in both aroma and cup. Acidity is buoyant and juicy; body is crisp and velvety, without heaviness. The finish offers ripe fruit and an enticing sweet herbaceousness.
notes: Produced by Edison Argote of Finca Quebraditas, entirely of the SL28 variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit), with the addition of yeast in a controlled fermentation environment. Second Spin Roasting is an homage to a former local vinyl shop in the owners’ hometown. Visit www.secondspinroasting.com for more information.
bottom_line: A thoughtfully executed, yeast-assisted natural SL28 from Huila with lively fruit, gentle herbs and cocoa depth.

title: Colombia Edwin Enrique Noreña / Black Honey Pink Bourbon Mosto & Passionfruit Co-Ferment
blind_assessment: Tropical, deep, harmonious. Passionfruit, star jasmine, myrrh, cocoa nib, pineapple saltwater taffy in aroma and cup. Bright, juicy acidity; crisp, syrupy mouthfeel. Resonantly fruity and floral finish.
notes: Produced by Edwin Enrique Noreñ of Finca Campo Hermoso, entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by carbonic maceration (which involves fermenting the whole fruit in a sealed container that has been flushed with CO2) and co-fermenting with Pink Bourbon mosto and passionfruit, then dried with most of the fruit flesh remaining on the beans. Little Waves Coffee is a Latina-owned, women-forward company that provides livable wages for its diverse team. Visit www.littlewaves.coffee for more information.
bottom_line: A floral and fruit extravaganza, with passionfruit and star jasmine notes leading the way, complicated by myrrh-like underpinnings.

title: Colombia Edwin Enrique Noreña / Black Honey Watermelon & Lulo Co-Ferment
blind_assessment: Nectar-like, sweetly tart, rich-toned. Watermelon candy, cocoa butter, loquat, freesia, graphite in aroma and cup. High-toned, phosphoric acidity; syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Sweet, long, candy-like finish
notes: Produced by Edwin Enrique Noreñ of Finca Campo Hermoso, entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by carbonic maceration (which involves fermenting the whole fruit in a sealed container that has been flushed with CO2) and co-fermenting with watermelon and lulo, then dried with most of the fruit flesh remaining on the beans. Produced by Edwin Enrique Noreña, Little Waves Coffee is a Latina-owned, women-forward company that provides livable wages for its diverse team. Visit www.littlewaves.coffee for more information.
bottom_line: Candy-sweet in its profile, this co-fermented Colombia Castillo evokes the tropics with a side of spicy florals.

title: Colombia Edwin Enrique Noreña Juice Box Processing Set / Natural Carbonic Maceration
blind_assessment: Floral-toned, very, very sweet. Tea rose, candied apple, agave syrup, dark chocolate, orange marmalade in aroma and cup. Gently brisk acidity; creamy-smooth mouthfeel. Citrusy finish with undertones of tea rose.
notes: Produced by Edwin Enrique Noreña of Finca Campo Hermoso, entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by carbonic maceration (which involves fermenting the whole fruit in a sealed container that has been flushed with CO2), and dried in the whole fruit. Little Waves Coffee is a Latina-owned, women-forward company that provides livable wages for its diverse team. Visit www.littlewaves.coffee for more information.
bottom_line: A richly floral, incredibly sweet carbonic macerated Colombia with tea rose notes at center, supported by orange marmalade.

title: Colombia Edwin Enrique Noreña Pink Bourbon
blind_assessment: Flavor-laden, aromatically exuberant. Passionfruit, elderberry, lemon-thyme, pomelo, cocoa nib in aroma and cup. Juicy-bright acidity; very full, syrupy mouthfeel. Tropical finish with fruit and sweet herb notes front and center.
notes: Produced by Edwin Enrique Noreña of Finca Campo Hermoso, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by carbonic maceration (which involves fermenting the whole fruit in a sealed container that has been flushed with CO2) and co-fermented with mixed berries and passionfruit, and dried with most of the fruit flesh remaining on the beans. Little Waves Coffee is a Latina-owned, women-forward company that provides livable wages for its diverse team. Visit www.littlewaves.coffee for more information.
bottom_line: This balanced, fruit-forward cup, processed by carbonic maceration and co-fermented with berries and passionfruit, does precisely what it is trying to do — it amplifies the inherent elegance of Pink Bourbon with high-acid fruits for a uniquely composed profile.

title: Colombia Edwin Noreña Geisha
blind_assessment: Richly floral, deeply fruit-forward. Cherry cordial, dark chocolate, pink peppercorn, aromatic orchid, marjoram in aroma and cup. Juicy, high-toned acidity; vibrant, silky-smooth mouthfeel. Expressive, juicy, long-lasting finish.
notes: Produced by Edwin Noreña of Finca Campo Hermosa, entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by a proprietary method Noreña calls “carbonic galaxy hops,” in which the whole fruit is fermented with hops and mossto (coffee fruit juice) before being dried. Utopian Coffee is a specialty roaster based in Fort Wayne, Indiana. Visit www.utopiancoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: This exciting Colombia Geisha is equal parts fruity and floral with undertones of rich chocolate and sweet spice notes — especially inviting mouthfeel.

title: Colombia Edwin Noreña Honey (Peach Coferment)
blind_assessment: Lush, stone fruit-driven. Ripe peach, lemon verbena, honeysuckle, cocoa nib and candied orange zest in aroma and cup. Gently bright, rounded acidity; creamy-smooth body. The finish lingers with peach sweetness and pretty cocoa undertones into the long.
notes: Sold as a two-pack at $27.00/8 ounces with another cofermented coffee from the same farm. Produced by Edwin Noreña, entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the honey method (in which some of the fruit flesh is left on during the drying process) with the addition of peach to the partially pulped coffee fruit. Produced by Edwin Noreña, Utopian Coffee is a specialty roaster based in Fort Wayne, Indiana. Visit www.utopiancoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A generously aromatic peach coferment that integrates fruit sweetness with cocoa depth for a harmonious, dessert-like cup with playful balance.

title: Colombia Edwin Noreña Natural (Raspberry Coferment)
blind_assessment: Vibrantly fruit-saturated. Raspberry jam, dark chocolate, hibiscus, blood orange zest and red grape in aroma and cup. Briskly sweet acidity; syrupy-plush body. The finish is long and sweetly tart, carrying raspberry and cocoa depth.
notes: Sold as a two-pack at $27.00/8 ounces with another cofermented coffee from the same farm. Produced by Edwin Noreña, entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit) with the addition of raspberry to the whole coffee fruit. Utopian Coffee is a specialty roaster based in Fort Wayne, Indiana. Visit www.utopiancoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A boldly expressive coferment that foregrounds vivid raspberry notes while retaining enough chocolate structure to keep the profile balanced and compelling.

title: Colombia Efren Echeverry
blind_assessment: Complex, fruit-driven, vibrant. Passionfruit, cocoa butter, rose hips, lavender, blood orange in aroma and cup. Bright, juicy, phosphoric acidity; very syrupy mouthfeel. Richly aromatic, nuanced finish consolidates to notes of cocoa butter and lavender.
notes: Produced by Efren Echeverry of Las Palmas Coffee, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by a variation on the honey method that includes 48 hours of oxidation, followed by a fruit-must inoculation and a 170-hour fermentation. Utopian Coffee is a specialty roaster based in Fort Wayne, Indiana. Visit www.utopiancoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: An exceptionally complex, balanced Colombia Pink Bourbon, experimentally processed to fun tropical, floral effect.

title: Colombia El Bado
blind_assessment: Crisply sweet, complete. Roasted cacao nib, orangy citrus, almond butter, honeysuckle, apricot in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart, juicy acidity; lightly but distinctly syrupy mouthfeel. Cacao and flowers in particular persist in a sweet finish.
notes: El Bado is a Cup of Excellence record holder of sorts with four consecutive top-twenty placements, a tribute to the efforts of farmer Maria Diaz, who took over operations with the help of her son after her husband passed away. Mr. Espresso is a San Francisco Bay Area wholesale roaster and espresso parts distributer that slow-roasts its coffees using traditional wood-fired roasting machines. Visit www.mrespresso.com or call 510-287-5200 for more information.

title: Colombia El Bombo
blind_assessment: Lively, delicate and sweetly floral. Red currant, white peach, cocoa nib, hibiscus and mandarin zest in aroma and cup. Bright, juicy acidity; delicate, silky mouthfeel. The finish is long and refreshing, carrying sweet-tart fruit, florals and cocoa nib into the long.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers of the Cooperativa de Caficultores El Bombo, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Rusty Dog Coffee is a Madison, Wisconsin-based specialty coffee roaster. Visit www.rustydogcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A graceful washed Pink Bourbon that pairs vibrant red fruit and floral lift with exceptional clarity, lively structure and a lingering, elegant finish.

title: Colombia El Castillo Micro-Lot Nelson Melo
blind_assessment: An aromatically rather simple coffee with a tremendous relaxed and almost voluptuous structure. In the aroma low-toned and round with hints of flowers and cherry-toned fruit. Softly acidy and sweetly and deeply rich in the cup. Sweet, almost sugary finish.
notes: A special small lot from farmer Nelson Melo. Alterra is a quality-oriented small-batch wholesale and retail roaster with a small chain of caf? locations in Milwaukee and environs. Visit www.alterracoffee.com or call 414-273-3747 for more information.

title: Colombia El Chaferote Pink Bourbon
blind_assessment: Balanced, brightly sweet. Tangerine, bay leaf, cocoa nib, narcissus, fresh-cut oak in aroma and cup. High-toned acidity; crisp, syrupy mouthfeel. Long, lingering resonant finish.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 20 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 30 Coffees of 2023. Produced by Luis Gerardo Bravo Ordonez of Finca El Chaferote, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Bird Rock Coffee Roasters is a retailer and wholesaler focused on organic and socially responsible coffees; it was named the “2012 Micro Roaster of the Year” by Roast Magazine. Visit www.birdrockcoffee.com or call 858-551-1707 for more information.
bottom_line: A compelling rendition of Pink Bourbon with distinct citrus, cocoa nib, and spicy floral tones — especially lively, juicy acidity.

title: Colombia El Descanso Full Flavor Roast
blind_assessment: Pure, flawless coffee, classic in its simplicity and directness. Tart, cherryish coffee fruit with a crisp, distinct cocoa complication runs through the profile from aroma to finish. Sweetly bright acidity, silky mouthfeel, balanced structure, rich, long, flavor-saturated finish.
notes: Rainforest Alliance certified, meaning this coffee was produced following sustainable ecological and socio-economic criteria developed by the Sustainable Agricultural Network, a coalition of independent, environment-focused non-governmental organizations. Terroir is a microroaster selling only elite single-origin coffees, no blends. It specializes in medium roast styles designed to foreground the character of the green coffee. Terroir is the creation of George Howell, one of the world's leading coffee visionaries. Visit www.terroircoffee.com or call 866-444-5282 for more information.

title: Colombia El Diviso Nestor Lasso Sidra Anaerobic Washed
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Lots of flowers with an herby edge—lavender, jasmine, orange blossom, cilantro—cushion on milk chocolate in this bright, light-footed espresso. Both co-taster John DiRuocco and Ken read this high-toned but resonant espresso in about the same terms with parallel ratings of 94. Resolves to an orangy, floral caramel in three parts milk.
notes: Produced by Nestor Lasso of Finca El Diviso, entirely of the Sidra variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic washed method, in which, after skin and pulp removal, fermentation takes place in a hermetically sealed vessel before the beans are washed and dried. OLI Cafe Roaster is a specialty coffee roaster based in Dali, Taichung, Taiwan. Visit www.facebook.com/OLI.caferoaster for more information.
bottom_line: A fine anthology of herbs and flowers in this buoyant, animated espresso.

title: Colombia El Diviso Sidra Natural
blind_assessment: Very sweet, floral, tropical fruit-toned. Lychee, green grape, pomegranate, baking chocolate, watermelon candy in aroma and cup. Tartly bittersweet in structure, with a delicate, silky mouthfeel. Crisply chocolaty in finish with a continued suggestion of watermelon candy.
notes: Produced by brothers Nestor and Adrian Lasso of Finca El Diviso entirely of the Sidra variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Sidra is an Ethiopian variety of coffee that at some unknown point in its history was selected and brought to Ecuador, then to nearby Colombia. Peach Coffee Roasters is an Atlanta-area specialty roaster. Visit www.peachcoffeeroasters.com for more information.
bottom_line: A pleasantly eccentric cup, with tropical fruit (especially lychee), candyish watermelon, and crisp, dry chocolate jostling for attention.

title: Colombia El Diviso
blind_assessment: Richly floral, sweetly herbaceous. Star jasmine, bay laurel, dark chocolate, frankincense, salted caramel in aroma and cup. Bright, balanced acidity; full, creamy-smooth mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to notes of salted caramel and frankincense.
notes: Produced by Nestor Lasso of Finca El Diviso, entirely of the Sidra variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed thermal shock method in which the coffee fruit undergoes two stages of fermentation: First, the whole cherries are submerged under water for 48 hours, then the beans are pulped and fermented with a strain of Lactobacillus for 24 hours. After fermentation, the beans are given a “thermal shock” using hot and cold rinses to help absorb the fermentation metabolites and halt any further fermentation. Goca Coffee is a roastery and cafe in Taiching, Taiwan. Visit Goca’s Instagram page for more information.
bottom_line: A multi-layered Colombia Sidra processed by the anaerobic thermal shock method — a sensory roller coaster that covers all the sweet, savory and floral bases.

title: Colombia El Espejo
blind_assessment: Sweetly bright, gently fruit-toned. Red apple, caramel, orange zest, almond butter and cocoa powder in aroma and cup. Lively, well-structured acidity; rounded, creamy mouthfeel. The finish consolidates to notes of soft caramel and citrus.
notes: Produced by Reinel Borbon of Finca El Espejo, entirely of the Tabi variety of Arabica, and processed by the honey method, in which some of the fruit flesh is left on the beans during the drying process. Big Shoulders Coffee is a Chicago roaster dedicated to a fresh-roasted, honest approach that lets great coffee speak for itself. Visit www.bigshoulderscoffee.com or call 312-846-1439 for more information.
bottom_line: A balanced honey-processed Colombia Tabi (a hybrid variety of Arabica) that pairs crisp fruit brightness with rich caramel and nut tones in a smooth, satisfying cup.

title: Colombia El Jardin Anaerobic Natural
blind_assessment: Deep-toned, fruit-saturated and richly sweet. Black cherry, red plum, dark chocolate, magnolia and molasses in aroma and cup. Bright, winey acidity; plush, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. The finish is long and resonant, with notes of black cherry, dark chocolate and magnolia.
notes: This coffee earned Finalist recognition in the Experimental category, U.S. division, of the inaugural Kenneth Davids Cup. Produced by the Restrepo Family and processed by the anaerobic natural method, in which the whole fruit is fermented in tanks with limited oxygen before drying, also in the whole fruit. Located in southwestern Colorado, Durango Coffee lays claim to a rich coffee history that dates to 1986. Its motto is “Tough Town, Great Coffee.” Visit durangocoffee.com or call 800-748-2275 for more information.
bottom_line: A richly expressive anaerobic natural Colombia that layers ripe fruit, chocolate and florals with deep sweetness in a full-bodied, beautifully balanced cup.

title: Colombia El Jardin Anaerobic Natural
blind_assessment: Balanced, bright, richly aromatic. Blackberry jam, hazelnut, baking chocolate, lemon verbena, sage in aroma and cup. Gently bright, citrusy acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Blackberry notes take center stage in the finish, with undertones of baking chocolate and lemon verbena.
notes: Produced by the Restrepo Family and processed by the anaerobic natural method, in which the whole fruit is fermented in tanks with limited oxygen before drying, also in the whole fruit. Located in southwestern Colorado, Durango Coffee lays claim to a rich coffee history that dates to 1986. Its motto is “Tough Town, Great Coffee.” Visit durangocoffee.com or call 800-748-2275 for more information.
bottom_line: A wide-ranging, flavor-saturated anaerobic-natural Colombia — delicately bright and nicely balanced.

title: Colombia El Jeromo Washed SOE
