blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Crisply chocolaty, rich-toned. Baking chocolate, caramel, pomegranate, lily, cedar in aroma and small cup. Velvety-smooth mouthfeel. Caramelly, gently tart finish. In cappuccino format, nicely chocolaty with lily and cedar undertones.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers, entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Buon Caffe is a specialty coffee roaster and cafe in Taipei, Taiwan. Visit www.buoncaffe.com.tw for more information.
bottom_line: A solid Colombia SOE that’s chocolaty and rich with sweet caramel and floral notes supported by tart fruit.

title: Colombia El Jordan Washed
blind_assessment: Chocolaty, balanced, bright. Dark chocolate, nectarine, lemon balm, fresh-cut oak, pink peppercorn in aroma and cup. Sparkling acidity; lightly satiny mouthfeel. Chocolate and nectarine center the confident finish.
notes: Produced at Finca El Jordan, from trees of the Colombia, Caturra and Castillo varieties of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Buon Caffe is a specialty coffee roaster and cafe in Taipei, Taiwan. Visit www.buoncaffe.com.tw for more information.
bottom_line: A classically chocolaty washed Colombia complicated by stone fruit and spice-toned herbs.

title: Colombia El Lechal Cup of Excellence
blind_assessment: A whisper of an aroma, but a complex one: flowering grass, caramel, honey, a hint of chocolate. Amazingly sweet and delicately lush in the cup, with the honey notes intensifying and the floral notes declaring as spicy tea rose. The honey and floral notes persist in the surprisingly long, resonant finish.
notes: A prize winner in the 2005 Colombia Second Harvest Cup of Excellence competition, where as a green (unroasted) coffee it placed fifteenth out of hundreds of entries. Produced from trees of the caturra variety of Arabica on the tiny "El Lechal" farm of Omar Antonio Perez Gomez at a growing altitude of approximately 5,900 feet. Terroir is a recently established microroaster selling only elite single-origin coffees, no blends. It specializes in medium roast styles designed to foreground the character of the green coffee. Terroir is the creation of George Howell, one of the world's leading coffee visionaries. Visit www.terroircoffee.com or call 866-444-5282 for more information.

title: Colombia El Mango
blind_assessment: Roundly classic, juicy, balanced. Caramel, hazelnut, lily-like flowers, plum and apricot in aroma and cup. Richly poised acidity; satiny mouthfeel. Flavor consolidates but persists in a sweetly and gently tart finish.
notes: Produced by farmer Heidler Gomez on El Mango, a farm in Buesaco in Nariño Department. Seasons is a micro-roaster of seasonal specialty coffee, selling its fine coffees online only. Visit www.seasonscoffee.us or call 916-905-7160 for more information.

title: Colombia El Mirador Gesha
blind_assessment: Elegant, gently perfumed. Jasmine, lime zest, white peach, cocoa powder, marjoram in aroma and cup. Bright, refreshing acidity; silky mouthfeel. Sweet lingering finish with citrus and floral undertones.
notes: Produced by Caesar Augusto of Finca El Mirador, entirely of the Gesha variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Big Shoulders Coffee is a Chicago roaster dedicated to a fresh-roasted, honest approach that lets great coffee speak for itself. Visit www.bigshoulderscoffee.com or call 312-846-1439 for more information.
bottom_line: A quietly confident washed Colombia Gesha — floral and citrus-driven with graceful structure and clarity.

title: Colombia El Mirador Natural Secret Stash
blind_assessment: Richly sweet, deeply chocolaty, fruit-forward. Chocolate fudge, strawberry, marjoram, Meyer lemon zest, cashew butter in aroma and cup. Bright, balanced acidity; rich, velvety mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to notes of chocolate fudge and marjoram.
notes: Produced by Elkin Guzman of Finca El Mirador, entirely of the Tabi variety of Arabica, and processed by the thermal shock method, in which the coffee fruit, after having been first sanitized with ozone, undergoes two stages of fermentation. First, the whole cherries are submerged under water for 48 hours, then the beans are pulped and fermented, then given a “thermal shock” using hot and cold rinses to help the beans absorb the fermentation metabolites and halt any further fermentation. Afterward, the washed parchment is rapidly dried quickly to avoid over-oxidation or continued fermentation. Old Soul is a roastery, bakery, and crafter of artisanal goods dedicated to quality in every form. Visit www.oldsoulco.com or call 916-443-7685 for more information.
bottom_line: A deeply chocolaty, berry-driven Colombia, processed by the thermal shock method, that delivers layers of fruit, nut and citrus tones.

title: Colombia El Naranjo
blind_assessment: Vividly aromatic, fruit-saturated and deeply sweet. Blackberry, red plum, blood orange, candied violet and chocolate fudge in aroma and cup. Bright, succulent acidity; full, velvety-smooth mouthfeel. The finish is expansive and flavor-laden, with notes of blackberry, candied violet and chocolate fudge.
notes: This coffee earned Finalist recognition in the Experimental category, U.S. division, of the inaugural Kenneth Davids Cup. Produced by Miryan Mercedes de la Cruz of Finca El Naranjo, from trees of the Colombia and Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by the white honey method, in which a small amount of fruit flesh is left on the beans during the drying process.. Telluride Coffee Roasters is a Colorado-based specialty roaster founded by coffee veteran Mick Hill in 1991. For more information, visit telluridecoffeeroasters.net.
bottom_line: An exceptional Nariño natural with concentrated dark fruit and citrus framed by violet-like florals and deep chocolate, combining impressive intensity with the high-toned brightness characteristic of this elevated growing region.

title: Colombia El Oasis
blind_assessment: Lush, quietly complex, fruit-driven. Blackberry, panela, cocoa nib, roasted almond, violet in aroma and cup. Briskly sweet acidity; very smooth, syrupy mouthfeel. The finish centers around cocoa nib and dark berry tones.
notes: Produced by Doña Luz Mila Gonzales of Finca El Oasis, entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the honey method, in which some of the fruit flesh is left on the beans during the drying process. Steel Oak Coffee is a community-driven, small-batch specialty roaster based in Ormond Beach, Florida. Visit www.steeloakcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A harmonious, integrated honey-processed Colombia that balances dark fruit sweetness with floral and nutty undertones.

title: Colombia El Obraje Gesha
blind_assessment: Complex, multi-faceted, spice-toned. Dahlia-like flowers, bergamot, almond, vanilla, roasted cacao nib in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart structure with balanced, bright acidity; delicate, silky-smooth mouthfeel. Bergamot and vanilla-toned cocoa carry the quiet, balanced finish.
notes: This coffee tied for the third-highest rating in a tasting of holiday coffees for Coffee Review‘s December 2018 tasting report. Produced from trees of the rare Ethiopia-derived botanical variety Gesha (also spelled Geisha) by Pablo Guerrero. With its generally elongated beans and distinctive floral and crisp, often chocolaty cup, the Gesha variety continues to distinguish itself as one of the world’s most unique coffees. This is a dry-processed or “natural” version, meaning the beans were dried inside the fruit rather than after the fruit has been removed, as is the case with wet-processed or “washed” coffees. The majority of Gesha coffees are grown in the Boquete region of Panama, but there is increased experimentation with this variety throughout Latin America, especially Colombia, where this exceptional version was grown. Joe Van Gogh is a small-batch roasting company with a focus on certified organic coffees. In addition to its Internet store, it operates six coffeehouses in Durham, Chapel Hill and Greensboro, North Carolina. Visit www.joevangogh.com or call 919-644-0111 for more information.
bottom_line: Layers upon layers of spicy floral and fruit notes resonate in this natural-processed Gesha from Colombia.

title: Colombia El Origen Pink Bourbon Thermal Shock Washed
blind_assessment: Radiant, lyrically complex. Tangerine, gardenia, lychee, white tea, and sugarcane in aroma and cup. Crisp, sparkling acidity; voluptuously silky body. The finish is long, floral, fruit-layered and resonant.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 18 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 50 Coffees of 2025. Produced by David Bedoya of El Origen Coffee Farms, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed thermal shock method, which begins with a standard washed process (fruit skin and pulp removed from the beans), but introduces a rapid temperature shift during the fermentation and rinsing stages. SÖT Coffee Roaster, based in Osaka, Japan, is a self-described Swedish-style roaster with an “aggressively light” roasting style. For more information, visit www.sotcoffee.com.
bottom_line: A standout Pink Bourbon — precise, perfumed and sweetly complex, with exceptional clarity and structure.

title: Colombia El Paraiso Castillo Yeast-Inoculated Decaf
blind_assessment: Aromatically expressive, fruit-driven and richly sweet. Strawberry, lychee, yellow peach, vanilla bean and white chocolate in aroma and cup. Softly juicy acidity; plush, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. The finish is resonant and sweet, with strawberry, lychee and white chocolate notes.
notes: Produced by Diego Bermudez of Finca El Paraiso, entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic washed method, in which the coffee fruit, after having been first sanitized with ozone, undergoes two stages of fermentation. First, the whole cherries are submerged under water for 48 hours; then the beans are pulped and fermented with a strain of Lactobacillus for 24 hours. After fermentation, the beans are given a “thermal shock” using hot and cold rinses to help the beans absorb the fermentation metabolites and halt any further fermentation. Afterward, the washed parchment coffee is rapidly dried with an in-house-designed Eco-Enigma dehumidifying dryer to avoid over-oxidation or continued fermentation. Decaffeinated by the ethyl acetate (EA) method in Colombia. Frequent Coffee is San Diego, California-based coffee roaster specializing in decaffeinated coffees. Visit www.frequentcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: An unusually expressive decaf whose elaborate processing brings vivid fruit and confectionary sweetness to a plush, aromatic cup while retaining impressive balance.

title: Colombia El Paraiso Floral Lychee
blind_assessment: Floral-toned, richly sweet-savory. Black cherry, dark chocolate, marjoram, sandalwood, agave syrup in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart structure with brisk acidity; syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. The finish leads with notes of black cherry, rounding to cocoa tones in the long.
notes: Produced by Diego Bermudez entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic washed method, in which the fermentation step occurs in a hermetically sealed vessel before the beans are washed and dried. Dr.Young Coffee is a Taiwan-based retail specialty coffee roaster with the goal of expressing each coffee’s best flavors. Visit https://lin.ee/HA27cIa for more information.
bottom_line: A fruit-driven anaerobic cup complicated by savory, sweetly herbaceous impulses.

title: Colombia El Paraiso Geisha Anti-Maceration
blind_assessment: Richly sweet-tart, fruit-centered. Bing cherry, hazelnut, candied violet, ginger, sandalwood in aroma and cup. Bright, tartly juicy acidity; very full, syrupy mouthfeel. Complex, multi-layered, very long finish.
notes: Produced by Wilton Benitez of Granja Paraiso 92, entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the thermal shock method, in which the coffee fruit, after having been first sanitized with ozone, undergoes two stages of fermentation. First, the whole cherries are submerged under water for 48 hours, then the beans are pulped and fermented with a strain of Lactobacillus for 24 hours. After fermentation, the beans are given a “thermal shock” using hot and cold rinses to help the beans absorb the fermentation metabolites and halt any further fermentation. Afterward, the washed parchment coffee is rapidly dried with an in-house designed Eco-Enigma dehumidifying dryer to avoid over-oxidation or continued fermentation. SÖT Coffee Roaster, based in Osaka, Japan, is a self-described Swedish-style roaster with an “aggressively light” roasting style. For more information, visit www.sotcoffee.com.
bottom_line: A Colombia Geisha on steroids, processed by a proprietary and meticulous method that concentrates the fruit, spice and floral tones inherent in this coffee.

title: Colombia El Paraiso Geisha Luna Washed
blind_assessment: Richly aromatic, chocolaty and fruit-forward. Dark chocolate, bergamot, lychee, musk, tarragon in aroma and cup. Juicy-bright acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Intense, quite long finish with leading notes of dark chocolate and tarragon.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 25 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 30 Coffees of 2023. Produced by Wilton Benitez of Granja Paraiso 92, entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic thermal shock method, in which the coffee fruit, after having been first sanitized with ozone, undergoes two stages of fermentation. First, the whole cherries are submerged under water for 48 hours, then the beans are pulped and fermented with a strain of Lactobacillus for 24 hours. After fermentation, the beans are given a “thermal shock” using hot and cold rinses to help the beans absorb the fermentation metabolites and halt any further fermentation. Afterward, the washed parchment coffee is rapidly dried with an in-house designed Eco-Enigma dehumidifying dryer to avoid over-oxidation or continued fermentation. SÖT Coffee Roaster, based in Osaka, Japan, is a self-described Swedish-style roaster with an “aggressively light” roasting style. For more information, visit www.sotcoffee.com.
bottom_line: A focused, intensely perfumed, experimentally processed Colombia Geisha that’s, at turns, chocolaty, musky, tropical and sweetly herbaceous.

title: Colombia El Paraiso Lychee Rose Cold Drip
blind_assessment: A ready-to-drink black coffee, tested cold. Deep-toned, rich-tart-savory. Asian pear, pipe tobacco, pink peppercorn, blood orange, cocoa nib. Brightly sweet, delicately tart acidity; round, plump, very smooth mouthfeel. Crisply sweet-savory finish. Milk brings up the richness and savory impulses while also highlighting pipe tobacco notes.
notes: Prepared by the cold-drip method, in which a controlled dripper brews the coffee over 4-6 hours in the refrigerator, at a coffee to water ratio of 1:15. which involves prolonged steeping of ground coffee in cold water. Contains no additives or ingredients other than coffee and water. The green coffee used is a Castillo produced by Wilton Benitez of Finca El Paraiso 92, processed by the anaerobic natural method. GK Coffee is a nano-roastery in Yilan, Taiwan that offers both retail and wholesale coffee. For more information, visit www.gkcoffee.com.tw or email gkcoffee2015@gmail.com.
bottom_line: An evocative, nuanced, downright elegant slow-drip RTD made with an anaerobically processed Wilton Benitez Castillo — a beauty.

title: Colombia El Paraiso Lychee Rose
blind_assessment: Richly floral-toned, deeply fruity. Passionfruit, tea rose, frangipane, cocoa nib, pineapple kefir in aroma and cup. Juicy-bright, balanced acidity; delicate, silky-smooth mouthfeel. Tea rose and cocoa nib carry the crisp finish.
notes: Produced by Wilton Benitez entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic thermal shock method, in which the coffee fruit is first sterilized and then fermented in a bio-reactor. After this whole-fruit fermentation, skin and pulp are removed and the coffee is subjected to a second anaerobic fermentation. A bean-sealing process follows, carried out through successive impacts of hot and cold water, before the beans are dried by machine for 46 hours. GK Coffee is a nano-roastery in Yilan, Taiwan, that offers both retail and wholesale coffee. For more information, visit www.gkcoffee.com.tw or email gkcoffee2015@gmail.com.
bottom_line: A lush, flavor-saturated anaerobic Colombia with leading notes of tropical fruit and dusky rose; exceptionally bright, balanced acidity.

title: Colombia El Pijao Divisa CM Java
blind_assessment: Tropical-toned, lavishly floral. Passionfruit, orange blossom, maple syrup, turmeric, roasted almond in aroma and cup. Sweet-tart structure with juicy, tropical acidity; plush, creamy mouthfeel. The finish highlights passionfruit and roasted almond, deepening to turmeric and orange blossom in the long.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 33 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 50 Coffees of 2025. Produced by Diofanor Ruiz, entirely of the Java variety of Arabica, and processed by the carbonic maceration method, which involves fermenting the whole fruit in a sealed container that has been flushed with CO2, then drying in the whole fruit. Corvus Coffee Roasters is based in Denver, Colorado and specializes in rare and exclusive coffees from some of the finest growers in the world. Corvus particularly focuses on processing methods and selective harvesting, which result in small, seasonal micro-lots of uniquely sweet, vibrant, and clean flavor profiles. For more information, visit www.corvuscoffee.com.
bottom_line: A tropical-fruit-forward Colombia, this carbonic maceration Java offers layers of floral sweetness and nutty depth, complicated by a turmeric-like sweet earthiness — uniquely composed, enigmatic, very compelling.

title: Colombia El Premio de Timana
blind_assessment: Muted, crisply chocolaty. Baking chocolate, graphite, cashew, lily, brown sugar in aroma and cup. Sharp acidity; light-bodied mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to notes of graphite and brown sugar.
notes: Purchased at an Oakland, California Whole Foods Market. Certifications: Fair Trade USA; Non-GMO. Processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Allegro Coffee, a subsidiary of Whole Foods Market, offers one of the country’s largest selections of single-origin coffees. Visit www.allegrocoffee.com or call 800-227-1107 for more information.
bottom_line: A sweet but thin washed Colombia cup with muted notes of baking chocolate and cashew with savory undertones.

title: Colombia El Puente
blind_assessment: Crisply chocolaty, berry-toned. Black raspberry, baking chocolate, jasmine, cedar, orange zest in aroma and cup. Bright, balanced acidity; crisp, lightly satiny mouthfeel. Chocolaty finish with undertones of orange zest and cedar.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers, from trees of the Caturra, Colombia and Castillo varieties of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit) at El Puente processing facility. Drink Coffee Do Stuff operates a roastery in Truckee, California, and a coffee shop in nearby Incline Village, Nevada. Visit www.drinkcoffeedostuff.com for more information.
bottom_line: A solid natural-processed Colombia with leading notes of chocolate and berries, complicated by spice-toned florals and citrus.

title: Colombia El Roble Chiroso Washed
blind_assessment: Delicate, sweetly herb- and flower-toned. Lemon verbena, violet, ginger blossom, baking chocolate, a crisp background hint of cedar in aroma and cup. Lightly juicy in structure, silky in mouthfeel. Baking chocolate comes forward in a comfortable finish.
notes: Produced by Jairo Ivan Lopez entirely of the Chiroso variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Chiroso is an Ethiopian variety of Arabica that at some point in its history was brought to the Urrao region of Antioquia, Colombia, where it was initially cultivated by farmer Jose Arcadio Caro. GK Coffee is a nano-roastery in Yilan, Taiwan, that offers both retail and wholesale coffee. For more information, visit www.gkcoffee.com.tw or email gkcoffee2015@gmail.com.
bottom_line: Delicate aromatic intrigue in a subtle, gardeny cup.

title: Colombia El Roble Natural Carbonic Java
blind_assessment: Round, deeply fruit- and cocoa-toned. Blackberry jam, dark chocolate, praline, peach, a hint of myrrh. Deep, ringing sweetness in the structure without a hint of sugary overstatement. Smooth, mouth filling in the body; jammy cocoa-toned finish.
notes: Produced by Jairo Ivan Lopez entirely of the Ethiopia-derived Java variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural carbonic method, which involves two fermentation phases in closed tanks injected with CO2. The first fermentation includes the whole coffee fruit, after which the skins and pulp are removed and the beans are fermented a second time with their skins and juice in the tank, after which they are washed and dried. Corvus particularly focuses on processing methods and selective harvesting, which results in small, seasonal micro-lots of uniquely sweet, vibrant and clean flavor profiles. For more information, visit www.corvuscoffee.com.
bottom_line: A naturally and deeply sweet cup with gentle, rather Geisha-like floral and chocolaty complication.

title: Colombia El Roble Single Origin Espresso
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Crisp, sweetly gentle, suave. Honey, orange, grapefruity citrus, fresh-cut fir in the aroma. Light, silky mouthfeel. Turns chocolaty and more distinctly citrusy in the light-bodied, silky cup. Superb flavor-saturated, sweetly clean  finish. In two parts milk the chocolate is nuanced by ripe citrus and a deeper, apricot-toned fruit.
notes: This coffee is certified organically grown and Rainforest Alliance Certified, meaning it was produced following sustainable ecological and socio-economic criteria developed by the Sustainable Agricultural Network, a coalition of independent, environment-focused non-governmental organizations. El Roble is a 740-acre farm situated on a small plateau called Mesa de los Santos located in the northern Colombian department of Santander, close to the border with Venezuela. Terroir is a microroaster focusing on elite single-origin coffees. It was a pioneer in the revival of medium roast styles designed to foreground the character of the green coffee. Terroir is the creation of George Howell, one of the world's leading coffee visionaries. Visit www.terroircoffee.com or call 866-444-5282 for more information.

title: Colombia El Sauce
blind_assessment: Richly sweet, floral-toned. Narcissus, roasted cacao nib, agave syrup, fir, red apple in aroma and cup. Sweet-toned structure with gentle, rounded acidity; smooth, satiny mouthfeel. The gently drying finish centers around roasted cacao nib and narcissus-like floral notes.
notes: Produced entirely from trees of the Castillo variety of Arabica. Processed by the wet or “washed” method, in which skin and fruit flesh are removed from the beans or seeds before they are dried. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: A crisply sweet Colombia cup driven by engaging floral notes and hints of red apple and fresh-cut fir.

title: Colombia El Silencio Castillo Natural
blind_assessment: Crisply sweet-tart. Dried plum, baking chocolate, lemon zest, thyme, cane sugar in aroma and cup. Brisk, sweet acidity; full, syrupy mouthfeel. Gently crisp finish with notes of baking chocolate and lemon zest.
notes: Produced by Robinson Rivera of Finca El Silencio, entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). SÖT Coffee Roaster, based in Osaka, Japan, is a self-described Swedish-style roaster with an “aggressively light” roasting style. For more information, visit www.sotcoffee.com.
bottom_line: A quietly confident Colombia natural with an especially full, syrupy body and notes of dried stone fruit throughout.

title: Colombia El Vergel #1
blind_assessment: Bright, juicy-tart, chocolaty. Dark chocolate, pie cherry, hazelnut, tangerine, cedar in aroma and cup. Bright, citrusy acidity; creamy-smooth mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to notes of pie cherry and dark chocolate.
notes: Produced by Marta Bayter and her sons, Shady and Elias, of Vergel Estate, from trees of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Speedwell Coffee, based in Plymouth, Massachusetts, is a wholesale and retail specialty roaster particularly dedicated to offering attractive coffee subscription plans. For more information, visit www.speedwellcoffee.com.
bottom_line: A tart-leaning washed Colombia Caturra that gets ballast from rich chocolate notes throughout the profile, and sweet-spicy citrus zest notes complicate and invite.

title: Colombia El Vergel #1
blind_assessment: Balanced, juicy, deep-toned. Dark chocolate, wisteria, apricot, hazelnut, coconut in aroma and cup. High-toned, sparkling acidity; very full, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Long, harmonious, integrated finish that carries over the promise of the cup.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 13 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 30 Coffees of 2024. Produced by Marta Bayter and her sons, Shady and Elias, of Vergel Estate, from trees of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Speedwell Coffee, based in Plymouth, Massachusetts, is a wholesale and retail specialty roaster particularly dedicated to offering attractive coffee subscription plans. For more information, visit www.speedwellcoffee.com.
bottom_line: A flavor-saturated, chocolaty, sweetly nut- and floral-toned washed Colombia with especially vibrant acidity — balanced, bright, and an exceptional value.

title: Colombia El Vergel Guava Banana
blind_assessment: Tropical fruit-toned. Mango, lychee, lime, dark chocolate, oak in aroma and cup. Very sweet structure with brisk acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Fruity and chocolaty finish with aromatic wood notes.
notes: Produced by Marta Bayter and her sons, Shady and Elias, of Vergel Estate from the Red and Yellow Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method (whole fruit is fermented with limited oxygen before drying, still in the whole fruit). Oak & Bond is a specialty retail and wholesale coffee roaster based in Charlotte, North Carolina. The company’s name combines “oak,” a reference to its first coffee, a barrel-aged release, and “bond,” referring to the founders’ happy marriage. For more information, visit www.oakandbondcoffee.com.
bottom_line: An exceptionally fruit-forward cup (think tropical melange) with undertones of dark chocolate throughout.

title: Colombia El Vergel Magnum Sidra
blind_assessment: Richly sweet-savory, nuanced and aromatic. Candy apple, almond nougat, hop flowers, frankincense, baking chocolate in aroma and cup. Even-keeled acidity; mouth-filling, viscous body. Richly bittersweet finish with notes of candy apple and hops.
notes: Produced by Marta Bayter and her sons, Shady and Elias, of Vergel Estate, from trees of the Sidra variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method, with the addition of mossto (fresh-pressed coffee fruit juice) to the fermentation. Hifalutin Coffee Roasters is a Charleston, South Carolina-based specialty coffee roaster with two cafes in town. Visit www.highfalutin.com for more information.
bottom_line: A uniquely composed, experimentally processed Sidra with the addition of coffee fruit juice (AKA mossto) to the anaerobic fermentation, which gives the coffee a candylike, rich-toned profile.

title: Colombia El Vergel Martha Montenegro Rubi Marti Anaerobic
blind_assessment: Complex, rich-toned. Watermelon candy, dried guava, pineapple taffy, cinnamon, toffee in aroma and cup. Brightly sweet, sparkling acidity; full, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Harmonious, very long, deep-toned finish.
notes: Produced by Martha Montenegro and her team of women pickers at El Vergel Estate, entirely of the Red Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method (fermented in an oxygen-free environment for 60 hours), then dried in the whole fruit. Torque Coffee has an unusual business model that promises 20 percent of the retail value of each coffee to its producer. Visit www.torquecoffees.com for more information.
bottom_line: An elegant, confident, multilayered anaerobic Colombia that leads with tropical fruit and baking spice notes — exceptionally sweet.

title: Colombia Elkin Diosa
blind_assessment: Exuberant and multilayered. Red currant, wildflower honey, star jasmine, cocoa nib, blood orange in aroma and cup. Balanced, juicy acidity; supple, syrupy mouthfeel. Long, clean, complex and lingering finish.
notes: Produced by Elkin Diosa of Fina La Yelena, entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by the honey method, in which some of the fruit flesh is left on the beans during the drying process. Utopian Coffee is a specialty roaster based in Fort Wayne, Indiana. Visit www.utopiancoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: The meticulous honey process elevates both mouthfeel and sweetness while preserving deep fruit complexity — both disciplined and indulgent.

title: Colombia Estrella del Sur
blind_assessment: Distinctly cocoa- and nut-toned aroma. In the cup softly acidy, medium-bodied, and very sweet with continued cocoa and nut notes. In the finish the cocoa deepens toward chocolate, softening a slight astringency.
notes: Batdorf & Bronson is a leading wholesale quality-oriented specialty roaster founded in 1986. Visit www.batdorfcoffee.com or call 800-955-5282 for more information.

title: Colombia Exótico De Altura
blind_assessment: Rich-toned, chocolaty, balanced. Dark chocolate, hazelnut butter, blackberry, yuzu, fresh-cut oak in aroma and cup. Deeply sweet structure with gentle, round acidity; plush, satiny-smooth mouthfeel. Particularly rich, complex finish, chocolaty and long.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers organized around Grupo Giraldo Exótico de Altura, a producer association with 81 members who live in the communities of Sierra, Sierrita y Cuajarón, from trees of the Colombia, Caturra and Castillo varieties of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and flesh are removed from the beans before they are dried). Oak & Bond is a specialty retail and wholesale coffee roaster based in Charlotte, North Carolina. The company’s name combines “oak,” a reference to its first coffee, a barrel-aged release, and “bond,” referring to the founders’ happy marriage. For more information, visit www.oakandbondcoffee.com.
bottom_line: A multi-layered washed Colombia cup with leading notes of dark chocolate and blackberry — intensely aromatic, balanced, deep.

title: Colombia Fair Trade Select (K-Cup)
blind_assessment: (As brewed in a Keurig B70 Platinum single-serve brewing device using a "K-Cup" capsule to produce 6-ounce serving): Sweet-toned, soft, balanced, with a grapy, Riesling-like fruit and hints of dark chocolate and flowers. Muted aroma and short (if rich) finish. Best in the cup: bright, delicate acidity, lightly syrupy mouthfeel and gently complex flavor.
notes: This coffee is Fair Trade certified, meaning this coffee was purchased from small-holding farmers at a “fair” or economically sustainable price. Reviewed in K-cup format for Keurig single-serve brewers. Keurig brewing devices were among the first single-serve brewers on the market, starting in the mid 1990's with office models and now offered in several home models with a variety of features and price points. Green Mountain Coffee Roasters is one of the country’s leading specialty roasters, offering a particularly wide-ranging variety of origins and roast styles. Visit www.greenmountaincoffee.com or call 800-223-6768 for more information.

title: Colombia Faver Emir Ninco Pink Bourbon
blind_assessment: Gently sweet-tart, cocoa-toned. Tamarind, cocoa nib, pomegranate, narcissus, lemon verbena in aroma and cup. Bright, juicy acidity; crisp, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Tamarind and cocoa nib lead in the quiet finish.
notes: Produced by Emir Ninco of Finca Costa Rica, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method, in which the whole fruit is fermented in tanks with limited oxygen before drying, also in the whole fruit. Buon Caffe is a specialty coffee roaster and cafe in Taipei, Taiwan. Visit www.buoncaffe.com.tw for more information.
bottom_line: An inviting Colombia anaerobic natural with notes of tart fruit, sweet citrus and crisp cocoa throughout the profile.

title: Colombia Finca Al Paraiso Y–05 Lychee
blind_assessment: Richly sweet-tart, fruit-driven. Rambutan, candied violet, ginger blossom, bittersweet chocolate syrup, sandalwood in aroma and cup. Bright, juicy-tart acidity; very full, creamy-smooth mouthfeel. Complex, multi-layered, exceptionally long finish.
notes: Produced by Wilton Benitez of Granja Paraiso 92, entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by the thermal shock method, in which the coffee fruit, after having been first sanitized with ozone, undergoes two stages of fermentation. First, the whole cherries are submerged under water for 48 hours, then the beans are pulped and fermented with a strain of Lactobacillus for 24 hours. After fermentation, the beans are given a “thermal shock” using hot and cold rinses to help the beans absorb the fermentation metabolites and halt any further fermentation. Afterward, the washed parchment coffee is rapidly dried with an in-house designed Eco-Enigma dehumidifying dryer to avoid over-oxidation or continued fermentation. Regent strives to deliver coffee with care and purpose. Visit regentcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A proprietary “thermal shock” processing method elevates this Colombia Castillo to a multisensory, dang-near poetic experience.

title: Colombia Finca Buenavista
blind_assessment: Deep, rich, chocolaty. The chocolate is nut-toned and fudge-like and complicated by raspberry-like fruit, night flowers and a hint of pungent cedar. Gentle, juicy acidity; lightly syrupy mouthfeel. Flavor fades slightly in the finish, but remains sweet and chocolate-toned with perhaps a deepening hint of savory.
notes: Farmer Carlos Imbachi’s Finca Buenavista won first place in the Specialty Coffee Association of America’s Coffee of the Year competition in both 2009 and 2010. CaféTaster is an aficionado nano-roaster of the style increasingly characteristic of East Asia countries like Taiwan and Korea, roasting very high-end coffees in very small volumes for a tiny clientele of passionate coffee enthusiasts, in the process selling coffee education as much as coffee itself. For more information, visit www.facebook.com/cafetaster or email roaster Jerry Huang at cafetaster.order@gmail.com.

title: Colombia Finca Campo Hermosa
blind_assessment: Lychee, rose hips, oolong tea, cocoa nib, magnolia in aroma and cup. Juicy-bright acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Floral-toned, oolong-like finish.
notes: Produced by Edwin Noreña of Finca Campo Hermosa, entirely of the Sidra variety of Arabica, and processed by the black honey method, in which much of the fruit flesh is left on the beans during the drying process. Bonlife Coffee Roasters is a woman-owned specialty roaster in Cleveland, Tennessee. Visit www.bonlifecoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: This Colombia Sidra black honey is sweet, tart, rich and elegant in equal measure and gets depth from notes of oolong tea and vibrancy from tropical fruit impulses.

title: Colombia Finca Campoalegre
blind_assessment: Brightly sweet-savory, richly layered. Narcissus, roasted cacao nib, dried apricot, sandalwood, maple syrup in aroma and cup. Juicy, lively acidity; deeply sweet structure with savory undertones. Plush, syrupy mouthfeel. The long, resonant finish consolidates to attractive floral and cocoa tones.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 28 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 30 Coffees of 2017. Produced by Ivan Quinayas at Finca Campoalegre from trees of the Caturra and Colombia varieties of Arabica. This is a wet-processed or “washed” coffee, meaning the fruit skin and pulp were removed from the beans immediately after harvesting and before drying. Located in southwestern Colorado, Durango Coffee lays claim to a rich coffee history that dates to 1986. Its motto is “Tough Town, Great Coffee.” Visit www.durangocoffee.com or call 800-748-2275 for more information.
bottom_line: A nuanced, complex Colombia cup that leads with lush floral notes and stone fruit grounded by suggestions of rich cocoa.

title: Colombia Finca Cerro Azul
blind_assessment: Intense, complex, inimitably distinctive aromatics and flavor: crisp cocoa, cherryish fruit, brandy, spicy tea rose, fresh pipe tobacco. Rich, fruit-toned acidity; syrupy mouthfeel; long finish with an exquisite balance of dry cocoa and sweet fruit notes.
notes: Cerro Azul is a coffee farm owned by brothers Rigoberto and Luis Eduardo Herrera. From trees of the now celebrated "Gesha" or "Geisha" variety of Arabica. With its distinctive floral and dry chocolate cup, the Gesha variety continues to distinguish itself as one of the world's most unique coffees. Based in the San Diego area, Bird Rock Coffee Roasters is a retailer and wholesaler that focuses on organic and socially responsible coffees. Visit www.birdrockcoffee.com or call 858-551-1707 for more information.

title: Colombia Finca Chambaku Pink Bourbon NIU Culturing Fermentation
blind_assessment: Sweetly aromatic and fruit-centered. Notes of strawberry compote, rose, honeydew melon, cocoa powder and lemongrass in aroma and cup. Rounded acidity; silky, buoyant mouthfeel. The finish is clean and gently floral with lingering strawberry and cocoa.
notes: Produced by the Restrepo family of Finca Chambaku, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by a proprietary method involving culturing fermentation, which combines fruit and selected yeast cultures to trigger complex metabolic reactions during fermentation. SÖT Coffee Roaster, based in Osaka, Japan, is a self-described Swedish-style roaster with an “aggressively light” roasting style. For more information, visit www.sotcoffee.com.
bottom_line: An engaging, modern Pink Bourbon — floral and fruit-sweet with a smooth mouthfeel and subtle fermentation complexity.

title: Colombia Finca Chambaku
blind_assessment: Tropical, deeply sweet-tart. Passionfruit, lemon verbena, cane sugar, bay leaf, cedar in aroma and cup. Crisply high-toned acidity; very full, satiny mouthfeel. Lemon verbena and bay leaf remain in the pleasing finish.
notes: Produced by Elmer and Juan Restrepo of Finca Chambaku, and processed by a proprietary natural yeast method called Lactic K, which involves whole-cherry fermentation with an added culture of lactic acid bacteria and water kefir. Established in 2010, Red Rooster is an organic-certified micro-roaster focusing on socially conscious, high-quality coffee. Visit redroostercoffee.com or call 540-745-7338 for more information.
bottom_line: A nuanced, multi-layered, experimentally processed Colombia that surfaces tropical fruit notes and sweet herbs with a throughline of decadent cane sugar.

title: Colombia Finca El Caucho Pink Bourbon
blind_assessment: Very sweet, floral-toned. Freesia, pink grapefruit zest, wild honey, guava, oak in aroma and cup. Balanced, richly sweet structure with high-toned acidity; viscous, satiny mouthfeel. The flavor-saturated finish centers around notes of freesia and pink grapefruit zest.
notes: This coffee tied for the second-highest rating in a cupping of single-farm coffees from Colombia for Coffee Review’s February 2021 report. Produced by Roberto Achicue of Finca El Caucho entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and flesh are removed before drying). Paradise Roasters specializes in micro-lot Arabica and Robusta coffees from Asia and other emerging origins. The company prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.
bottom_line: A sweetly evocative presentation of Colombia Pink Bourbon, a rare and possibly misnamed variety particularly associated with the Huila region of Colombia. Classically wet-processed and driven by spicy floral, sweet citrus and tropical fruit notes.

title: Colombia Finca El Diviso Java
blind_assessment: Lush, richly floral-toned. Lilac, almond paste, passionfruit, pink grapefruit zest, thyme in aroma and cup. High-toned, complex acidity; very syrupy mouthfeel. Floral-toned finish with pink grapefruit zest and passionfruit undertones.
notes: Produced by Nestor Lasso of Finca El Diviso, entirely of the Java variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic washed method, in which, after skin and pulp removal, fermentation takes place in a hermetically sealed vessel before the beans are washed and dried. Imported by Genuine Origin. Elevator Coffee is a Portland, Oregon-based specialty coffee roaster. Visit www.elevatorcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A strikingly aromatic Java that marries lifted florals and tropical fruit with syrupy depth, showing how controlled anaerobic washing can deliver both intensity and composure in a truly top-tier Colombia cup.

title: Colombia Finca El Faldon
blind_assessment: Bright, floral, and fruit-driven. Notes of hibiscus, mandarin orange, red currant, honey, and almond in aroma and cup. Juicy, lively acidity; lightly satiny mouthfeel. Sweet-tart finish emphasizes citrus and berry notes.
notes: Produced by Luis Felipe Leguizamo Giraldo of Finca El Faldon, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method ( fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Utopian Coffee is a specialty roaster based in Fort Wayne, Indiana. Visit www.utopiancoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A high-toned Pink Bourbon from Huila: lively, juicy, and complex, balancing bright florals with sweet fruit and honey notes.

title: Colombia Finca El Mirador
blind_assessment: Vibrant, gracefully layered. Red apple, cashew butter, pear nectar, jasmine, sandalwood in aroma and cup. Crisp, sweet-tart acidity; light yet creamy mouthfeel. Long, lingering, and gently floral finish that reflects the cup’s bright, rounded character.
notes: Produced at Finca La Playita, entirely of the Red Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the honey method, in which some of the fruit flesh is left on the beans during the drying process. Based in Phoenix, Arizona, Press Coffee roasts in small batches to ensure the highest quality and consistency, while sharing their knowledge and passion for coffee with customers. Visit www.presscoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: This elegantly fruit-driven, subtly floral honey-process selection is framed by a throughline of jasmine, offering a clear, confident, inviting profile.

title: Colombia Finca El Paraiso Castillo Red Plum
blind_assessment: Richly floral, resonantly fruit-toned. Apricot blossom, Bing cherry, amber, cocoa nib, black sage in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart structure with gently bright, floral-driven acidity; buoyant, silky mouthfeel. The finish centers around notes of Bing cherry, apricot blossom and amber.
notes: Produced by Diego Bermudez entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic washed method, in which the fermentation step occurs in a hermetically sealed vessel before the beans are washed and dried. Paradise prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information
bottom_line: A uniquely composed, double-anaerobic washed Colombia cup that’s flavor-saturated and harmoniously sweet-tart-savory — unusual and inviting.

title: Colombia Finca El Paraiso Double Anaerobic Geisha
blind_assessment: Bright, intensely pungent, oddly engaging. Spearmint, blueberry, fresh yogurt, sweet cocoa, musk in aroma and cup. Tart and bittersweet in structure; in mouthfeel, syrupy and plush. The finish consolidates richly around suggestions of sweet cocoa and fresh yogurt, with a very slight suggestion of earthy decay.
notes: This coffee tied for third-highest rating in a cupping of coffees produced using reduced oxygen (“Anaerobic”) processing methods for Coffee Review’s November 2019 tasting report. Anaerobic processing in this case means this coffee went through “double” or two-stage fermentation in a sealed oxygen-evacuated tank, first in the whole fruit for two days, then after removal of skin and fruit pulp, for two more days. Produced from the celebrated Geisha (also spelled Gesha) variety of Arabica. Lucky Café is a roaster located in the northern Taiwan city of Zhongli committed to developing the best possibilities of the finest coffees available. Visit https://www.facebook.com/lucky.cafe.studio/ or email fr083276@gmail.com for more information.
bottom_line: The startling aromatic surprises of the Geisha variety are overlaid and intensified by the less familiar surprises of an experimental lactic-acid-inducing fermentation step. For those who pursue the rare and remarkable in beverages.

title: Colombia Finca El Paraiso Geisha Letty
blind_assessment: Ultra-high-toned, fruit-driven, richly floral. Wisteria, dried nectarine, pistachio brittle, calamansi lime, tarragon in aroma and cup. Deeply sweet structure with resoundingly bright, lively acidity; delicately silky, viscous mouthfeel. Long, floral-toned finish supported by bittersweet citrus.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 4 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 30 Coffees of 2022. Produced by Diego Bermudez of Finca El Paraiso entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic washed method, in which the fermentation occurs in a hermetically sealed vessel. Paradise Roasters specializes in micro-lot Arabica and Robusta coffees from Asia and other emerging origins. Paradise prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.
bottom_line: This double-anaerobic Colombia Geisha has a remarkable and surprising cup profile that is, at turns, fruity and floral, tart yet singingly sweet.

title: Colombia Finca El Paraíso Geisha Sake
blind_assessment: Exuberantly aromatic, rich, very complex. Bergamot, Concord grape, ginger blossom, pistachio, lychee in aroma and cup. Juicy-bright, exceptionally high-toned acidity; lush, silky mouthfeel. Rich, pungent, crisply sweet finish.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 10 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 30 Coffees of 2023. Produced by Diego Bermudez, from trees of the original Panama T.2722 cultivar of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic washed method, in which the coffee fruit, after having been first sanitized with ozone, undergoes two stages of fermentation. First, the whole cherries are submerged under water for 48 hours, then the beans are pulped and fermented with a strain of Lactobacillus for 24 hours. After fermentation, the beans are given a “thermal shock” using hot and cold rinses to help the beans absorb the fermentation metabolites and halt any further fermentation. Afterward, the washed parchment coffee is rapidly dried with an in-house designed Eco-Enigma dehumidifying dryer to avoid over oxidation or continued fermentation. Paradise prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.
bottom_line: A decadent, expressive, voluptuous double-anaerobic Colombia Geisha with a wide range of aromas and flavors, from spice-toned bergamot to super-sweet lychee.

title: Colombia Finca El Paraiso Rose Tea
blind_assessment: Subtly intense anaerobic flower bomb. Sweetly tangy, very brightly floral. Rose, yogurt, blood orange, peach, cashew butter in aroma and cup. Juicy and sweet-tart in structure; full, syrupy mouthfeel. Flowers lead in a balanced finish.
notes: Produced by Diego Samuel Bermudez Tapia of El Paraiso Farm from trees of the Castillo, Colombia and Caturra varieties of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic method: Whole fruit is fermented in hermetically sealed tanks for 24 hours before the skins are removed. The fruit flesh or mucilage is left on the bean for another 36-hour sealed-tank fermentation. Finally, the coffee is dried on raised beds with the mucilage still on the bean, as in the honey method. GK Coffee is a nano-roastery in Yilan, Taiwan that offers both retail and wholesale coffee. For more information, visit www.gkcoffee.com.tw or email gkcoffee2015@gmail.com.
bottom_line: An original yet balanced anaerobic profile: Bright rose-like flowers are enveloped in a plushly juicy, peach-yogurt-like matrix.

title: Colombia Finca El Paraiso
blind_assessment: Chocolaty, deeply sweet-savory. Dark chocolate, fresh ginger, plum blossom, lemon verbena, Italian parsley in aroma and cup. Savory-leaning structure with sweet undertones and crisp, citrusy acidity; lively, tannic mouthfeel. Gently drying, chocolaty and spice-toned finish.
notes: Produced by Diego Samuel Bermudez Tapia of the Castillo, Caturra and Colombia varieties of Arabica and processed by the double anaerobic method (subject to oxygen-restricted fermentation first in the whole fruit, then, after skins are removed, in the fruit flesh). Dory Coffee Roasters is a Taipei-based nano-roaster of specialty coffee. For more information, visit https://www.facebook.com/dorycoffee99/.
bottom_line: Processed by an experimental anaerobic fermentation method that nets a savory, sweetly spicy and gingery, intriguingly unconventional cup.

title: Colombia Finca El Roblar
blind_assessment: Exceptionally high-toned, sweetly tart, chocolaty. Juicy peach, dark chocolate, caramel, pink peppercorn, fresh-cut cedar in aroma and cup. Sweet-tart structure with sparkling acidity; full, creamy mouthfeel. In the spice-toned finish sweet pink-peppercorn notes transform to something resembling Szechuan peppers, supported by dark chocolate and peach.
notes: This coffee tied for the second-highest rating in a cupping of coffees roasted by Black-owned coffee companies for Coffee Review’s August 2020 report. Produced by German Peña of Finca Roblar from trees of the Caturra, Castillo and Colombia varieties of Arabica and processed by the washed method. BeanFruit Coffee Co. is an award-winning coffee roasting company located in the Jackson, Mississippi metro area that provides fresh-roasted coffee with a focus on single origins. Visit www.beanfruit.com or call 601-624-2605 for more information.
bottom_line: A nuanced, voluptuous Colombia cup with distinct notes of stone fruit, dark chocolate, and complex peppercorn tones: balanced, bright, juicy, deep.

title: Colombia Finca El Roble Chiroso
blind_assessment: Sweetly nut-toned. Pistachio, red apple, lemon verbena, oak, agave syrup in aroma and cup. Sweet structure with gently brisk acidity; crisp, satiny mouthfeel. The nut-toned finish has undertones of lemon verbena and oak.
notes: Produced by Jairo Ivan Lopez, entirely of the Chiroso variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Chiroso is an Ethiopian variety of Arabica that at some point in its history was brought to the Urrao region of Antioquia, Colombia, where it was initially cultivated by farmer Jose Arcadio Caro. VERYTIME is a specialty nano-roaster based in Taoyuan, Taiwan. Visit www.verytime.com.tw/ for more information.
bottom_line: A friendly, balanced Colombia Chiroso with sweet nut tones and a crisp, citrusy herbaceousness.

title: Colombia Finca El Ventilador Pink Bourbon Anaerobic Natural
blind_assessment: Sweet, deep, balanced. Caramel, clover flowers, cedar, baking chocolate, a hint of passionfruit with a gently sweet yogurty tang. Tartly sweet but deeply savory in structure. Lightly syrupy mouthfeel. Dry and richly layered in the finish; passionfruit and hint of chocolate.
notes: Produced by Yesid Galindo of Finca El Ventilador entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method, in which the whole fruit is fermented in an oxygen-free environment before drying, still in the whole fruit. Magnolia Coffee is a Charlotte, North Carolina-based specialty roaster whose mission is to use sustainably sourced coffees to make a difference in the lives of coffee workers and to foster a socially conscious community with cause-supporting coffees. Visit www.magnoliacoffeeco.com for more information.
bottom_line: Anaerobic processing overlays a balanced cup with a pleasing, flavor-complicating yogurty tang.

title: Colombia Finca El Vergal Geisha/Java Natural
blind_assessment: Fruit-forward, delicately spice-toned. Pink grapefruit zest, apricot, freesia-like flowers, fresh-cut oak, almond butter in aroma and cup. Sweet-tart structure with brisk acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. The resonant finish consolidates to notes of pink grapefruit zest and almond butter.
notes: Produced by Robinson Rozo from a blend of the Geisha and Java varieties of Arabica, both processed by the natural method (beans are dried in the whole fruit). Paradise Roasters specializes in micro-lot Arabica and Robusta coffees from Asia and other emerging origins. The company prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.
bottom_line: An unusual blend of two varieties of Arabica, both natural-processed and both derived from Ethiopian landraces — the well-known, floral-toned Geisha and the lesser-known, more balanced Java.

title: Colombia Finca Jardines del Eden Ice Fermentation Natural
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Extremely sweet, intentionally fermenty, wine-like aroma. Red wine, salted caramel, gardenia, pomelo, hazelnut brittle in aroma and small cup. Plush, syrupy mouthfeel; crisply nut-toned and caramelly finish. In milk, this coffee is dessert-like in its impossibly deep sweetness.
notes: Produced at Finca Jardines del Eden entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by an experimental variation on the fermented natural method that involves freezing the whole fruit for five days before drying. GK Coffee is a nano-roastery in Yilan, Taiwan that offers both retail and wholesale coffee. For more information, visit www.gkcoffee.com.tw or email gkcoffee2015@gmail.com.
bottom_line: Designed for milk drinks, this very sweet, very rich-toned experimentally processed Colombia coffee is for fans of caramelly, nutty profiles with intentional wine-like ferment.

title: Colombia Finca Juan Martin Aced Sidra
blind_assessment: Intensely fruit- and floral-toned. Passionfruit, star jasmine, pink grapefruit zest, amber, salted caramel in aroma and cup. Richly bittersweet structure with balanced, juicy acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Resonant, lingering, flavor-saturated finish.
notes: Produced by Juan Martin, entirely of the Sidra variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Revel Coffee is a micro-roaster located in Billings, Montana. Its motto: “Quality is paramount – a difference you can revel in.” Visit www.revelcoffee.com or call 406-534-9621 for more information.
bottom_line: A gorgeous presentation of the rare and admired Sidra variety — natural-processed to amplify fruit and florals — juicy, bright, balanced.

title: Colombia Finca Juan Martin Sidra Natural
blind_assessment: Richly fruit-centric, flavor-saturated. Lavender, cherry candy, Orange Crush, baking chocolate, oak in aroma and cup. Brisk, citrusy acidity; plush, creamy mouthfeel. Lavender and cherry candy carry the focused finish.
notes: Produced at Finca Juan Martin, owned and operated by Banexport, entirely of the Sidra variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Established in 2009 by Amy and Scott Angelo, Oceana brews specialty coffees that have been roasted in small batches at its roasting house and café in Tequesta, Florida. Visit www.oceanacoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: Spice-toned florals and sweetly tart fruit notes are front and center in this confident natural Colombia Sidra.

title: Colombia Finca La España Gesha
blind_assessment: Brightly sweet, deeply floral. Star jasmine, apricot, almond, caramel, marjoram in aroma and cup. Sweet-toned structure with gently bright, juicy acidity; very appealing silky mouthfeel. Floral-and nut-toned finish.
notes: Produced by Duberney Cifuentes, entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Founded in 2013, modcup coffee focuses on fresh roasting and distinctive natural-processed coffees. Visit modcup.com for more information.
bottom_line: A lovely floral-driven washed Geisha cup, with the flowers supported by richly sweet stone fruit and sweet herb.

title: Colombia Finca La Guaca Ají
blind_assessment: Elegant, delicate, rich-toned. Mango, cocoa nib, marjoram, lavender, cane sugar in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart structure with bright, juicy acidity; very full, syrupy mouthfeel. The pretty finish leads with lavender and cocoa nib.
notes: Produced by José Hernán Salazar Benavides and Marina Elina Ansasoy of Finca La Guaca entirely of the Ají (an Ethiopian landrace) variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method. Founded in 1995 by Brooke McDonnell and Helen Russell, Equator Coffees operates retail stores in the San Francisco Bay Area and southern California and provides coffee to hundreds of wholesale accounts. Visit www.equatorcoffees.com or call 800-809-7687 for more information.
bottom_line: A focused but lush cup from trees of a rare indigenous Ethiopian landrace variety grown in Colombia called Aji — tropical-leaning with a cocoa backbone.

title: Colombia Finca La Ilusion Rosevel Ortiz Escarpeta Natural Espresso
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Richly fruit-toned, balanced. Blackberry, baker's chocolate, hazelnut butter, honey, oak in aroma and small cup. Satiny-smooth mouthfeel; crisp, resonant finish. In cappuccino-scaled milk, chocolate tones are foregrounded, supported by berry and hazelnut.
notes: Produced by Rosevel Ortiz Escarpeta from trees of the Caturra and Castillo varieties of Arabica and processed by the natural method, meaning the beans were dried inside the fruit rather than after the fruit has been removed, as is the case with wet-processed or “washed” coffees. Soul Work Coffee focuses on sourcing exceptional coffees and meticulously roasting them for memorable sensory experiences. Visit www.soulworkcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A fruit-driven natural-processed espresso from Colombia, particularly inviting in milk.
coffee_origin: San Agustín growing region, Huila Department, Colombia

title: Colombia Finca La Loma Antonio Gualguan
blind_assessment: Balanced, richly sweet. Black cherry, molasses, cedar, baker's chocolate, lily-like flowers in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart structure with brisk acidity; crisp, velvety mouthfeel. Notes of baker's chocolate and molasses frame the short finish, while cedar and lily re-emerge in the gently drying long.
notes: Produced by Antonio Gualguan at Finca La Loma, entirely from trees of the Caturra variety of Arabica. This is a wet-processed or “washed” coffee, meaning the fruit skin and pulp were removed from the beans immediately after harvesting and before drying. Soul Work Coffee focuses on sourcing exceptional coffees and meticulously roasting them for memorable sensory experiences. Visit www.soulworkcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A crisp, sweet-toned Colombia cup with engaging stone fruit and chocolate notes throughout.

title: Colombia Finca La Loma Microlot
blind_assessment: High-toned, sweetly tart. Bing cherry, cocoa nib, honeysuckle, cedar, a hint of thyme in aroma and cup. Sweet-tart structure with bright, juicy acidity. Full, syrupy mouthfeel. The engaging finish leads with notes of cherry and honeysuckle, and cocoa nib resurfaces in the long.
notes: Produced at Finca La Loma of the Pink Bourbon, Colombia and Castillo varieties of Arabica and processed by the wet, or washed, method. BeanFruit Coffee Co. is an award-winning coffee roasting company located in the Jackson, Mississippi metro area that provides fresh-roasted coffee with a focus on single origins. Visit www.beanfruit.com or call 601-624-2605 for more information.
bottom_line: An exceptional Colombia cup with sweet and tart impulses in balance: deeply sweet florals and bright fruit notes throughout.

title: Colombia Finca La Maria Geisha Natural
blind_assessment: Intoxicatingly (though cleanly) fruit-toned. Raspberry coulis, halvah, plumeria, pink peppercorn, lemon verbena in aroma and cup. Richly sweet-tart structure with bright, high-toned acidity; delicate, silky smooth mouthfeel. The finish maintains the tart-sweetness of the cup, while intensifying its herby citrus.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 17 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 30 Coffees of 2019. This coffee also tied for the second-highest rating in a cupping of coffees of the Geisha/Gesha variety of Arabica for Coffee Review’s September 2019 tasting report. Produced from trees of the rare Ethiopia-derived botanical variety Geisha (also spelled Gesha) by Orlando and Maria Ospina of Finca La Maria farm. With its generally elongated beans and distinctive floral and crisp, often chocolaty cup, the Geisha/Gesha variety continues to distinguish itself as one of the world’s most unique coffees. This is a “natural” or dry-processed version, meaning the beans were dried inside the fruit, encouraging a flavor profile that is sweeter and deeper-toned than the more familiar wet-processed profiles of Colombia. Klatch Coffee is an award-winning small-batch roasting company in the Los Angeles area whose resident barista and trainer, Heather Perry, won both the 2003 and 2007 United States Barista Championships brewing a Klatch Coffee espresso blend. Visit www.klatchroasting.com or call 877-455-2824 for more information.
bottom_line: An unabashedly fruit-centered natural-processed Geisha with big florals to match the fruit and compelling, subtle spice undertones.

title: Colombia Finca La Primavera Sidra
blind_assessment: Delicately aromatic, complex, citrusy. Bergamot, candied violet, cocoa nib, honeysuckle, pineapple taffy in aroma and cup. Richly bittersweet structure with bright acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Resonant, long, flavor-laden finish that carries through on the promise of the cup.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 19 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 30 Coffees of 2022. Produced by Arnulfo Leguizamo of Finca La Primavera, entirely of the admired Sidra variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method. Paradise Roasters specializes in micro-lot Arabica and Robusta coffees from Asia and other emerging origins. Paradise prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.
bottom_line: A gorgeous rendition of the Sidra variety of Arabica from Colombia: complex, lyrical, nuanced, deep.

title: Colombia Finca La Reserva Coferment
blind_assessment: Fruit-forward, sweetly fermenty. Strawberry, watermelon taffy, cocoa nib, sour cherry, lemongrass in aroma and cup. Brisk, sweet-tart acidity; plush, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Fruity, crisply tart finish.
notes: Produced by Marlon Rojas Perez of Finca La Reserva, entirely of the Sidra variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method and fermented with fruit musts of melon and strawberry. Roasted in Rome, Italy, by Aliena Coffee Roasters and distributed in the U.S. by Torrefare, in Brooklyn, New York. Visit www.torrefare.com for more information.
bottom_line: A fun, playful Colombia coferment that centers big fruit notes that range from very sweet to very tart, with a cocoa nib throughline that harmonizes all.

title: Colombia Finca La Reserva
blind_assessment: Intensely sweet, deeply aromatic. Magnolia, dried apricot, cocoa nib, lemon drop, pineapple taffy. Tart-savory acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Cocoa-toned pineapple taffy and magnolia notes lead in the finish.
notes: Produced by Juan Felipe of Finca La Reserva, entirely of the Gesha variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method (fermented in an oxygen-free environment for 96 hours), then dried in the whole fruit. Bonlife Coffee Roasters is a woman-owned specialty roaster in Cleveland, Tennessee. Visit www.bonlifecoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A fun roller coaster of a sensory ride: floral, fruity, citrusy and cocoa-toned, this complex anaerobic Colombia Geisha delights at every surprising turn.

title: Colombia Finca La Roca
blind_assessment: Juicy, fruit-driven. Dried apricot, rambutan, cocoa nib, magnolia, bergamot in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart structure with bright, vibrant acidity; full, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Floral finish with dried apricot undertones.
notes: Produced by Jorge Rojas of Finca La Roca, entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the honey anaerobic method, in which some of the fruit flesh is left on the beans both while they undergo fermentation in a hermetically sealed vessel, and when they are dried. Jaunt Coffee Roasters is a San Diego-based roaster and café with an extensive coffee and food menu. Visit www.jauntcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A Colombia honey anaerobic with a profile driven by tropical fruit, sweet floral, cocoa and bittersweet citrus notes, impressively complex, nuanced and engaging.

title: Colombia Finca La Secreta Lychee Caturra Anaerobic
blind_assessment: Floral-toned, richly fruity. Wisteria, lychee, kumquat, cocoa nib, marjoram in aroma and cup. High-toned, juicy acidity; viscous, syrupy mouthfeel. Very floral finish with cocoa undertones.
notes: Produced by Juan Carlos Mejia of Finca La Secreta, entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method with the addition of lychee to the fermentation. Bear Lake Coffee Co., a B Corp-certified coffeehouse and roastery located in Barronett, Wisconsin, is committed to sustainability through its Coffee with a Purpose™ initiative, which ensures that farmers receive compensation well above the Fairtrade Premium for their exceptional small-batch coffee. Visit www.bearlakecoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: Colombia Caturra co-fermented with Lychee for dramatic and delicious effect — think floral bomb carried by distinct lychee notes (and cocoa nib).

title: Colombia Lychee Co-Ferment
blind_assessment: Very fruit-forward, richly sweet. Lychee, kiwi, nectarine, freesia, tangerine zest on aroma and cup. Juicy, bright acidity; full, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Lychee-laden finish with spicy floral undertones.
notes: Produced by Juan Carlos Mejia of Finca La Secreta, entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method with the addition of lychee to the fermentation. Revel Coffee is a micro-roaster located in Billings, Montana. Its motto: “Quality is paramount – a difference you can revel in.” Visit www.revelcoffee.com or call 406-534-9621 for more information.
bottom_line: A flavor-bomb of a co-fermented anaerobic — Finca La Secreta’s Caturra processed with lychee is for the coffee lover who hasn’t quite yet tried everything.

title: Colombia Finca La Sirena Mango Co-Ferment
blind_assessment: Richly floral, deeply fruity. Guava, cocoa nib, neroli, almond butter, cedar in aroma and cup. Crisply tart acidity; very satiny, viscous mouthfeel. Resonant, lingering, flavor-saturated finish.
notes: Produced by Juan Puerta of Finca La Sirena, entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by the honey method with osmotic dehydration (which involves soaking coffee cherries in a hypertonic glucose solution to create osmotic pressure that gently removes moisture from the fruit) and co-fermented with mango. Bonlife Coffee Roasters is a woman-owned specialty roaster in Cleveland, Tennessee. Visit www.bonlifecoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: Tropical fruit and floral notes carry this confident, complex Colombia co-ferment with a particularly bright, multilayered finish.

title: Colombia Finca Las Margaritas Natural Sudan Rume
blind_assessment: Sweetly fermenty, wine-toned. Lychee, dried raspberry, grappa, dark chocolate fudge, lily in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart structure with crisp, citrusy acidity; delicate, silky-smooth mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to notes of dried raspberry, grappa and dark chocolate.
notes: This coffee tied for the third-highest rating in a cupping of “desert-island coffees” submitted by roasters for Coffee Review’s May 2020 tasting report. Comprised entirely of beans from the rare Sudan Rume, a presumably very old variety of Arabica originally selected from wild trees growing on the Boma Plateau of Sudan, close to the border with Ethiopia. Produced by Rigoberto Herrera at Granja La Esperanza in Colombia and processed by the dried-in-the-fruit, or natural, method. modcup coffee, founded in 2013, focuses on fresh roasting and distinctive natural-processed coffees. Visit modcup.com for more information.
bottom_line: Intensely sweet, boldly fermenty, soothingly seductive with its winy aromas and flavors.
coffee_origin: Valle del Cauca growing region, Colombia

title: Colombia Finca Las Nubes
blind_assessment: Richly sweet-savory. Tamarind, candycap mushroom, fresh-cut fir, grapefruit zest, freesia in aroma and cup. Bittersweet structure with brisk acidity; crisp, satiny mouthfeel. Gently drying finish centered around notes of tamarind and fresh-cut fir.
notes: Produced by Claudia Samboni, entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Hub Coffee Roasters is a specialty roaster focused on single-origin coffees, with several cafes in the Reno area. Visit www.hubcoffeeroasters.com for more information.
bottom_line: A savory-leaning Colombia cup with undertones of spicy florals and tangy tropical fruit.

title: Colombia Finca Lord Baltimore Papayo
blind_assessment: Floral, citrusy, delicate yet deeply sweet. Honeysuckle, blood orange, sugar cane, nougat, cocoa nib in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart structure with high-toned, juicy acidity; plush, lively mouthfeel. The crisp finish centers around notes of honeysuckle, blood orange and cocoa nib.
notes: Produced by Deiro Garcia in Colombia at Finca Lord Baltimore entirely of the Ethiopia landrace Papayo variety, and fermented in the whole fruit inside a hermetically sealed vessel, making it one version of what the coffee industry has come to call “anaerobic” or limited-oxygen processing. Paradise Roasters specializes in micro-lot Arabica and Robusta coffees from Asia and other emerging origins. The company prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.
bottom_line: A bright, richly aromatic Colombia cup from a rare tree variety worth seeking out: intricately balanced, exceptionally high-toned, both rich and delicate.

title: Colombia Finca Luisa Juan Pablo Carbonic Maceration
blind_assessment: Fruit-toned, crisply cocoa-driven. Tropical fruit melange, cocoa powder, gardenia, balsa wood, cashew in aroma and cup. Sweet-tart structure with brisk acidity; lightly satiny mouthfeel. Sweet, wood-framed finish with quiet fruit notes.
notes: Produced by Juan Pablo of Finca La Luisa, from trees of the Yellow and Red Caturra varieties of Arabica, and processed by the natural carbonic maceration method, which involves fermenting whole coffee fruit inside a sealed container that has been flushed with CO2, then drying the coffee in the whole fruit. Avatar Coffee Roasters is a specialty roaster based in Montclair, California. Visit www.avatarcoffeeroasters.com.
bottom_line: A fruit-forward Colombia cup processed by carbonic maceration, with supporting notes of cocoa and rich aromatic wood.

title: Colombia Finca Mikava Gesha Hybrid Washed Process
blind_assessment: Lush, orchestral, uniquely savory. Ginger blossom, pineapple guava, frankincense, pistachio, fennel seed, hint of cumin in aroma and cup. Deeply sweet, umami-laced acidity; crisp, silky mouthfeel. Expressive, harmonious, complete finish.
notes: Produced by Paul and Kevin Doyle of Finca Mikava, entirely of the Gesha variety of Arabica, and processed by a hybrid washed method involving a double-phase fermentation in sealed tanks filled with carbon dioxide, first in whole cherry and again after depulping. Mossto from the first fermentation is added, along with an additional amount of mossto from the two prior fermentations. Fermentation continued for approximately two additional days until the desired PH was reached. Chuck’s Roast was founded by Chuck Patton, founder of Bird Rock Coffee Roasters, to bring rare, often elusive coffees to discerning coffee lovers. Visit www.chuckroastscoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A profoundly original Colombia Gesha that fuses explosive florals, tropical fruit and savory spice into a cup of extraordinary complexity, precision and multilayered resonance.

title: Colombia Finca Milan Nitro Caturra
blind_assessment: Boozy-sweet, richly layered. Caramelized pineapple, toffee, pink grapefruit zest, baking chocolate and candied ginger in aroma and cup. Gently bright, fruit-toned acidity; plush, syrupy body. The finish is long and resonant, centered around caramel, citrus and resonant chocolate notes.
notes: Produced by Julio Cesar of Finca Milano, entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by a proprietary “Nitro Toffee” culturing fermentation that involves first sealing the whole cherries in a bioreactor and inoculating with a custom mix of yeast and bacteria. The environment is flushed with nitrogen to optimize microbial metabolic activity, while temperature, acidity, and sugar content are closely tracked. Once fermentation reaches its target profile, the coffee is dried slowly to 10 to 12 percent moisture before hulling. Revel Coffee is a micro-roaster located in Billings, Montana. Its motto: “Quality is paramount — a difference you can revel in.” Visit www.revelcoffee.com or call 406-534-9621 for more information.
bottom_line: A confidently executed fermentation-driven Caturra that balances confection-like sweetness with structure, delivering a lush, fermenty yet composed cup.

title: Colombia Finca Milan Washed Nitro Caturra
blind_assessment: Delicately sweet, richly perfumed. Watermelon candy, lychee, magnolia, almond butter, black sage in aroma and cup. Balanced, bright acidity; very full, creamy mouthfeel. Resonant finish centers notes of watermelon candy, magnolia and almond.
notes: Produced by Julio Cesar Madrid Tisnes of Finca Milan, entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by nitro-washed method in which ripe cherries undergo embryonic stress. After pulping, the beans are placed in a bioreactor and inoculated with yeast and bacteria for controlled fermentation. Nitrogen is injected to facilitate microbial metabolic processes, closely monitoring temperature, acidity, and Brix throughout. Following bioreactor treatment, the coffee beans are solar-dried to 40% moisture, then transferred to mechanical dryers until they reach 10%-12% moisture. The coffee undergoes a 45-day resting period in the warehouse before hulling. Revel Coffee is a micro-roaster located in Billings, Montana. Its motto: “Quality is paramount – a difference you can revel in.” Visit www.revelcoffee.com or call 406-534-9621 for more information.
bottom_line: A layered, enigmatic, experimentally processed Colombia, rich with complex fruit, floral and herb notes throughout the profile.

title: Colombia Finca Monte Verde, Gildardo Gutierrez
blind_assessment: This deeply nuanced coffee requires patience to fully engage its originality and distinction. Sweet-savory in structure with honey, lilac, roasted cacao nib and ripe peach in aroma and cup. Plump, juicy acidity; an almost honeyish viscosity in the mouthfeel. Lilac, honey and cacao nib in particular carry into a long, flavor-saturated finish.
notes: This exceptional coffee is only available in-store at Sightglass Coffee in San Francisco. Produced by farmer Gildardo Gutierrez, who was gifted the farm by his father as a wedding present. Sightglass Coffee is a small-batch sibling-owned coffee company with two roasteries located in San Francisco. Sightglass works tirelessly at its craft to perfect and deliver excellence in coffee. Visit www.sightglass.com or call 415-861-1313 for more information.

title: Colombia Finca Monteblanco Purple Caturra Passionfruit Washed
blind_assessment: Delicately fruit-forward, deep-toned. Pomegranate, alyssum, saltwater taffy, almond, brown sugar in aroma and cup. Brisk acidity; satiny-smooth mouthfeel. Gentle finish centered around suggestions of pomegranate and almond.
notes: Produced at Finca Monteblanco, entirely of the Purple Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp are removed before drying) with the addition of passionfruit to the conventional fermentation step. GK Coffee is a nano-roastery in Yilan, Taiwan, that offers both retail and wholesale coffee. For more information, visit www.gkcoffee.com.tw.
bottom_line: Tart fruit and delicately sweet florals characterize this conventionally fermented, passionfruit-infused Colombia Purple Caturra.

title: Colombia Finca Monteverde
blind_assessment: Gently fruit-toned. Dried cranberry, agave syrup, freesia, cedar, marjoram in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart with brisk acidity; crisp, satiny mouthfeel. Quietly fruity finish with undertones of spicy florals.
notes: Produced by Newerley Gutierrez of Finca Monteverde, entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Yipao Coffee Roasters, based in San Diego, was founded by two native Colombians who specialize in single-origin Colombia coffees. Visit www.yipao-coffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A balanced, easygoing natural-processed Colombia Geisha with engaging fruit, floral and herb notes.

title: Colombia Finca Nogales Java Advanced Fermentation
