bottom_line: An exceptional light-roasted Colombia Sidra that delivers striking fruit and floral intensity with an almost weightless clarity, its elaborate processing expressed through vivid acidity, sweetness and aromatic complexity.

title: Colombia Las Flores Mint-Macerated
blind_assessment: Deep, rich, sweetly herbaceous. Heavy cream, sweet herb melange, caramel, Meyer lemon, the aroma of oak forest in aroma and cup. Gentle, round acidity; plump mouthfeel. Fades gracefully to bittersweet herb notes.
notes: Produced by John Vergara of Finca Las Flores, entirely of the Yellow Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed anaerobic process with the addition of mint leaves to the fermentation step. Founded in 1995 by Brooke McDonnell and Helen Russell, Equator Coffees operates retail stores in the San Francisco Bay Area and Southern California and provides coffee to hundreds of wholesale accounts. Visit www.equatorcoffees.com or call 800-809-7687 for more information.
bottom_line: A uniquely composed mint-macerated Colombia that’s balanced, sweetly herbal and floral and quite subtle in its complex sweetness

title: Colombia Las Flores Red Bourbon Natural
blind_assessment: Richly sweet-tart. Tamarind, raspberry, cocoa nib, thyme, cedar in aroma and cup. Juicy-tart acidity; plush, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to notes of raspberry and cocoa nib.
notes: Produced by the Ayure Family of Finca Las Flores, entirely of the Red Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). RamsHead Coffee Roasters is a family-owned company founded by Bozeman, Montana natives Caleb and Laura Walker that specializes in direct trade microlot coffees. For more information, visit www.ramsheadcoffee.com.
bottom_line: A zesty, invigorating natural-processed Colombia with tart fruit notes grounded by cocoa nib and sweet herbs.

title: Colombia Las Hermosas Medium Roast
blind_assessment: Sweet, delicate, floral-toned aroma with hints of lemon and a buttery chocolate. Reveals weight and power in the cup, with a rich acidity with continued floral, lemon and butter notes. Clean, rich finish.
notes: This coffee reflects an ongoing partnership between Reunion Island Coffee and the Las Hermosas Cooperative of small farms in southern Tolima Department of Colombia. In the last two years of the project partnership Reunion Island Coffee has donated funds to build drying beds and a cupping laboratory for the cooperative. Reunion Island Coffee is a quality-oriented roasting company founded by Canadian specialty coffee veteran Peter Pesce. Visit www.reunionislandcoffee.com or call 800-565-5950 for more information.

title: Colombia Las Hermosas
blind_assessment: Sweetly bright, balanced, classic. Ripe tangerine, apricot, honeysuckle-like flowers, hazelnut, fresh-cut cedar in aroma and cup. Delicate, lively acidity; lightly plush mouthfeel. Flavor consolidates in a gently tart, richly balanced finish.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the #29 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 30 Coffees of 2015. This coffee reflects an ongoing partnership between Reunion Island Coffee and the Las Hermosas Cooperative of small farms in southern Tolima Department of Colombia. Since the project began in 2004, Reunion Island has donated funds improve both the quality of coffee and the standard of living for the cooperative farmers, having supported parabolic drying beds for two hundred farms, a full cupping lab, a complete overhaul of sanitation and water purification systems for seven schools, and multiple computer labs within schools. Various farmers from this cooperative have placed well in Colombia’s Cup of Excellence competition. Reunion Island Coffee is a quality-oriented roasting company founded by Canadian specialty coffee veteran Peter Pesce. Visit www.reunionislandcoffee.com or call 800-565-5950 for more information.

title: Colombia Las Joyas: Fidencio Martinez Lot
blind_assessment: High-toned sweetness, crisply tart, pleasantly salty-edged. Dried apricot, tamarind, salted chocolate, cedar, magnolia in aroma and cup. Gently low-toned with balanced tart and salty/savory structure; briskly juicy acidity. Full, buttery mouthfeel. Flavor simplifies in the finish, with hints of salted cocoa and dry cedar carrying into the long.
notes: This lot was produced by Fidencio Martinez, who operates one of five plots on the family estate. Processed by the honey method, which means that the outer skin is removed as it is in the wet or “washed” process, but at least some of the sticky fruit residue is allowed to dry on the bean and later removed by machine along with the parchment skin. BeanFruit Coffee Coffee Company is a small coffee-roasting company located in the Jackson, Mississippi area, founded on a desire to provide freshly roasted coffee to the Jackson area and educate local consumers about great-tasting coffee. Visit www.beanfruit.com or call 601-624-2605 for more information.
bottom_line: An attractively tart and savory honey-processed coffee. Try it with salty morning dishes, which should develop its subtle, complementary sweetness.

title: Colombia Las Margaritas Sudan Rume
blind_assessment: Intricate, immensely sweet. Dried raspberry, orange zest, mousse-like chocolate, Cognac, sandalwood in aroma and cup. Punchy, sweet acidity; velvety mouthfeel. The flavor consolidates to chocolate and dried raspberry, with a hint of sweet ferment, in the finish.
notes: Comprised entirely of beans from the rare Sudan Rume, a presumably very old variety of Arabica originally selected from wild trees growing on the Boma Plateau of Sudan, close to the border with Ethiopia. Processed by the honey method, which means that the outer skin is removed as it is in the wet or “washed” process, but at least some of the sticky fruit residue is allowed to dry on the bean and later removed by machine along with the parchment skin. Produced by farmer Rigoberto Herrera at Granja La Esperanza in Colombia, an innovative producer that specializes in impressive and innovative work with unusual cultivars of Arabica. Water Avenue Coffee is a tiny roastery nestled next to the railway in the old Industrial Southeast quarter in Portland, Oregon. Visit www.wateravenuecoffee.com or call 503-808-7083 for more information.
bottom_line: An elegant, berry-toned, chocolaty version of the rare coffee variety Sudan Rume.
coffee_origin: Valle del Cauca growing region, Colombia

title: Colombia Las Mercedes 2011 Cup of Excellence #2 Auction Lot
blind_assessment: Complex, explosively fresh aroma: ripe strawberry, watermelon, sweet lemon, raspberry. In the cup the fruit simplifies and turns zesty and bittersweet, dry yet juicy. Lean-bodied; dry-finishing.
notes: The Cup of Excellence is the most esteemed competition for green coffees from a given country of origin; this was the second-place prize winner from the Colombia 2011 competition chosen by a select group of national and international cuppers. Linking Coffee is a specialty coffee roaster and broker of green, unroasted coffees in Taipei City, Taiwan. Its focus is on high-quality green coffee imports and espresso blends by design. Visit www.linkingcoffee.blogspot.com or call +886-2-23826549 for more information.

title: Colombia Las Mingas Micro-Lot – Anival Gomez
blind_assessment: The aroma is sweet-toned and alive with flowers, ripe tomato, a hint of cedar; the mouthfeel silky. The issue in the cup is the acidity, sweet but intense, all but sidelining delicate cocoa and floral notes and carrying with dry authority into the finish.
notes: La Mingas is a program set up by coffee exporter Virmax Cafe, designed to promote direct trade relationships between quality-minded Colombian coffee growers and importers and roasters in coffee consuming countries. Based in the San Diego area, Bird Rock Coffee Roasters is a retailer and wholesaler that focuses on organic and socially responsible coffees. Visit www.birdrockcoffee.com or call 858-551-1707 for more information.

title: Colombia Las Palmas Co-Ferment
blind_assessment: Spice-toned, richly sweet-savory. POG, pink peppercorn, lemon verbena, oak, frankincense in aroma and cup. Gentle, round acidity; plush, satiny mouthfeel. Notes of POG and pink peppercorn are front and center in the brisk finish.
notes: Produced by Brayan Alvear, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by co-fermenting the whole cherries with dehydrated coconut and coconut water, then drying them in the whole fruit with lemon peel. Based in Livingston, Montana, RamsHead Coffee Roasters is a family-owned company that specializes in direct trade microlot coffees. For more information, visit www.ramsheadcoffee.com.
bottom_line: A uniquely composed Colombia co-ferment with a spice throughline supported by sweet herbs and resiny aromatics.
coffee_origin: San Adolfo, Acevedo, Huila Department, Colombia

title: Colombia Las Palmas Tropical Splash
blind_assessment: Fruity-sweet, gently spice-toned. Fruit punch, green peppercorn, blackberry leaf, oak, hazelnut in aroma and cup. Briskly sweet acidity; velvety-smooth mouthfeel. Green peppercorn and fruit punch notes carry the quiet finish.
notes: Produced by Brayan Alvea, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by co-fermenting the whole cherries with dehydrated coconut and coconut water, then drying them in the whole fruit with lemon peel. Bonlife Coffee Roasters is a woman-owned specialty roaster in Cleveland, Tennessee. Visit www.bonlifecoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A uniquely composed juxtaposition of sweet and spicy notes, with fruit punch at the top (remember Hi-C) and forestry oak at the bottom.

title: Colombia Las Perlitas Anaerobic Honey
blind_assessment: Bright, balanced, juicy-sweet. Cocoa nib, strawberry guava, cashew butter, pink peppercorn, lemongrass in aroma and cup. High-toned, malic acidity; very smooth, satiny mouthfeel. Cocoa-toned finish with notes of lemongrass and pink peppercorn.
notes: Sourced from Coffee Quest in Medellin, Colombia; produced by smallholding farmers and comprised of “las perlitas” (little pearls) of green coffees that are a blend of high-end varieties from lots that are too small, as well as salvaged high-end green coffees that were re-sorted and salvaged from the defect piles. Processed by the anaerobic honey method, in which in some of the fruit flesh is removed from the beans, then fermented in an oxygen-free environment before drying. Iconik Coffee Roasters is a specialty coffee roaster in Santa Fe, New Mexico with three cafes. Visit www.iconikcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: This uniquely composed blend of green coffees has tart fruit, crisp cocoa nib and herby citrus notes throughout its profile.

title: Colombia Las Perlitas
blind_assessment: Bright, fruit-forward, and floral. Aromas and flavors of mandarin orange, red currant, honeysuckle, cocoa nib, and almond. Sweetly tart acidity; light, silky body. Crisp, citrusy finish.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Kafe Coffee Roastery is a specialty roaster based in Zhubei, Taiwan. Visit shopee.tw/zengkaochen for more information.
bottom_line: A lively washed Pink Bourbon from Huila with citrus and floral top notes balanced by cocoa depth.

title: Colombia Las Rosas
blind_assessment: Soft, floral-toned. Almond blossom, cocoa nib, date, pear cedar in aroma and cup. Gentle, round acidity; smooth, very satiny mouthfeel. Quiet, sweet-toned finish with hints of almond blossom and pear.
notes: Produced by smallholding members of the Association of Women Coffee Growers of West Huila (Asociación de Mujeres Cafeteras del Occidente del Huila), which makes up the Las Rosas Women’s Coffee Project, from trees of the Caturra and Castillo varieties of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Founded in 1995 by Brooke McDonnell and Helen Russell, Equator Coffees operates retail stores in the San Francisco Bay Area and Southern California and provides coffee to hundreds of wholesale accounts. Visit www.equatorcoffees.com or call 800-809-7687 for more information.
bottom_line: Balanced and comforting, this washed Colombia offers subtle complexity and familiar richness — and it’s a very nice medium roast.

title: Colombia Limited Release 2024
blind_assessment: Richly aromatic, sweetly savory. Pineapple kefir, cocoa nib, lavender, pink grapefruit zest, lemon verbena in aroma and cup. Briskly sweet-savory acidity; plush, satiny mouthfeel. Especially long, lingering finish that extends the promise of the cup.
notes: Produced by Don Hernando Laverde of Finca La Guirnalda, entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed at La Palma y Tucan by the anaerobic natural method, in which the whole fruit is fermented in tanks with limited oxygen before drying, also in the whole fruit. In this case, lactic acid was added to the fermentation step. Blue Sail Coffee Roasters is an Arkansas roastery and cafe whose mission is “to inspire people to adventure more.” Visit www.bluesailcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A lactic-anaerobic Colombia with a sweet pineapple tanginess throughout and undertones of cocoa nib, complex citrus, and spice-toned florals.

title: Colombia Linarco Rodriguez Ospina Pink Bourbon Washed 94
blind_assessment: Delicately bright, balanced, richly sweet-tart. Red plum and cocoa nib in the aroma, deepening into Meyer lemon zest, shortbread and lilac in the cup. Gently bright, vibrant acidity; plush, silky mouthfeel. Very rich, multi-layered finish, deeply aromatic finish.
notes: Produced by Linarco Rodriguez Ospina, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Buon Caffe is a specialty coffee roaster and cafe in Taipei, Taiwan. Visit www.buoncaffe.com.tw for more information.
bottom_line: An unassuming initial break opens up on the table with big florals, stone fruit and complex citrus notes throughout the cup and into the very long finish.

title: Colombia Lisandro Cardenas Gesha Natural
blind_assessment: Lush, perfumed, and deeply fruit-toned. Raspberry, yellow peach, passion fruit, jasmine, and cocoa nib in aroma and cup. Bright, juicy acidity; plush, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. The finish is exceptionally long and expressive, with raspberry, jasmine, and cocoa nib lingering.
notes: Produced by Lisandro Cardenas of Finca Las Brisas, entirely of the Gesha variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Intuition Coffee is a specialty roaster and cafe based in Peoria, Illinois. Visit www.intuitioncoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: An elegant yet exuberant natural-process Gesha that layers ripe fruit and heady florals over a deep cocoa sweetness, with impressive structure and persistence.

title: Colombia Los Lirios Cup of Excellence
blind_assessment: Fine aroma: high-toned, elegant, combining suggestions of flowers, lemon, cedar and peach in a single suave, tight-knit aromatic gesture. In the cup delicately rich, light-bodied but not lean, gently acidy. The peach-floral-lemon gesture deepens and leans toward chocolate. Only the finish is disappointing: short and slightly but distractingly astringent.
notes: A prize winner in the 2005 Colombia Second Harvest Cup of Excellence (www.cupofexcellence.org) competition, where as a green (unroasted) coffee it placed 29th out of hundreds of entries. Offered by Batdorf & Bronson as a selection in its Latitudes Limited Edition Coffees. Batdorf is a premium wholesale specialty roaster with a long and honorable commitment to quality and sound relationships with growers. Visit www.batdorfcoffee.com or call 800-955-5282 for more information.

title: Colombia Los Naranjos San Agustin
blind_assessment: Sweet, rich and balanced aroma complicated by cherry- and strawberry-like fruit. Continued balance in the cup; caramel notes combine with tartly sweet fruit suggesting lemon and cranberry. Sweetness and flavor outlast a very slight astringency in the finish.
notes: Growing areas east of the Andes in the southern Colombia Department of Huila are particularly admired for their fine coffees. Roasted at PT's Coffee, where the motto is "without the love, it's just coffee." Visit www.ptscoffee.com or call 888-678-5282 for more information.
coffee_origin: San Agustin growing region, Huila Department, southern Colombia

title: Colombia Los Nogales Yellow Bourbon
blind_assessment: Tangy-sweet, fruit-driven. Muscat grape, strawberry yogurt, dark chocolate, maple syrup, candycap mushroom in aroma and cup. Tangy, juicy acidity; very full, syrupy mouthfeel. Dark chocolate and muscat notes are front and center in the resonant finish.
notes: Produced at Finca Los Nogales, entirely of the Yellow Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed anaerobic method, in which the fermentation step occurs in a hermetically sealed vessel before the beans are washed and dried. SÖT Coffee Roaster, based in Osaka, Japan, is a self-described Swedish-style roaster with an “aggressively light” roasting style. For more information, visit www.sotcoffee.com.
bottom_line: A complex, sweet-tangy-savory Colombia anaerobic that’s as rich as it is high-toned and juicy, covering all sensory bases in both aroma and flavor.

title: Colombia Los Pinos Robeiro Sarmiento
blind_assessment: Chocolaty, deep-toned. Baking chocolate, date, cedar, narcissus, almond in aroma and cup. Sweet structure with brisk acidity; velvety mouthfeel. The finish consolidates to notes of baking chocolate and cedar.
notes: Produced by Robeiro Sarmiento and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and flesh are removed from the beans before they are dried). Founded in 1994, Coffee By Design is a specialty coffee roaster in Portland, Maine that also operates three coffee shops in town, as well as one in Freeport. Visit www.coffeebydesign.com.
bottom_line: A friendly, accessible, crisply sweet coffee with dried fruit, floral, and rich nut tones.

title: Colombia Luis Alberto Montoya Antioquia
blind_assessment: High-toned, crisply sweet. Date, cashew butter, magnolia, grapefruit zest, cedar in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart in structure with brisk acidity; full, velvety mouthfeel. The resonant finish leads with notes of date and magnolia in the short, rounding to cashew butter and grapefruit zest in the long.
notes: Produced by Luis Alberto Montoya at Finca Arboleda entirely from trees of the Caturra variety of Arabica. This is a wet-processed or “washed” coffee, meaning the fruit skin and pulp were removed from the beans immediately after harvesting and before drying. Temple Coffee is a quality-focused retail and wholesale specialty roaster active in Sacramento, California since 2005. Committed to sourcing, roasting and brewing the finest coffees, Temple features coffee from distinguished single estates and cooperatives around the world. Visit www.templecoffee.com or call 916-454-1282 for more information.
bottom_line: A vivacious, sweetly tart Colombia redolent of notes of rich nut butter and citrus zest.

title: Colombia Luis Calderon
blind_assessment: Sweetly tart, fruit-forward. Mango, baking chocolate, lemongrass, honey, fresh-cut fir in aroma and cup. Juicy-sweet acidity; crisp, velvety mouthfeel. Lemongrass and baking chocolate predominate in the finish.
notes: Produced by Luis Calderon of Finca Betulia, entirely of the Caturron variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Bonlife Coffee Roasters is a woman-owned specialty roaster in Cleveland, Tennessee. Visit www.bonlifecoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: Tropical fruit notes carry this brightly sweet-tart Colombia, supported by crisp chocolate and lemongrass tones.

title: Colombia Lulo Wonka Wonka & Sebastian Gomez
blind_assessment: Fruit-forward, deep-toned, enigmatic. Strawberry-guava, candied ginger, star jasmine, myrrh, lemongrass in aroma and cup. Brightly sweet-tart acidity; elegantly silky mouthfeel. Long, lingering, integrated finish.
notes: This outstanding coffee was selected as the No. 23 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 30 Coffees of 2024. A blend of two Colombia coffees, a honey-processed Caturra co-fermented with lulo fruit by Jairo Arcila, and a natural-processed Gesha from Sebatian Gomez. Bonlife Coffee Roasters is a woman-owned specialty roaster in Cleveland, Tennessee. Visit www.bonlifecoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: What do you get when you cross a honey co-ferment with a natural Gesha? An extraordinary international collab between roaster and producers — this Colombia blend is exciting, dramatic, rich, complex, and above all, harmonious and integrated, and a darn good value, to boot.

title: Colombia Luminosa (K-Cup)
blind_assessment: (As brewed in a Keurig B70 Platinum single-serve brewing device using a licensed K-Cup capsule containing 11+ grams of coffee to produce a 6-ounce serving). Quietly but robustly pungent. Bitter orange, prune, pecan, fresh-cut oak in aroma and cup. Crisp, rich acidity; lightly syrupy, roughish mouthfeel. A floral suggestion complicates a dry, oaky finish.
notes: Peet’s, which in the 1970s almost single-handedly launched the dark-roasting trend that came to dominate specialty coffee in the 1980s through 1990s, recently debuted a line of medium-roasted coffees, including this blend. Peet’s, now a privately owned corporation under the John A. Benckiser Investment group, has arguably managed to maintain its essential identity during a slow, careful expansion from its original, intensely loyalist base in the San Francisco Bay area. Visit www.peets.com or call 800-999-2132 for more information.
coffee_origin: Huila Department, southwestern Colombia; southern Ethiopia.

title: Colombia Luminosa Light Roast
blind_assessment: Mild, sweetly pungent. Apricot, brown sugar, hints of dark chocolate and lily in aroma and cup. Round, backgrounded acidity; plump mouthfeel. Flavor makes a rather faint last stand in a quiet finish.
notes: Purchased pre-ground in a 12-ounce foil bag with one-way degassing valve at a Safeway supermarket in northern California. This sample was roasted, roast-dated, and packaged at Peet’s Alameda, California facility. Peet’s, now a privately owned corporation under the John A. Benckiser Investment group, has arguably managed to maintain its essential identity during a slow, careful expansion from its original, intensely loyalist base in the San Francisco Bay area. Visit www.peets.com or call 800-999-2132 for more information.

title: Colombia Luna Azul
blind_assessment: Richly fruit-forward, deeply aromatic. Ripe blueberry, tangerine, dark chocolate, cedar, magnolia in aroma and cup. Gently bright acidity; plush, creamy mouthfeel. Blueberry-driven finish supported by dark chocolate and cedar.
notes: Produced by Álvaro Andrés Cardona Molina and processed by the black honey method, in which much of the fruit flesh is left on the beans during the drying process. Founded in 2007 and named after the white rhino, which is both rare and social, White Rhino Coffee is based in Dallas, Texas and currently has nine coffee shops in addition to its roastery. Visit whiterhinocoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A confidently fruity, richly chocolaty Colombia black honey complicated by sweet citrus and florals and pungent aromatic wood.

title: Colombia Luna Azul
blind_assessment: Richly fruit-forward, deep-toned. Black cherry, chocolate fudge, tangerine zest, amber, cedar in aroma and cup. Lively, high-toned acidity; very full, syrupy mouthfeel. Crisply sweet-tart, cherry-toned finish.
notes: Produced by Andres Cardona of Villa Lucia, from trees of the Colombia and Castillo varieties of Arabica, and processed by the black honey method, in which the skins are removed from the fruit but virtually all of the fruit flesh is allowed to dry slowly on the beans. Founded in 1990, Roadmap CoffeeWorks, formerly Lexington Coffee Roasters, is an award-winning artisan roasting company based in Lexington, Virginia. Roadmap CoffeeWorks focuses on producing fresh, distinctive and sustainable coffees. Visit www.roadmapcoffeeworks.com or call 800-322-6505 for more information.
bottom_line: A deeply sweet black honey Colombia with a throughline of black cherry and tangerine grounded by distinct chocolate fudge notes.

title: Colombia Luz Helena Salazar Wine Yeast Grape Honey
blind_assessment: Sweetly spice-toned. Concord grape, ginger blossom, baking chocolate, lemon verbena, maple syrup in aroma and cup. Gently vibrant structure with a fruity/juicy acidity; viscous, satiny mouthfeel. Cocoa-toned finish, supported by notes of lemon verbena and maple syrup.
notes: Produced by Luz Helena Salazar, entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and fermented with wine yeasts before drying by the honey method (some fruit flesh is left on the beans during drying). GK Coffee is a nano-roastery in Yilan, Taiwan that offers both retail and wholesale coffee. For more information, visit www.gkcoffee.com.tw or email gkcoffee2015@gmail.com.
bottom_line: A Colombia Castillo experimentally fermented with wine yeasts— spice-toned and lively with an especially viscous mouthfeel.

title: Colombia Manos Juntas Anaerobic Natural
blind_assessment: Delicately fruit-toned, sweetly fermenty. Ripe strawberry, rum cordial, cedar, magnolia, nutmeg in aroma and cup. Sparkling acidity; very syrupy mouthfeel. Strawberry and rum cordial lead in the long finish.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers surrounding the Manos Juntas Micromill, entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method (fermented in an oxygen-free environment, then dried in the whole fruit). Intuition Coffee is a specialty roaster and cafe based in Peoria, Illinois. Visit www.intuitioncoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A sweetly fermenty, strawberry-driven cup complicated by notes of rum cordial and bittersweet spice.

title: Colombia Manos Juntas Anaerobic Natural
blind_assessment: Sweetly berry-toned, gently fermenty. Raspberry coulis, wine barrel, dark chocolate, clove, gardenia in aroma and cup. Juicy-bright acidity; full, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Finish revolves around notes of raspberry and wine barrel.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers surrounding the Manos Juntas Micromill, entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method (fermented in an oxygen-free environment, then dried in the whole fruit). Intuition Coffee is a specialty roaster and cafe based in Peoria, Illinois. Visit www.intuitioncoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A wide-ranging natural anaerobic Colombia Castillo, both in aromatics and on the palate: berry-driven, richly chocolaty, complicated by a wine barrel throughline.

title: Colombia Manos Juntas
blind_assessment: Crisply sweet-savory. Baking chocolate, raspberry, cedar, shiitake mushroom, hazelnut in aroma and cup. Sweetly savory structure with brisk acidity; velvety mouthfeel. The finish consolidates to notes of baking chocolate and cedar.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method (fermented in the whole fruit in a hermetically sealed vessel) at Manos Juntas Micromill. Conscious Cup Coffee Roasters is an independent and family-owned and -operated cafe and coffee roaster specializing in socially and environmentally sustainable coffees. Visit www.consciouscup.com or call 815-356-0115 for more information.
bottom_line: A savory-leaning, berry-toned anaerobic natural Colombia cup, nuanced and deep.

title: Colombia Maragogipe Rainforest Alliance
blind_assessment: Lightly and sweetly acidy with delicately crisp floral, walnut and orange notes running from aroma through cup to the particularly impressive finish, where the sweetness peaks and the flavor notes consolidate and survive a slight tightness.
notes: Maragogipe (MAH-rah-go-ZHE-pay) is a variety of Arabica first discovered growing near the Brazilian town of the same name. It displays enormous bean size. But despite the showy appearance of the beans, it is not a popular variety with farmers because of low yields and an often thin, ordinary cup character. However, this particular Maragogipe from the traditional farm of El Boton in southwestern Antioquia Department, is delicate rather than thin and quietly distinctive, its subtle grace aided by a tactful light-roasted presentation. It is Rainforest-Alliance certified, meaning it was produced following sustainable ecological and socio-economic criteria developed by the Sustainable Agricultural Network, a coalition of independent, environment-focused non-governmental organizations. Leopard Forest is the brand name of a roasting company that features coffees from its own sustainably operated Zimbabwe farm as well as other fine coffees. Visit www.leopardforestcoffee.com or call 864-834-5500 for more information.

title: Colombia Martha Cecelia Rojas
blind_assessment: Refreshing, delicate, very sweet-toned. Orange, lemon, nut, and intense floral notes in aroma and cup. Juicy, wine-like acidity; silky to lightly syrupy mouthfeel. Fades very slightly in an otherwise clean, balanced finish.
notes: Lone Pine Coffee Roasters is a Bend, Oregon based company founded in 2007 by Scott and Anna Withman to bring exquisite coffees to Central Oregon and beyond. Visit www.lonepinecoffeeroasters.com or call 541-306-1010 for more information.
coffee_origin: Pitalito growing region, Huila Department, Colombia.

title: Colombia Mary Cielo Salazar Soto
blind_assessment: Deeply sweet, intensely floral. Dark chocolate, lily, clove, plum, cashew in aroma and cup. Spicy, rich acidity; full, syrupy mouthfeel. The richly drying, flavor-saturated finish consolidates to clove in the short, while cashew returns in the long.
notes: This coffee placed ninth overall at the 2016 Best of Huila green coffee competition, and was purchased at the auction following the competition. Duluth Coffee Company is a craft micro-roaster in Duluth, Minnesota, committed to providing high-quality coffee with a focus on single origins. Duluth uses insightful roasting techniques to highlight the natural nuances of each origin and retain balance in the coffee. Coffees are sourced seasonally and roasted fresh, allowing them to be enjoyed at their peak. For more information, visit www.duluthcoffeecompany.com.
bottom_line: A sweet, spice-toned, floral-edged Colombia cup.

title: Colombia Maximino Gutierrez
blind_assessment: Delicate but deep; crisply sweet. Orange, vanilla, roasted cacao nib, dried hibiscus in aroma and cup. Brisk but juicy acidity; lightly syrupy mouthfeel. Flavor consolidates but rings on in an impressively sweet, long finish.
notes: From trees of the Caturra variety, a compact growing selection of Bourbon, this coffee was grown at high elevations by Maximino Gutierrez in the Tolima Department of Colombia. BeanFruit Coffee Coffee Company is a small coffee-roasting company located in the Jackson, Mississippi area, founded on a desire to provide fresh-roasted coffee to the Jackson area and educate local consumers about great tasting coffee. Visit www.beanfruit.com or call 601-624-2605 for more information.

title: Colombia Mebsuta VMAR Espresso
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Fruity, chocolaty-sweet. Chocolate fudge, mango, fresh-cut fir, cashew, spearmint in aroma and small cup. Crisp, velvety mouthfeel; gently drying, chocolaty finish with fir undertones. In cappuccino format, mango and spearmint notes resurface to complicate the chocolate throughline.
notes: Produced by Luis Mauricio Riviera, from trees of the Caturra and Colombia varieties of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method, in which the whole fruit is fermented in tanks with limited oxygen before drying, also in the whole fruit. Roasted in Naples, Italy, by Saka Caffé and distributed in the U.S. by Torrefare. Visit www.torrefare.com for more information.
bottom_line: Especially nice prepared as cappuccino, this Colombia anaerobic natural has both depth and brightness, as well as fudgy chocolate notes throughout the profile.

title: Colombia Medellin Supremo Washed
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Chocolaty-sweet, rich-toned. Pomegranate, baking chocolate, almond,gently scorched fir, dark caramel in aroma and small cup. Creamy-smooth mouthfeel; crisp, chocolaty finish with almond and smoky fir undertones. In three parts milk, chocolaty and floral (magnolia notes emerge).
notes: Bluekoff is a Thai company involved in all aspects of coffee, from milling and roasting to coffee wholesale and retail and related equipment and training services. Bluekoff produces more than 1,200 tons of green coffee and 1,000 tons of roasted coffee per year. Visit www.bluekoff.com or email info@bluekoff.com or call +66-819799565 for more information.
bottom_line: A richly chocolaty, gently and pleasingly smoky Colombia espresso roasted in Thailand — especially appealing in cappuccino format.

title: Colombia Medium Roast
blind_assessment: Crisply chocolaty, sweetly nut-toned. Baking chocolate, cashew butter, orange zest, agave syrup, fresh-cut oak in aroma and cup. Gently bright, sparkling acidity; velvety-smooth mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to baking chocolate and cashew with oak undertones.
notes: Produced by smallholding women farmers and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Dios Mio is a Florida-based coffee company that exclusively features women-farmed Colombia coffees. Visit www.diosmiocoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: Actress Sophia Vergara’s line of Colombia coffees celebrates her homeland and its chief export — all farmed by women. The medium roast is balanced, chocolaty and richly sweet.

title: Colombia Medium Roast
blind_assessment: Deep-toned, simple aroma with fir and molasses notes. In the cup low-toned acidity, syrupy mouthfeel, continued fir and molasses notes, caramel, and perhaps a slight fruity tartness suggesting dry berry or tamarind. Sweet, simple, rich finish.
notes: Available whole-bean in bulk at many Safeway supermarkets. In early October 2008 on sale for $7.99 per pound; normally $10.64 per pound. Safeway is the third-largest supermarket chain in the United States, with nearly 1,800 stores in western and central United States and western Canada. Visit www.safeway.com for more information.

title: Colombia Micro-Lot Huila La Argentina
blind_assessment: Delicate but intense aroma, with milk chocolate, nut and coffee fruit notes that read as tart cherry. In the cup impressive balance and structure: lushly sweet but crisply acidy with a lightly syrupy mouthfeel. Continued tart cherry and chocolate notes carry into a simple but cleanly rich finish.
notes: This coffee is grown at very high altitudes by small producers in southwest Huila Department. Willoughby's Coffee & Tea is a pioneer specialty coffee roaster recently reinvigorated and refocused on artisan roasting and a very extensive collection of elite single-origin coffees. Visit www.willoughbyscoffee.com or call 800-388-8400 for more information.

title: Colombia Micro-Lot Humberto Gonzales
blind_assessment: Richly sweet-toned aroma: orange, cocoa, butterscotch. In the cup big, simple, authoritative but ingratiating, with round, ringing acidity and the pure expression of coffee fruit, a tart cherry sensation. Clean, deep, cherryish finish.
notes: From the farm of Humberto Gonzales and part of the Las Mingas project, a green coffee quality competition in southern Colombia supported by several leading small North-American roasting companies. Coffee Klatch is an award-winning small-batch roasting company in the Los Angeles area featuring small lots of exceptional coffees and whose resident barista and trainer, Heather Perry, won the 2003 and 2007 United States Barista Championships and placed second in the 2007 World Championship brewing Coffee Klatch espresso blends. Visit www.klatchroasting.com or call 877-455-2824 for more information.

title: Colombia Micro-Lot Wilmer Delgado
blind_assessment: Explosive aromatics: In the break deep, rich, buttery and honey-like with suggestions of flowers, coffee fruit, fresh-tanned leather. In the cup the butter notes turn rather pungent, toward butterscotch with continued flowers and a fruit that softens toward milk chocolate. Medium bodied, slightly underpowered and short in the finish but intense and intriguing aromatics throughout.
notes: From the farm of Wilmer Delgado, grown at an elevation of 6,000 feet from trees of the caturra variety. Coffee Klatch is an award-winning small-batch roasting company in the Los Angeles area featuring small lots of exceptional coffees and whose resident barista and trainer, Heather Perry, won the 2003 and 2007 United States Barista Championships and placed second in the 2007 World Championship brewing Coffee Klatch espresso blends. Visit www.klatchroasting.com or call 877-455-2824 for more information.

title: Colombia Miranda
blind_assessment: Elegant, deeply sweet, floral. Lush floral composite (wisteria, violet, lavender), chocolate fudge, oak, mango in aroma and cup. Lyrical, bittersweet acidity; plush, lightly silky mouthfeel. The gently drying finish simplifies to lavender and dark chocolate.
notes: Produced from the Colombia and Castillo varieties of Arabica by a collective of five farmers in the small Municipality of Miranda in the Department of Cauca, where some of Colombia’s most admired coffees are produced. This coffee tied for the second-highest rating in a test of coffees from Australian roasters conducted for Coffee Review‘s June 2016 tasting report. Ritual Coffee Tasmania was founded in Launceston, Tasmania in 2009 by Tim and Mel Jarosz, who were joined by roaster Stu Grant in 2010. They partner with skilled farmers and dedicated suppliers to find great coffees, then carefully roast them to unlock their sensory potential. For more information, visit www.ritualcoffee.com.au.
bottom_line: A solid cup nicely balanced between sweet flowers and tart fruit supported by a deeply expressed chocolate.
coffee_origin: Valle del Cauca Department, southwest Colombia

title: Colombia Mokka Anaerobic Natural Finca Hawaii
blind_assessment: Sweetly spice-toned, complex and satiatingly fruity. Black cherry kombucha, clove, pipe tobacco, molasses in aroma and cup. Lively, sparkling acidity; creamy, lithe mouthfeel. Incredibly long, harmonious, integrated finish.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 5 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 30 Coffees of 2024. Produced by Rigoberto Herrera Correa and his brother Luis at Finca Hawaii, a farm in Cundinamarca operated by Cafe Granja La Esperanza, entirely of the Mokka variety of Arabica (from seeds of Mokka trees grown in Kāʻanapali, Maui) and processed by the anaerobic natural method (whole coffee fruit is fermented with limited oxygen before drying). Paradise prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 808-498-4048 for more information.
bottom_line: A unique — and uniquely compelling  Colombia-grown Mokka from Hawaiian seeds, experimentally fermented to dramatic (fruity, spicy, savory) effect. Complex, elusive, evocative.

title: Colombia Monserrate Espresso
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. High-toned, sweet aroma: caramel and hints of orange, lemon and aromatic wood. In the small cup the fruit brightens and the suggestions of lemon and aromatic wood become more distinct, though still softened by caramel. Two parts milk deepen the caramel to a dark chocolate nuanced by continued hints of citrus and aromatic wood.
notes: Monserrate is produced by a community of forty-two family farms near the town of La Plata in Colombia's Huila Department. These farmers organized several years ago into the Associative Group of Producers of the New Millennium and have been expanding their numbers since. Coava is a Portland based coffee roaster that aims to provide quality coffee and the knowledge needed to properly brew that coffee. Visit www.coavacoffee.com or call 503-894-8134 for more information.

title: Colombia Monserrate Huila
blind_assessment: Soft and balanced in the aroma with toasty notes of caramel, milk chocolate and nut. Rich acidity, silky mouthfeel and flavors that balance the sweet milk chocolate and nut complex with a softly tart, citrus-infused cocoa. Not a long finish, but a sweet one.
notes: Monserrate is produced by a community of 42 family farms near the town of La Plata in Huila Department. These farmers organized several years ago into the Associative Group of Producers of the New Millennium and have been expanding their numbers since. With two coffee houses located in California's state capitol Sacramento, Temple Coffee recently transitioned from serving coffee roasted by others to roasting its own. Visit www.templecoffee.com or call 916-601-5363 for more information.

title: Colombia Monserrate
blind_assessment: Soft but complex aroma, suggesting milk chocolate, caramel, nut, aromatic wood. Vivid fruit-toned acidity; a distinct orangy citrus brightens the soft chocolate and caramel tendencies of the aroma. Rich, flavor-saturated, rather dry finish.
notes: Monserrate is produced by a community of 42 family farms near the town of La Plata in Huila Department. These farmers organized several years ago into the Associative Group of Producers of the New Millennium and have been expanding their numbers since. Coava is a Portland based coffee roaster that aims to provide quality coffee and the knowledge needed to properly brew that coffee. Visit www.coavacoffee.com or call 503-894-8134 for more information.

title: Colombia Monteblanco Coconut Lemonade
blind_assessment: Refreshingly bright, citrusy-sweet. Tangerine, lychee, ginger blossom, agave syrup, cedar in aroma and cup. High-toned, citrusy acidity; crisp, satiny mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to notes of tangerine and cedar with hints of ginger blossom.
notes: Produced by Rodrigo Sanchez Valencia of Finca Monteblanco, entirely of the Purple Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method with the addition of coconut and citrus fruit to the conventional fermentation step. SÖT Coffee Roaster, based in Osaka, Japan, is a self-described Swedish-style roaster with an “aggressively light” roasting style. For more information, visit www.sotcoffee.com.
bottom_line: Vibrant and juicy-bright, this Colombia Purple Caturra was co-fermented with coconut and citrus fruits to wonderfully tropical effect.

title: Colombia Monteblanco Geisha
blind_assessment: Delicate, high-toned, complex. Guava, cocoa nib, narcissus, sandalwood, hazelnut butter in aroma and cup. Sweet-tart structure with bright, juicy acidity; very smooth, syrupy mouthfeel. Resonant finish consolidates to attractive notes of guava and cocoa nib.
notes: Produced by Rodrigo Sanchez of Monteblanco Farm entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica and processed by a proprietary cold-fermentation process. Merge is a specialty coffee roaster in Harrisonburg, Virginia dedicated to ethical sourcing of high-quality coffees. Visit www.mergecoffeeco.com for more information.
bottom_line: A nuanced, elegant Colombia Geisha with notes of tropical fruit, spice-toned florals and rich cocoa nib.

title: Colombia Monteblanco Gesha Cold Fermentation
blind_assessment: Richly sweet-savory. Black tea, dried lavender, baking chocolate, fresh peach, fresh sugarcane in aroma and cup. Sweet-tart-savory structure with rich, vibrant acidity; plump, syrupy mouthfeel. The gentle finish centers around savory notes of black tea with sugarcane and a hint of lavender.
notes: Produced by Rodrigo Sanchez Valencia at Finca Monteblanco entirely of the celebrated Gesha (also spelled Geisha) variety of Arabica and processed by a cold fermentation method. High-sugar ripe coffee fruit is fermented in refrigerated tanks for three days before drying. Old Soul is a roastery, bakery and crafter of artisanal goods dedicated to quality in every form. Visit www.oldsoulco.com or call 916-443-7685 for more information.
bottom_line: Deeply sweet in structure with savory undertones and intriguing, original aromatics centered on brisk, bittersweet flowers.

title: Colombia Monteblanco Nectar Citrullus Secret Stash
blind_assessment: Exceptionally sweet, gently tart. Passionfruit, honeydew melon, baking chocolate, bergamot, myrrh in aroma and cup. Crisp, mild acidity; plush, creamy mouthfeel. Long, resonant, lingering, complex finish.
notes: Produced by Rodrigo Sanchez and Claudia Samboni of Finca Monteblanco, from trees of the Caturra and Bourbon varieties of Arabica, and processed by the washed method with the addition of Citrullus fruit (melon of various types) to the fermentation. Old Soul is a roastery, bakery, and crafter of artisanal goods dedicated to quality in every form. Visit www.oldsoulco.com or call 916-443-7685 for more information.
bottom_line: This uniquely composed co-fermented Colombia displays a melony sweetness supported by baking chocolate and tropical fruit.

title: Colombia Monteblanco Purple Caturra Natural
blind_assessment: Sweet, nut-toned. Pistachio, lilac, dried lemon zest, very ripe papaya, cedar in aroma and cup. Roundly sweet-tart in structure; delicately plump in mouthfeel. Nut and floral notes carry a quietly satisfying finish.
notes: Produced by Rodrigo Sanchez Valencia on Finca Monteblanco from trees of the Purple Caturra variety, and processed by the natural method, meaning the beans were dried inside the fruit rather than after the fruit has been removed, as is the case with the wet-processed or “washed” coffees. Old Soul is a roastery, bakery and crafter of artisanal goods dedicated to quality in every form. Visit www.oldsoulco.com or call 916-443-7685 for more information.

title: Colombia Monteblanco Rodrigo Sanchez Carbonic Maceration
blind_assessment: Subtly suave, brightly juicy anaerobic. Rose, strawberry, cocoa, pink lemonade, yogurt in aroma and cup. A juicy floral acidity dominates in structure, deepened by a hint of savory depth. Lightly silky, lively mouthfeel. Strawberry and cocoa give way to flowers in a drying finish.
notes: Produced by Rodrigo Sanchez of Finca Monteblanco from trees of the Caturra and Bourbon varieties of Arabica, and processed by a carbonic maceration method involving two fermentation phases in closed tanks injected with CO2. The first fermentation involves the whole coffee fruit, after which the skins and pulp are removed and the beans are fermented a second time with their skins and juice, after which they are washed and dried. Klatch Coffee is an award-winning small-batch roasting company in the Los Angeles area whose resident barista and trainer, Heather Perry, won both the 2003 and 2007 United States Barista Championships brewing a Klatch Coffee espresso blend. Visit www.klatchroasting.com or call 877-455-2824 for more information.
bottom_line: A light-footed and balanced anaerobic cup, floral without perfumy excess, cleanly fruit-toned and silky in texture.

title: Colombia Nariño
blind_assessment: Crisply sweet, chocolaty. Baking chocolate, raisin, cedar, almond, lily in aroma and cup. Sweet-toned structure with brisk acidity; velvety mouthfeel. Gently drying finish consolidates to notes of chocolate-toned raisin and cedar.
notes: Processed by the washed method using an experimental double fermentation. A 36-hour maceration in the whole fruit is followed by pulping and 60-70 hours of further fermentation. Dragonfly Coffee, named 2019 Micro-Roaster of the Year by Roast magazine, is now based in Henderson, Nevada. Visit www.dragonflycoffeeroasters.com or call 303-579-2154 for more information.
bottom_line: A friendly, accessible (and accessibly priced) Colombia cup with engaging chocolate and raisin notes throughout.

title: Colombia Nariño Aponte Honey
blind_assessment: Savory-leaning, deep-toned. Artichoke blossom, salted caramel, lemon verbena, oak, a hint of musk in aroma and cup. Sweet-savory structure with brisk acidity; syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. The savory finish centers around notes of artichoke blossom and salted caramel.
notes: Produced by members of the indigenous Inga community and processed by the honey method, in which the fruit skin is removed but some mucilage is left on the bean during drying. Founded in 1994, Coffee By Design is a specialty coffee roaster in Portland, Maine that also operates three coffee shops in town, as well as one in Freeport. For more information, visit www.coffeebydesign.com.
bottom_line: Sweet herb and perfumy musk notes complicate this intriguingly savory-toned honey-processed Colombia cup.

title: Colombia Nariño Aponte Single Origin
blind_assessment: Balanced, richly aromatic. Dark chocolate, Bing cherry, hazelnut butter, tangerine, cedar in aroma and cup. Sparkling acidity; crisp, satiny mouthfeel. Chocolaty, nut-toned finish with undertones of Bing cherry.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Mortem Labs is a Norfolk, Virginia roastery that offers small-batch blends and select single-origin coffees. Visit www.mortem-labs.com for more information.
bottom_line: This juicy, balanced, classic washed Colombia is also a bargain at $16.99 a bag — especially nice phosphoric acidity from the volcano terroir it was grown in.

title: Colombia Nariño Decaf
blind_assessment: Crisply chocolaty, deep-toned. Baking chocolate, date, almond, Meyer lemon zest, oak forest in aroma and cup. Briskly sweet acidity; plush, satiny mouthfeel. Baking chocolate and sweet lemon zest carry the agreeable finish.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers, entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Decaffeinated in Colombia using ethyl acetate, a solvent derived from sugarcane. Paradise Roasters specializes in micro-lot Arabica and Robusta coffees from Asia and other emerging origins. Paradise prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 808-498-4048 for more information.
bottom_line: A mighty nice decaf Colombia — chocolaty, very sweet and quite citrusy.

title: Colombia Nariño
blind_assessment: Softly floral and citrus-forward. Lemon blossom, pink grapefruit zest, pear, cocoa nib and honey in aroma and cup. Brisk acidity; light, silky body. Short, elegant finish with citrus-cocoa interplay.
notes: Produced by La Jacoba smallholding farmer association, from trees of the Geisha, Caturra, Colombia and Castillo varieties of Arabica, and processed by the Imported by Ally Coffee. Doma Coffee Roasting specializes in organic and Fair-Trade certified coffees and takes pride in a rigorous program of recycling and environmentally responsible business practices. The Doma slogan is “Coffee/Culture/Meaning.” The Doma slogan is “Coffee/Culture/Meaning.” Visit www.domacoffee.com or call 208-667-1267 for more information.
bottom_line: An approachable Colombia coffee that prioritizes balance over extravagance, delivering gentle florals and citrus clarity in a confident, easy-drinking profile.

title: Colombia Nariño Duende
blind_assessment: Spice-toned, chocolaty. Chocolate-toned malt, date, hazelnut, fresh pipe tobacco, stick cinnamon in aroma and cup. Richly bittersweet in structure; velvety-smooth mouthfeel. The finish is richly chocolate-toned with a hint of cinnamon.
notes: Paradise Roasters specializes in micro-lot Arabica and Robusta coffees from Asia and other emerging origins. The company prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.
bottom_line: Low-toned and deeply rich, reminiscent of Ibarra Mexican chocolate with cinnamon, enveloped in fruit and nut tones.

title: Colombia Narino Excelsio
blind_assessment: Balanced, rich-toned, crisply sweet. Baker’s chocolate, plum, hazelnut, maple syrup, wisteria in aroma and cup. Deeply sweet structure with lively acidity; viscous, lightly syrupy mouthfeel. The richly drying finish is cocoa-laden, with supporting notes of stone fruit and nuts.
notes: This coffee tied for the fourth-highest rating in a cupping of coffees from U.S. Mountain States roasters for Coffee Review’s October 2018 tasting report. From an admired growing region in the southernmost Colombia Department of Nariño. Jackrabbit Java selects the finest coffees from around the world and roasts them in Thermopolis, Wyoming’s mountain air. All Jackrabbit Java coffees are specialty-grade and roasted to order. Visit www.jackrabbitjava.com for more information.
bottom_line: A solid Colombia cup with balanced structure and acidity and engaging, understated fruit and floral tones.

title: Colombia Nariño Fiesta Natural
blind_assessment: Complex, sweetly rich. Blueberry, redwood, grapefruit blossom, roasted cacao nib, faint jasmine in aroma and cup. Tartly sweet, juicy acidity; buoyant, satiny mouthfeel. Blueberry and hazelnut carry the dry though flavor-saturated finish.
notes: From an admired growing region in the southernmost Colombia Department of Nariño. Virtually all Colombias are wet-processed, but this is an atypical dry-processed or “natural” Colombia, meaning the beans were dried inside the fruit rather than after the fruit has been removed, as is the case with wet-processed or “washed” coffees. Modern Times is a well-loved, exuberantly inventive Point Loma, San Diego brewery that has long specialized in coffee-beer crossovers and overlaps. Visit www.moderntimescoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A complex, deeply sweet coffee, nut- and fruit-toned.

title: Colombia Nariño Fiesta
blind_assessment: Unusual, exotic pungency; richly tart, juicy acidity. Notes of violet, white sage, apricot and tobacco in aroma and cup. Lively, lightly syrupy mouthfeel. Crisp, richly drying finish.
notes: From an admired growing region in the southernmost Colombia Department of Nariño. Unusual for a Colombia, a dry-processed or "natural" coffee, meaning the beans were dried inside the fruit rather than after the fruit has been removed, as is the case with wet-processed or "washed" coffees. The WestBean is a San Diego-based roastery founded by two friends with a passion for coffee and a determination to bring their customers the highest quality hand-crafted coffee possible. Visit www.thewestbean.com or call 619-709-3232 for more information.

title: Colombia Nariño Floral Station Geisha Washed
blind_assessment: Refined and luminous. White peach, pink grapefruit zest, magnolia, lemongrass and cocoa nib in aroma and cup. High-toned, crystalline acidity; elegant, lightly syrupy body. Lingering floral-citrus finish with subtle cocoa undertones.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers, entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Imported by Bean Super. Coffeebox is a Taipei-based specialty coffee roaster. Visit shop.coffeebox.tw for more information.
bottom_line: A beautifully restrained washed Geisha that emphasizes clarity and finesse, showcasing floral lift and citrus precision anchored by delicate chocolate notes.

title: Colombia Nariño Lucido Diaz Pink Bourbon
blind_assessment: High-toned, richly sweet. Yellow plum, almond, cocoa nib, lilac, cedar in aroma and cup. Brightly sweet structure with juicy acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. The crisply sweet-tart finish centers around notes of plum and almond.
notes: Produced by Lucido Diaz entirely of the admired Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and flesh are removed before drying). Founded in 1994, Coffee By Design is a specialty coffee roaster in Portland, Maine that also operates three coffee shops in town, as well as one in Freeport. Visit www.coffeebydesign.com.
bottom_line: A balanced, harmonious Colombia Pink Bourbon with notes of stone fruit and almond as throughlines, supported by sweet florals.

title: Colombia Nariño Medium Roast
blind_assessment: Delicately and richly sweet. Orange marmalade, tea rose, fresh-cut fir, cashew in aroma and cup. Round, bittersweet acidity; full, lightly velvety mouthfeel. Fir and plum predominate in the quietly sweet, slightly drying finish.
notes: Purchased as whole bean in a 12-ounce foil bag with one-way degassing valve at a Safeway supermarket in northern California. This sample was roasted and packaged at Mr. Espresso’s Oakland, California facility. Mr. Espresso is a San Francisco Bay Area wholesale roaster and espresso parts distributer that slow-roasts its coffees using traditional wood-fired roasting machines. Visit www.mrespresso.com or call 510-287-5200 for more information.

title: Colombia Nariño Single-Origin Espresso
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Richly chocolaty, deep-toned. Dark chocolate, graham cracker, almond butter, cedar, tangerine zest in aroma and small cup. Very smooth, viscous mouthfeel; crisply chocolaty, nut-toned finish. In cappuccino-scaled milk, dark chocolate is further amplified to an almost dessert-like intensity.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers, from trees of the Castillo and Caturra varieties of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and flesh are removed before beans are dried). Temple Coffee is a quality-focused retail and wholesale specialty roaster active in Sacramento, California since 2005. Committed to sourcing, roasting and brewing the finest coffees, Temple features selections from distinguished single estates and cooperatives around the world. Visit www.templecoffee.com or call 916-454-1282 for more information.
bottom_line: A very chocolaty Colombia roasted for espresso applications, with rich sweetness and aromatic cedar notes in both straight shot and milk.

title: Colombia Narino Sugarcane Decaf
blind_assessment: Caramel-toned, richly wood-framed. Gently scorched fir, dark caramel, lily, raisin, bay leaf in aroma and cup. Briskly sweet-savory acidity; crisp, velvety mouthfeel. Wood-framed finish with caramel undertones.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers and decaffeinated in Colombia using ethyl acetate, a solvent derived from sugar cane. Side By Each Brewing Co. is a specialty roaster, craft brewery, kitchen, and community gathering space all under one roof in sunny Auburn, Maine. The company closed permanently in December 2024.
bottom_line: Rich aromatic wood notes carry this crisply caramelly decaf cup with notes of sweet florals and dried fruit.

title: Colombia Narino Supremo
blind_assessment: The roast dominates here, deeply pungent and cedary in the aroma, with floral and Mediterranean herb top notes. Roundly and sweetly roasty in the cup, lightish in body but deep in dimension, with floral top notes and a cedary, herb-toned chocolate. Clean, rich and chocolaty in the short finish, though a burned astringency surfaces in the long, particularly as the cup cools.
notes: This Colombia, purchased at a Starbucks retail outlet, represents a higher grade of Colombia (Supremo) based on bean size than the Starbucks Colombia sold in bags in supermarkets, which consists of the smaller bean Excelso grade. This coffee also boasts some regional pedigree, as it was grown in Narino Department, a particularly respected growing region in southern Colombia. Visit www.starbucks.com for more information.

title: Colombia  Nariño Villa Maria La Chorrera Geisha Washed
blind_assessment: Elegantly sweet, spice-toned. Bergamot, pear butter, cashew, cocoa nib, wisteria in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart with vibrant acidity; very satiny mouthfeel. Cocoa-toned finish has undertones of bergamot and wisteria.
notes: Produced by Keny Adarme of Finca La Chorrera, entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). CoffeeBox Coffee founders Godfrey and Coco focus on small-batch coffee roasting with the goal of making the joy of premium coffee accessible to everyone. Visit shop.coffeebox.tw for more information.
bottom_line: A deep, spice-toned, richly aromatic washed Colombia, vibrant and balanced.

title: Colombia Nariño
blind_assessment: Deeply and richly sweet, quite chocolaty. Dark chocolate, red grape, magnolia, maple syrup, oak in aroma and cup. Sweet-toned structure with bright, lively acidity; smooth, velvety mouthfeel. The pleasing finish consolidates to notes of dark chocolate and magnolia.
notes: From an admired growing region in the southernmost Colombia Department of Nariño and comprised of the Castillo, Caturra and Colombia varieties of Arabica; processed by the wet, or washed method. Revel Coffee is a micro-roaster located in Billings, Montana. Its motto: “Quality is paramount – a difference you can revel in.” Visit www.revelcoffee.com or call 406-534-9621 for more information.
bottom_line: A balanced, chocolaty Colombia cup with especially engaging, high-toned acidity.

title: Colombia Nativo Nogales
blind_assessment: Deep-toned, fruit-forward and richly sweet. Black cherry, red plum, bittersweet chocolate, molasses and cardamom in aroma and cup. Briskly sweet acidity; full, creamy-smooth mouthfeel. The finish is sweet and persistent, with black cherry, bittersweet chocolate and cardamom notes.
notes: Produced by Oscar Fernando Hernandez and processed by the anaerobic natural method, in which the whole fruit is fermented in tanks with limited oxygen before drying, also in the whole fruit.. The Westside Coffee Company is a Utah-based specialty coffee roaster and cafe. Visit www.thewestsidecoffeecompany.com for more information.
bottom_line: A full-bodied anaerobic natural Colombia that layers ripe fruit and crisp chocolate with a molasses sweetness and alluring aromatic spice.

title: Colombia Natural Huila Eulises Guzman
blind_assessment: Deeply sweet-tart, fruit-toned and floral. Dried plum, freesia, lemon verbena, tamarind, cedar in aroma and cup. Gently bright, winey acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to notes of dried plum and freesia.
notes: Produced by Eulises Guzman of Finca La Lomita, entirely of the Colombia variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Kakalove Café is a nano-roaster located in the small city of Chia-Yi in Taiwan that strives to procure and roast the finest quality coffee. Visit www.kakalovecafe.com.tw or email kahiyuho@gmail.com for more information.
bottom_line: A lovely natural-processed single-variety Colombia that commingles dried stone fruit and spicy floral notes with a sweet herb throughline.

title: Colombia Nestor Lasso El Diviso Chiroso
blind_assessment: Delicately fruit-forward, resonantly tart. Pomegranate, lime zest, vanilla kefir, baking chocolate, cedar in aroma and cup. Briskly sweet acidity; full, satiny-smooth mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to notes of pomegranate, kefir and cedar.
notes: Produced by Nestor Lasso of Finca El Diviso, from trees of the Caturra and Chiroso varieties of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic method, in which the whole fruit is fermented in tanks with limited oxygen before drying, also in the whole fruit. Achilles Coffee Roasters is a San Diego-based specialty roaster. Visit www.achillescoffeeroasters.com for more information.
bottom_line: A fruity-tart anaerobic natural Colombia that gets ballast from notes of baking chocolate and rich aromatic cedar.

title: Colombia Nestor Lasso El Diviso DF Caturra
blind_assessment: Intensely aromatic, intricately layered. Blood orange, red currant, hibiscus, panela and cocoa nib in aroma and cup. Bright, wine-toned acidity; plush, syrupy body. The finish is long and resonant, echoing citrus zest, dark berry, and sweet ferment undertones.
notes: Produced by Nestor Lasso of Finca El Diviso, entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic washed method, with the addition of mossto from a previous fermentation to the current batch. Coffee Cycle Roasting is a San Diego-based specialty roaster founded by cycling enthusiasts. Visit www.coffeecycleroasting.com for more information.
bottom_line: A boldly expressive, fermentation-driven Caturra that delivers vivid fruit complexity and transparent structure while maintaining impressive clarity and balance.

blind_assessment: Opulent, fruit-saturated, vibrant. Passionfruit, raspberry liqueur, star jasmine, dark chocolate, and sugarcane in aroma and cup. Sparkling, sweet-tart acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. The finish is long and resonant, carrying berry and floral sweetness with a grounding chocolate depth.

Produced by Nestor Lasso and Jhoan Vergara at Peñas Blancas Coffee Mill, entirely of the Java variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). bottom_line: A spectacular natural-processed Colombia Java: exuberant fruit and floral aromatics supported by rich chocolate and sugarcane sweetness — a cup that dazzles with both intensity and finesse.

title: Colombia Nestor Lasso Sidra
blind_assessment: Sweet, tangy, high-toned. Intense star jasmine, tangerine, passionfruit, cocoa nib, sandalwood in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart in structure with a savory edge; satiny mouthfeel. Long, sandalwood-toned finish.
notes: Produced by brothers Nestor and Adrian Lasso of Finca El Diviso, entirely of the Sidra variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Sidra is an Ethiopian variety of coffee that at some unknown point in its history was selected and brought to Ecuador, then to nearby Colombia. Chromatic Coffee prides itself in doing everything in-house and meticulously, from printing its attractive bags to modifying equipment to sourcing and roasting its fine coffees. bottom_line: A very sweet, flower-driven cup, smoothly bright and intricate with nuance.

title: Colombia Ombligon Red Dragon Washed Thermo-Shock
blind_assessment: Intensely aromatic, fruit-saturated and complex. Red currant, blood orange, black cherry, rose and dark chocolate in aroma and cup. Vibrant, juicy acidity; plush, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. The finish is exceptionally long and resonant, with lingering red currant, rose and dark chocolate notes.

title: Colombia Organic
blind_assessment: Crisp and gently tart. Cocoa, ripe plum, flowers, and a hint of pungent fresh-cut fir in aroma and cup. Rich, forward acidity; lightly syrupy mouthfeel. Balanced, gently flavor-saturated finish.

Although a logo for "FairTradeProof.org" appears on the label, the absence of the trademarked Fair Trade seal indicates this coffee is not certified by Fair Trade USA. title: Colombia Osmanthus Bouquet Granja Paraiso 92
blind_assessment: Big, round, very sweet anaerobic, intensely floral. Lilac, lavender, strawberry yogurt, roasted macadamia, a hint of musk in aroma and cup. Candy-like sweetness dominates in the structure, balanced by lactic tang and a savory bottom. Buoyantly syrupy mouthfeel. Complex flowers and nut notes dominate in a continuing sweet but savory-edged finish.
notes: Produced by Wilton Benitez of Finca El Paraíso entirely of the rare Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by a complexly detailed version of the double-anaerobic method (sealed-tank fermentation of the whole fruit with the addition of brewer’s yeast, removal of skin and pulp, and a second fermentation of the beans shut in the tank with the removed skin and pulp). Additional processing nuance includes a thermal shock wash (soaking the whole fruit in hot water for 30 seconds, then cold water for 30 seconds) to reduce astringency. Prism Coffee Works is a specialty roaster, cafe and barista training center based in Seoul, South Korea. Visit www.instagram.com/prismcoffeeworks for more information.
bottom_line: A delightful flower bomb of a coffee, with a savory nut-like edge and an inherent balance that saves it from sentimentality.

title: Colombia Pablo Zuniga Micro Lot
blind_assessment: Tart and rather savory. Grape, prune, lemon, cocoa in aroma and cup. Quiet but assertive acidity; syrupy mouthfeel. Rich, tart, rather simple finish.
notes: Grown and processed at Finca Santa Marta by Pablo Zuniga, this coffee is Rainforest Alliance Certified, meaning it was produced following sustainable ecological and socio-economic criteria developed by the Sustainable Agricultural Network, a coalition of independent, environment-focused non-governmental organizations. Olympia Coffee Roasting is a small-batch wholesale and retail roasting company with a youthful, no-nonsense style and a commitment to high quality organic coffees. Visit www.olympiacoffeeroasting. or call 360-753-0066 for more information.

title: Colombia Pacamara Natural
blind_assessment: Crisply fruity, cocoa-toned. Baking chocolate, pink grapefruit, lychee, fresh-cut fir, almond in aroma and cup. Briskly sweet-tart acidity; lightly satiny mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to notes of pink grapefruit and baking chocolate.

title: Colombia Pacamara
blind_assessment: Citrus-toned, sweetly herbal. Meyer lemon, lavender, panela, thyme, cocoa nib in aroma and cup. Juicy-sweet structure with brisk acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Finish centers on sweet lemon and cocoa nib notes.
notes: Produced by five smallholding farmers, entirely of the Pacamara variety of Arabica, and processed bt the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Rusty Dog Coffee is a Madison, Wisconsin-based specialty coffee roaster. Visit www.rustydogcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A refined washed Colombia, this double-fermented Pacamara showcases clarity and balance with bright citrus notes and a savory-sweet depth.

title: Colombia Papayo
blind_assessment: Balanced, brightly sweet-tart. White peach, watermelon candy, agave syrup, pink grapefruit zest, lilac in aroma and cup. Floral-toned acidity; very silky-smooth mouthfeel. Lilac and watermelon notes carry the easygoing finish.

Mostra Coffee is a women-, minority-, veteran-, and immigrant-owned micro-roaster based in north county San Diego. For more information, visit www.mostracoffee.com.

title: Colombia Paraiso 92 Double Anaerobic
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Sweet grapefruit and orange blossom notes shimmer inside a deeply expressed chocolate in aroma and cup. Velvety mouthfeel. Ken and co-taster John DiRuocco shared parallel descriptors and the same 95-point enthusiasm for this poised, resonantly finishing espresso. Floral-toned chocolate with a continued grapefruit hint graces three parts milk.
notes: Produced by Wilton Benitez entirely of the Colombia variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic kōji method, in which the coffee fruit is first sterilized and then fermented in a bio-reactor and inoculated with a selection of Japanese kōji (Aspergillus oryzae). This mold species breaks down starch into simple sugars and is commonly used in the production of soy sauce, miso, sake and shōchū. After this whole-fruit fermentation, skin and pulp are removed and the coffee is subjected to a second anaerobic fermentation. A bean-sealing process follows, carried out through successive impacts of hot and cold water, before the beans are dried by machine for 46 hours. Imported to Taiwan by Pebble Coffee. ​​Bargain Cafe is a specialty coffee roaster in Taitung, Taiwan. Visit www.bargain-cafe.com for more information.
bottom_line: Chocolate is deep, nuanced and alive with sweet citrus and flowers in this espresso co-taster John DiRuocco called “elegant, round yet complex.”

title: Colombia Paraiso 92 Geisha Double Anaerobic
blind_assessment: Nuanced, multi-layered fruit-forward. Bergamot, apricot nectar, star jasmine, lemon balm, sandalwood in aroma and cup. Complex, juicy acidity; full, syrupy mouthfeel. Long-lasting finish that carries over all the flavor notes from the cup.
notes: Produced by Wilton Benitez entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica. Processed by the kōji method, in which the coffee fruit is first sterilized and then fermented in a bio-reactor and inoculated with a selection of Japanese kōji (Aspergillus oryzae). This mold species breaks down starch into simple sugars and is commonly used in the production of soy sauce, miso, sake and shōchū. After whole-fruit fermentation, the coffee is pulped and subjected to a second fermentation phase. A bean-sealing process follows, carried out through impacts of hot and cold water, before the beans are dried by machine for 46 hours. Bargain Cafe is a specialty coffee roaster in Taitung, Taiwan. Visit shopee.tw/iamjiter for more information.
bottom_line: Resonant, deep-toned, multi-layered, this experimentally processed Colombia Geisha delivers pungent aromatics and complexity throughout the cup.

title: Colombia Patio Bonita
blind_assessment: Richly cocoa-toned, citrusy. Tangerine, dark chocolate, pecan, marjoram, narcissus in aroma and cup. Gently bright acidity; crisp, creamy mouthfeel. Chocolaty finish with undertones of tangerine and pecan.
notes: Produced by Carlos and Paola Arturo Trujillo, a father-daughter team, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Big Shoulders Coffee is a Chicago artisan roaster that emphasizes a fresh-roasted, no-nonsense approach to fine coffee. Visit www.bigshoulderscoffee.com or call 312-846-1439 for more information.
bottom_line: A complex, multi-layered washed Colombia driven by chocolate and citrus notes in harmonious balance.

title: Colombia Peñas Blancas Java Natural
blind_assessment: Tropical, high-toned. Star jasmine, passionfruit, clove, pink peppercorn, cocoa nib in aroma and cup. Bright, juicy, layered acidity; buoyantly silky mouthfeel. Complex, expressive finish with passionfruit and cocoa nib notes front and center, complicated by a sweet clove throughline.
notes: Produced by Nestor Lasso and Jhoan Vergara at Peñas Blancas Coffee Mill, entirely of the Java variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). title: Colombia Peñas Blancas Natural Process
blind_assessment: Exuberant, fruit-forward, and lushly textured. Strawberry jam, lemon verbena, cocoa nib, wisteria and sandalwood in aroma and cup. Round, juicy mouthfeel with a soft malic acidity that lifts rather than cuts. The finish is long and sugary, with dried strawberry and wisteria lingering into the long.
notes: Produced by Nestor Lasso and Jhoan Vergara of Peñas Blancas Coffee Mill, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Achilles Coffee Roasters is a San Diego-based specialty roaster. Visit www.achillescoffeeroasters.com for more information.
bottom_line: A generous and richly expressive natural from Huila that channels the experimental processing expertise of Peñas Blancas into a cup defined by berry intensity, winey depth, and a disarming sweetness — indulgent in character yet clean and well-structured throughout.

title: Colombia Piendamo Meseta de Popayan
blind_assessment: Crisp, delicate. Sweet cocoa, fresh-cut fir and complexly layered, gently tart fruit in aroma and cup. Sweet-toned, bright acidity; lightly syrupy mouthfeel. Balanced, delicately rich finish.
notes: Mtn. Air Roasting is a micro-roaster of single origin specialty coffees based in Asheville, North Carolina. Visit www.mtnairroasting.com or call 828-423-0321 for more information.

title: Colombia Piendamo Regional Select
blind_assessment: Sweetly pungent, complex, original. Cherry-like fruit, brown sugar, roasted cacao nib, hints of clove and vanilla in aroma and cup. Crisp, lightly juicy acidity; light, silky mouthfeel. The cacao nib and spice in particular carry into a gently drying but sweet-toned finish.
notes: Bean Fruit is a quality-oriented small-batch roaster based in Jackson, Mississippi, whose motto is a Biblical quotation from Galatians 5:22-23: “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, long suffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.” Visit www.beanfruit.com or call 601-624-2605 for more information.

roaster: Lin Jen Wei’s Black Jar Coffee
title: Colombia Pink Bourbon
blind_assessment: Crisply sweet, delicately tart. Pomegranate, grapefruit zest, magnolia, elm, maple syrup in aroma and cup. Sweet-tart structure with brisk acidity; satiny-smooth mouthfeel. Rich-toned finish with notes of pomegranate and magnolia in the short and maple syrup in the long.
notes: Produced entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica and processed by the wet, or washed, method. FFor more information, visit Black Jar's Facebook page.

title: Colombia Pink Bourbon
blind_assessment: Complex, nuanced, high-toned. Wild raspberry, honeysuckle, cocoa nib, tangerine zest, honey in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart with juicy-bright acidity; full, satiny-smooth mouthfeel. The inviting finish leads with notes of cocoa nib and honey.
notes: Produced by Carlos Ramon Diaz of Finca La Esperanza entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and flesh are removed from the beans before they are dried). Paradise prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.
bottom_line: A focused, complex Colombia Pink Bourbon with top notes of wild berry and cocoa nib and a throughline of spicy-sweet florals and citrus zest.

title: Colombia Pink Bourbon
blind_assessment: Richly chocolaty, deeply sweet. Dark chocolate, almond butter, peach, cedar, magnolia in aroma and cup. Sweet-toned structure with balanced acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Chocolaty and nut-toned finish.

bottom_line: An inviting floral-toned Colombia cup with sweet chocolate notes, rich nuttiness, and classic Colombia balance.
coffee_origin: Sur de Huila, Huila Department, Colombia

title: Colombia Pink Bourbon
blind_assessment: Wildly tropical, fruity and deep. Passion fruit, mango, tamarind, rice candy, hop flowers in aroma and cup. Richly bittersweet structure with juicy acidity; plushly syrupy mouthfeel. Long, lingering, fruity finish.
notes: Produced by Wilton Benitez entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica and processed by a proprietary anaerobic fermentation method in which ​​the coffee fruit is first sterilized, then fermented anaerobically in the whole fruit with added microorganisms for 36 hours. After this fermentation in the whole fruit, the coffee is subjected to thermal shock (first a high temperature to swell the beans and allow the unique flavors and aromas from the initial anaerobic yeast fermentation to penetrate the seeds, then a cold temperature to constrict the beans and lock in those flavors and aromas). Finally, the whole cherries are carefully dried by machine until the beans reach 10.5% internal humidity. title: Colombia Pink Bourbon El Corazon
blind_assessment: Rich-toned, deeply floral. Honeysuckle, nectarine, pink peppercorn, oak, Meyer lemon zest in aroma and cup. Vibrantly sweet-tart structure with juicy acidity; crisp, satiny mouthfeel. Spice-toned finish with pretty floral and citrus notes.

bottom_line: An inviting, nuanced Colombia Pink Bourbon cup: richly chocolaty with spicy floral and sweet fruit notes throughout.

title: Colombia Pink Bourbon Filadelfia
