blind_assessment: Intricate, vibrantly floral, citrusy. Lilac, tangerine, almond brittle, sage, wild honey in aroma and cup. High-toned, harmonious structure with elegantly juicy acidity; full, creamy mouthfeel. Flavor-saturated, very long finish.
notes: Produced by Fabian Rodriquez of Finca Filadelfia entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and flesh are removed from the beans before they are dried). Bird Rock Coffee Roasters is a retailer and wholesaler focused on organic and socially responsible coffees; it was awarded the “2012 Micro-Roaster of the Year” title by Roast Magazine. Visit www.birdrockcoffee.com or call 858-551-1707 for more information.
bottom_line: A classically complete Colombia Pink Bourbon cup crisply focused around complex floral, citrus, and delicately sweet herb notes.

title: Colombia Pink Bourbon Finca El Chaparote
blind_assessment: Elegantly floral, delicately fruit-toned. Honeysuckle, pink grapefruit zest, agave syrup, cocoa nib, lemon balm in aroma and cup. Richly sweet structure with bright, balanced acidity; lyrically silky mouthfeel. Pretty floral-leaning finish centers on notes of honeysuckle and lemon balm with undertones of cocoa nib.
notes: Produced by Erick Fernando Bravo Urbano of Finca El Chapapote entirely of the admired Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica and processed by the washed method. Paradise Roasters specializes in micro-lot Arabica and Robusta coffees from Asia and other emerging origins. The company prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.
bottom_line: An integrated, harmonious Pink Bourbon from Colombia with high-toned floral and fruit notes throughout — richly aromatic, juicy and bright.

title: Colombia Pink Bourbon Honey
blind_assessment: Bright, juicy, high-toned. Guava, almond butter, wild honey, tangerine zest, narcissus-like flowers in aroma and cup. Richly sweet, elegantly tart structure with high-toned, vibrant acidity; very full, syrupy mouthfeel. The long, lingering, flavor-saturated finish carries forward all the notes from the cup.
notes: Produced by Wilfredo Trujillo Mota of Finca Los Alpes entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica and processed by the honey method. Bird Rock Coffee Roasters is a retailer and wholesaler focused on organic and socially responsible coffees; it was awarded the “2012 Micro-Roaster of the Year” title by Roast Magazine. Visit www.birdrockcoffee.com or call 858-551-1707 for more information.
bottom_line: A lush, balanced, juicy-sweet Pink Bourbon from Colombia, lyrical in its balance and elegance.

title: Colombia Pink Bourbon Honey
blind_assessment: Floral and sweetly spice-toned. Jasmine, pink peppercorn, apricot, baking chocolate, fresh-cut oak in aroma and cup. Sweet-savory structure with balanced, bright acidity; satiny-smooth mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to notes of apricot and baking chocolate with hints of jasmine at the top and oak underneath.
notes: Produced by Wilfredo Trujillo Mota of Los Alpes Farm, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica and processed by the honey method, in which some fruit flesh (“honey”) is allowed to adhere to the beans during drying. Bird Rock Coffee Roasters is a retailer and wholesaler focused on organic and socially responsible coffees; it was awarded the “2012 Micro-Roaster of the Year” title by Roast Magazine. Visit www.birdrockcoffee.com or call 858-551-1707 for more information.
bottom_line: A deeply sweet, balanced Colombia cup characterized by rich floral and spice tones throughout, with an especially lively acidity.

title: Colombia Pink Bourbon Natural
blind_assessment: Spice-toned, very nuanced. Pomegranate, ginger, wisteria, bay leaf, cocoa nib in aroma and cup. High-toned acidity; silky mouthfeel. Spice-toned finish with notes of ginger and bay leaf.
notes: Produced by Delfin Carvajal and his six brothers of Finca El Corozal, entirely of the Colombia Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Paradise prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.
bottom_line: Aromatically driven by notes of warming spices and richly sweet-tart in the cup, this Colombia Pink Bourbon is multi-layered and bright.

title: Colombia Pink Bourbon/Pink Lemonade Collaboration
blind_assessment: Sweetly tart, floral-driven. Honeysuckle, vanilla bean, cocoa nib, peach, fresh-cut oak in aroma and cup. Crisply sweet structure with gently bright, ripe acidity; very full, viscous mouthfeel. The finish consolidates to notes of peach, vanilla bean and oak.
notes: Produced by Jose Ortiz of Finca El Danubio from trees of the Tabi and Pink Bourbon varieties of Arabica and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and flesh are removed before drying). Badbeard's Microroastery is a Portland, Oregon-based small-batch roaster focused on quality and freshness. Badbeard's encourages its customers to "make great coffee at home."For each bag sold, Badbeard's donates over $5 to Pink Lemonade Project, a non-profit organization dedicated to serving those affected by breast cancer in the Portland, Oregon and Vancouver, Washington metro area. Visit www.badbeardscoffee.com or call 503-232-7327 for more information.
bottom_line: A crisp, delicate yet confident Colombia cup — classically sweet and cocoa-toned with juicy acidity.

title: Colombia Pink Bourbon
blind_assessment: Elegant, tropical, rich-toned. Strawberry guava, honeysuckle, almond, sandalwood, cacao nib in aroma and cup. Richly sweet structure with bright, vibrant acidity; lush, syrupy mouthfeel. Lingering notes of strawberry and honeysuckle in the delicate finish.
notes: Produced by Angel Ortega and Irma Blancos (both members of the San Agustin Cooperative) entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica and processed by the wet or washed method. Paradise Roasters specializes in micro-lot Arabica and Robusta coffees from Asia and other emerging origins. The company prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.
bottom_line: A beautiful fruit- and floral-toned Colombia cup with undertones of rich chocolate and resonant sandalwood.

title: Colombia Pink Champagne El Mirador Blend
blind_assessment: Delicately fruit-forward, richly floral-toned. Wild raspberry, cocoa nib, narcissus, tangerine, amber in aroma and cup. Bright, juicy acidity; crisp, velvety mouthfeel. Exceptionally long, resonant, cohesive finish that maintains the harmony of the cup.
notes: Produced at Finca El Mirador, from trees of the Caturra and Catiope varieties of Arabica, and processed by the carbonic maceration method, which involves fermenting the whole fruit in a sealed container that has been flushed with CO2, and drying in the whole fruit. Old World Coffee Roasters is a specialty coffee roaster with cafes in Reno and Carson City, Nevada. Visit OldWorldCoffeeRoasters.com for more information.
bottom_line: A deeply aromatic, integrated, berry- and floral-toned Colombia carbonic maceration with high-toned acidity and a very long, satisfying finish.

title: Colombia Pitalito Estate
blind_assessment: A classically lyric coffee. The aroma is intense and enveloping, with spicy ripe tomato, bittersweet chocolate, caramel, and banana-like fruit notes. The ripe tomato and dark chocolate notes carry into a cup shimmering with sweet, wine-toned acidity and the unusual banana-like fruit notes, which even seem reflected in the pleasant viscosity of the mouthfeel.
notes: Pitalito comes from a highly respected growing area east of the Andes in the southern Colombian Department of Huila. The term "Estate" may be a bit of a misnomer, as it appears that this coffee comes from a community of small-holding growers, growers who have benefited from a long-term, supportive relationship with The Roasterie. The Roasterie is a leading, quality-oriented specialty roaster that specializes in building ongoing relationships with growers and that emphasizes its commitment to "air roasting," a technology utilizing a column of hot air rather than the conventional turning drum to agitate the roasting beans. Visit www.theroasterie.com or call 800-376-0245 for more information.
coffee_origin: San Augustin growing region, Huila Department, southern Colombia

title: Colombia Planadas Ibague
blind_assessment: Sweetly savory, fruit-driven. Candy apple, lime zest, baking chocolate, cedar, narcissus in aroma and cup. Bittersweet structure with brisk acidity; crisp, satiny mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to notes of chocolate and citrus.
notes: Comprised entirely of the rare Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica and processed by the anaerobic natural method, in which fermentation of the whole fruit occurs in a hermetically sealed vessel. Jaunt Coffee Roasters is a San Diego-based roaster and café with an extensive coffee and food menu. Visit www.jauntcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: An invitingly bittersweet Colombia Pink Bourbon processed by the anaerobic natural method: chocolaty and citrusy with floral undertones.

title: Colombia Planadas Tolima
blind_assessment: Delicate, richly aromatic. Pineapple, almond nougat, magnolia, myrrh, bergamot in aroma and cup. Richly bittersweet structure with high-toned acidity; smooth, syrupy mouthfeel. Gentle, crisply sweet finish with notes of almond and myrrh.
notes: Produced by Jorge Elias Rojas entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the honey method, in which the skins are removed from the fruit but some of the fruit flesh (mucilage) is allowed to dry on the beans. Jaunt Coffee Roasters is a San Diego-based roaster and café with an extensive coffee and food menu. Visit www.jauntcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A lovely Colombia Geisha cup, finely tea-like in its aromatic delicacy.

title: Colombia Planadas Tolima
blind_assessment: Crisply sweet-savory, deep-toned. Concord grape, baking spices, dark chocolate, tea rose, the scent of balsa wood in aroma and cup. Sweet structure with brisk acidity; very full, viscous mouthfeel. Crisp, sweetly wood-framed finish with undertones of baking spices.
notes: Produced by Jorge Elias Rojas Vasquez entirely of the Yellow Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Jaunt Coffee Roasters is a San Diego-based roaster and café with an extensive coffee and food menu. Visit www.jauntcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A rich, fruit- and fragrant wood-framed natural-processed Colombia cup.

title: Colombia Planadas
blind_assessment: Chocolaty and sweetly nut-toned. Baking chocolate, almond butter, nougat, lychee, lily in aroma and cup. Sweet structure with gentle, round acidity; velvety-smooth mouthfeel. Crisp, chocolaty finish with undertones of almond and lily.
notes: Produced by members of the Asociación de Cafés Diferenciados Brisas Nevado de la Vereda el Mirador Cadibrine from trees of the Caturra, Castillo, Colombia and Typica varieties of Arabica and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp are removed before drying). SkyTop Coffee is a USDA certified-organic specialty coffee roaster based in Manlius, New York. For more information, visit skytopcoffee.com.
bottom_line: A balanced, easygoing Colombia cup: chocolaty, nutty, and deeply sweet.

title: Colombia Pomelo Jin Xuan Tea (espresso)
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. High-toned, sweetly tart. Pomegranate, tangerine, dark chocolate, myrrh, cedar in aroma and small cup. Viscous, syrupy body; crisply sweet-savory finish. In three parts milk, a pretty floral note akin to orange blossom emerges alongside cedar.
notes: Produced by Yesid Castañeda of Finca Las Delicias, from trees of the Pink Bourbon and Typica varieties of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic method (fermented in an oxygen-free environment, then dried in the whole fruit). Bargain Cafe is a specialty coffee roaster in Taitung, Taiwan. Visit www.bargain-cafe.com for more information.
bottom_line: A complex, rich-toned Colombia anaerobic, bold in the straight shot and cedary and floral in cappuccino-scaled milk.

title: Colombia Pomelo Jin Xuan Tea
blind_assessment: Delicately aromatic, confidently complex. Pink grapefruit, cocoa nib, amber, apricot, graphite in aroma and cup. Bright, balanced acidity; vibrant, silky-smooth mouthfeel. Cocoa-toned, citrusy finish with amber notes underneath.
notes: Produced at Finca Las Delicias, from trees of the Pink Bourbon and Typica varieties of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic method (fermented in an oxygen-free environment, then dried in the whole fruit). Bargain Cafe is a specialty coffee roaster in Taitung, Taiwan. Visit www.bargain-cafe.com for more information.
bottom_line: A uniquely composed anaerobic natural cup that’s, at turns, bright-citrusy and savory-resiny.

title: Colombia Pomelo & Taiwanese No. 12 Tea Flavor
blind_assessment: Rich-toned, uniquely composed. Grape candy, lime zest, lemon verbena, oak forest, wild honey in aroma and cup. Balanced, bright acidity; crisp, satiny mouthfeel. Sweet-toned, quietly citrusy finish.
notes: A blend of two coffees: a Colombia fermented with pomelo and a Taiwan fermented with tea. Bargain Cafe is a specialty coffee roaster in Taitung, Taiwan. Visit www.bargain-cafe.com for more information.
bottom_line: A combination of two fermented coffees that makes this profile unlike any other. The Colombia brings candy-like aromas and flavors, and the Taiwan adds a savory richness and complexity.

title: Colombia Primavera COE First Place Winner
blind_assessment: Honey and sweet night flowers balanced by a gently lemony tartness and pungent, fresh-cut cedar. Pronounced but roundly balanced acidity; syrupy mouthfeel. Rich, resonant short finish simplifies very slightly in the long.
notes: The Cup of Excellence is the most esteemed competition for green coffees from a given country of origin; this was the first prize winner from the Colombia 2011 competition chosen by a select group of national and international cuppers. It was produced on Arnulfo Leguizamo’s Primavera farm and is Rainforest Alliance certified, meaning it was produced following sustainable ecological and socio-economic criteria developed by the Sustainable Agricultural Network, a coalition of independent, environment-focused non-governmental organizations. Equator is a specialty roaster based in the San Francisco Bay Area driven by “passion for quality and sustainability.” Visit www.equatorcoffees.com or call 800-809-7687 for more information.
coffee_origin: San Agustín growing region, Huila Department, southern Colombia

title: Colombia Progreso
blind_assessment: Crisply balanced with a shifting, tight-knit complexity. Flowers, nut, fir, and a dark chocolaty fruit in aroma and cup.  The flowers and chocolate carry long into the finish. Gentle acidity, silkily smooth mouthfeel.
notes: Huila is probably the most admired of Colombia coffee growing regions; this small lot was grown by farmer Julio Medina and is made up of the Caturra variety of Arabica. Coava is a Portland based coffee roaster that aims to provide quality coffee and the knowledge needed to properly brew that coffee. Visit www.coavacoffee.com or call 503-894-8134 for more information.

title: Colombia Purple Fruit Anaerobic
blind_assessment: Intense, eccentric anaerobic candy-bomb. Very sweet, intensely fruity and spicy. Bubblegum, musk, raspberry, pistachio, ginger in aroma and cup. Profoundly sweet in structure with a touch of delicately tart acidity. Velvety, lively mouthfeel. In the finish candyish notes fade and musky flowers come forward.
notes: Produced by Sebastián Ramirez of Finca El Placer entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by a proprietary anaerobic method, in which 95% ripe and 5% semi-ripe cherries undergo two phases of fermentation. First, the coffee is fermented in the whole cherry in sealed 200-liter tanks for 120 hours at 18 degrees Celsius, with microorganisms present. Then, skins and pulp are removed, leaving some of the fruit flesh on the beans, which are fermented anaerobically for 72 hours with the addition of CO2. The coffee is then slow-dried for 15 days. Chromatic Coffee prides itself in doing everything in-house and meticulously, from printing its attractive bags to modifying equipment to sourcing and roasting its fine coffees. Visit www.chromaticcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A candy-like sweetness is complicated by a lavish, unpredictable display of eccentric aromatic notes, from bubblegum to ginger to musk.

title: Colombia Quindio Anaerobic Natural
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Brightly fruit-toned, deeply chocolaty, with savory undertones. Rambutan, sandalwood, kumquat, dark chocolate, freesia in aroma and small cup. Crisp, satiny mouthfeel; especially long, flavor-laden finish. In three parts milk, sandalwood notes frame the dark chocolate and tropical fruit throughlines.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers and processed by the natural anaerobic method (whole fruit is fermented in hermetically sealed vessels before drying). Paradise prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.
bottom_line: An unusual espresso profile, this anaerobic Colombia is fruit-forward with spicy floral and deep chocolate notes, especially inviting in the plush, tartly savory straight shot.

title: Colombia Quindio Anaerobic Natural
blind_assessment: Richly fruit and spice-toned. Dried elderberry, clove, agave syrup, marjoram, sandalwood in aroma and cup. Sweet-savory structure with vibrant acidity; syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. The resonant finish leads with notes of elderberry and sandalwood.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers and processed by the natural anaerobic method ((whole fruit is fermented in hermetically sealed vessels before drying). Paradise prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.
bottom_line: A deeply satisfying, savory-sweet Colombia anaerobic with wide-ranging aromatics and dried fruit and warming spices on the palate.

title: Colombia Quindio Campo Hermoso Wush Wush
blind_assessment: Richly chocolaty, fruit-driven. Raspberry jam, baking chocolate, agave syrup, cedar, bay leaf in aroma and cup. Gently bright acidity; plush, creamy mouthfeel. Crisply sweet-tart finish centered around berry and chocolate notes.
notes: Produced by Edwin Noreña of Finca Campo Hermoso, entirely of the Wush Wus variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method, in which the whole fruit is fermented in an oxygen-free environment before drying. Regent strives to deliver coffee with care and purpose. Visit regentcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A fruity, chocolaty Colombia Wush Wush natural with an especially viscous, satiating mouthfeel.

title: Colombia Red Bomb
blind_assessment: Delicately fruit-forward, berry-driven. Mulberry jam, cocoa nib, lemon balm, agave syrup, a hint of wine barrel in aroma and cup. Balanced, sweet-tart structure with citrusy acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Fruit-toned finish consolidates to notes of mulberry and lemon balm.
notes: Produced by the Renancer Project from trees of the Caturra, Castillo and Colombia varieties of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying) with a double ferment step. Founded in 1990, Roadmap CoffeeWorks, formerly Lexington Coffee Roasters, is an award-winning artisan roasting company based in Lexington, Virginia. Roadmap CoffeeWorks focuses on producing fresh, distinctive and sustainable coffees. Visit www.roadmapcoffeeworks.com or call 800-322-6505 for more information.
bottom_line: A quietly fruit-driven washed Colombia with mulberry and lemon throughlines and ballast from cocoa nib, all complicated by a hint of sweet ferment.

title: Colombia Red Bourbon Thermal Shock Natural
blind_assessment: Lush, fruit-saturated and aromatically complex. Red raspberry, nectarine, hibiscus, dark chocolate and candied tangelo in aroma and cup. Vibrant, juicy acidity; plush, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. The finish is long and resonant, with red raspberry, hibiscus and dark chocolate notes lingering into the long.
notes: This coffee earned Finalist recognition in the Experimental category, U.S. division, of the inaugural Kenneth Davids Cup. Produced by Jhoan Vergara of Finca Las Flores, entirely of the Red Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method, with the addition of a thermal shock step (a rapid temperature shift during the fermentation and rinsing stages). Theory Coffee Roasters is a specialty roaster and coffee shop based in Redding, California. Visit www.theorycoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: An expressive thermal-shock Colombia Red Bourbon that layers ripe fruit, sweet florals and chocolate richness into a vivid yet beautifully balanced cup.

title: Colombia Red Fruits Campo Hermosa Edwin Noreña
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Co-taster John DiRuocco (95) was particularly impressed by the lavish sweetness and fruit of this elaborately anaerobic-processed coffee from Colombian processing innovator Edwin Noreña. John found the well-structured and clean-finishing character sufficient to contain and balance the aromatic fireworks. Ken (92), on the other hand, found the sweetness and fruit a bit too intense and candy-like, though he found compensating value in underlying musk and sandalwood tendencies. Both tasters admired the coffee in three parts milk, which rounded and diluted the intensely sweet fruit.
notes: Produced by Edwin Noreña of Finca Campo Hermosa, entirely of the Red Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by a complex version of carbonic maceration. Whole coffee fruit is soaked in water for four hours, then subject to carbonic maceration for 72 hours with coffee must or mossto (juice from compressed coffee fruit). After removal of skins and pulp (pulping), a second carbonic maceration with mossto, red fruits and wine yeast follows, after which the coffee is sun dried for about 25 days. Imported by Yellow Rooster. Royal Flamingo is a Columbus, Ohio-based specialty coffee roaster. Visit www.royalflamingocoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: If you like extravagant fruit grandeur (or if you are a coffee classicist looking for a fling), try this one.

title: Colombia Red Honey Geisha Campo Hermoso
blind_assessment: Elegantly fruit-forward, richly aromatic. Wild strawberry, cocoa nib, lemon verbena, amber, narcissus in aroma and cup. Balanced, juicy acidity; full, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Long, resonant, flavor-saturated finish.
notes: Produced by Edwin Noreña of Finca Campo Hermoso, entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the red honey method, in which much of the fruit flesh is left on the beans during the drying process. Bear Lake Coffee Co., a B Corp-certified coffeehouse and roastery located in Barronett, Wisconsin, is committed to sustainability through its Coffee with a Purpose™ initiative, which ensures that farmers receive compensation well above the Fairtrade Premium for their exceptional small-batch coffee. Visit www.bearlakecoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A high-toned, pretty, complexly aromatic red honey Colombia that leads with berry and cocoa notes with undertones of spicy florals.

title: Colombia Red Sunset
blind_assessment: Sweetly tart, spice-toned. Cocoa nib, Meyer lemon, clove, wild honey, amber in aroma and cup. Briskly sweet, gently tart acidity; satiny-smooth mouthfeel. Long, lingering, resonant integrated finish.
notes: Produced by Andres Cardona of Villa Lucia, from trees of the Colombia and Castillo varieties of Arabica, and processed by the semi-washed (or honey) method, in which some of the fruit flesh is left on the beans during the drying process. Founded in 1990, Roadmap CoffeeWorks, formerly Lexington Coffee Roasters, is an award-winning artisan roasting company based in Lexington, Virginia. Roadmap CoffeeWorks focuses on producing fresh, distinctive and sustainable coffees. Visit www.roadmapcoffeeworks.com or call 800-322-6505 for more information.
bottom_line: This tart-leaning Colombia honey is rife with citrus and warm spice notes and undertones of richly sweet wild honey.

title: Colombia Reserva Del Patron
blind_assessment: Very deep, complex profile that hints as much at Sumatra as it does at Colombia. Intense aroma dominated by earth and ripe, almost overripe fruit notes that together can be read as a dark, raisiny chocolate. Quiet acidity, medium body with syrupy mouthfeel, and continued richly earthy/fruity notes that at moments suggest pungent butterscotch, at other times elegantly cherryish dark chocolate. Lemon hints become more explicit in the sweet finish; a very slight hint of bitter astringency in the long.
notes: Reserva del Patron is a very high-grown and exceptionally rigorously selected green coffee from an admired growing region in the southernmost Colombia Department of Narino. Atomic Cafe is a coffee house on the North Shore of Massachusetts that began its refined in-house roasting program in 2005. Visit www.atomicafe.com or call 978-922-0042 for more information.

title: Colombia Reserva Especial
blind_assessment: Low-toned, rich aroma: molasses, nut, floral topknots. In the cup smooth, deep, simple. The roast-influenced sweet caramel and molasses notes grow crisper under the influence of a gentle acidity, taking on a dark chocolate nuance.
notes: This coffee is certified organically grown and Rainforest Alliance certified, meaning it was produced following sustainable ecological and socio-economic criteria developed by the Sustainable Agricultural Network, a coalition of independent, environment-focused non-governmental organizations. Produced by the Mesa de los Santos farm (www.cafemesadelossantos.com), one of Colombia's most sustainably advanced farms. Bold ! Bean is a small-batch, artisan roaster offering, in its own words, "Single Origin and Artful Blends" to northeast Florida. Visit www.boldbeancoffee.com or call 904-855-1181 for more information.

title: Colombia Rigoberto Herrera Granja La Esperanza Hybrid Washed Gesha
blind_assessment: Lushly aromatic, deeply floral-toned. Wisteria, ginger blossom, nectarine, pink grapefruit, lemon balm in aroma and cup. Delicately bright, confident acidity; exceptionally silky-smooth mouthfeel. Notes of wisteria and ginger blossom harmonize alongside a throughline of nectarine and citrus undertones.
notes: Produced by Rigoberto Herrera of Granja La Esperanza, entirely of the Gesha variety of Arabica, and processed by a proprietary hybrid washed method, in which the whole cherries are fermented in water for 19-22 hours. Then, the fruit is depulped and undergoes a second fermentation begins, this time in parchment and mucilage for 35 hours. Founded in 2013, modcup coffee focuses on fresh roasting and distinctive natural-processed coffees. Visit modcup.com for more information.
bottom_line: Sweet and spice-toned florals are front and center in this experimentally processed Colombia Geisha with gently bright stone fruit, sweet herb, and pretty citrus notes throughout the profile.

title: Colombia Rio Dulce Gesha
blind_assessment: Elegant, floral and fruit-saturated. Notes of pineapple, white peach, honeysuckle, lemon balm and cacao husk in aroma and cup. Bright, crystalline acidity; silky, tea-like body. The finish is long and resonant, carried by pineapple and honeysuckle tones.
notes: A collaboration between Little Waves and Standart, this coffee was produced by José Julián Giraldo of Finca Las Marias, entirely of the Gesha variety of Arabica, and processed by an elaborate proprietary washed method (learn more here). Little Waves Coffee is a Latina-owned, women-forward company that provides livable wages for its diverse team. Visit www.littlewaves.coffee for more information.
bottom_line: A radiant washed Gesha from Quindío — refined, perfumed and gracefully structured, balancing vivid fruit and floral character with a compelling, deeply sweet structure.

title: Colombia Rose Panther
blind_assessment: Intensely aromatic, fruit-saturated and sweetly floral. Aromatic orchid, red currant, lychee, cocoa nib and blood orange in aroma and cup. Gently winey acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. The finish is exceptionally long and perfumed, carrying ripe red fruit, florals and cocoa with impressive integration.
notes: Produced at Finca Esmeralda Negra, entirely of the Sidra variety of Arabica, and processed by a proprietary mosto fermentation and thermal shock method. Intrinsic Coffee Roasters, founded in 2026, is a specialty coffee roaster based in Murrieta, California. Visit www.intrinsicroasters.com for more information.
bottom_line: An expressive Sidra whose elaborate fermentation amplifies its lush fruit and floral character while maintaining balance, sweetness and an especially resonant finish.

title: Colombia San Adolfo Geisha
blind_assessment: Exquisitely floral, crystalline and sweetly layered. White peach, bergamot, frangipani, wild honey and cocoa nib in aroma and cup. Sparkling, high-definition acidity; silky, buoyant body. The finish is exceptionally long and perfumed, layering citrus blossom and stone-fruit sweetness over a floral and cocoa throughline.
notes: Produced by Wilder Lasso of Finca Bella Alejandria, entirely of the Geisha of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Jaunt Coffee Roasters is a San Diego-based roaster and café with an extensive coffee and food menu. Visit www.jauntcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A beautifully realized washed Colombia Geisha that combines floral elegance, radiant citrus clarity and honeyed sweetness in a seamless, deeply expressive cup.

title: Colombia San Adolfo Huila
blind_assessment: Delicate, tropical, cocoa-toned. Cocoa nib, passion fruit, bergamot, amber, wild honey in aroma and cup. Juicy, malic acidity; smooth, very satiny mouthfeel. The finish fulfills the promise of the cup with rich aromatics that linger.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 45 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 50 Coffees of 2025. Produced by Wilder Lasso and Nikolai Furst of Finca El Rubi, entirely of Ethiopia landrace varieties of Arabica they germinated in Colombia. Processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Jaunt Coffee Roasters is a San Diego-based roaster and café with an extensive coffee and food menu. Visit www.jauntcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A Colombia-Ethiopia mashup of the highest order: Sidama varieties germinated in Colombia to produce 3,200 seedlings that became the trees that produced this elegant, enticing cup.

title: Colombia San Adolfo
blind_assessment: Delicately rich, subtly intricate. Violet-like flowers, pink peppercorn, almond butter, peach, myrrh in aroma and cup. Juicy, vibrant, balanced acidity; silky, buoyantly levitating mouthfeel. The crisply sweet, flavor-saturated finish is animated by spicy suggestions of myrrh and pink peppercorn.
notes: Produced entirely from the rare Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, a hybrid of Red and Yellow Bourbon that producers report has some resistance to leaf rust, a devastating disease of the coffee plant. Carefully isolated and cultivated on multiple farms in San Adolfo, this coffee is fully washed — meaning the fruit residue is removed from the beans before drying, a method that typically intensifies acidity and aromatic top notes — and dried in parabolic driers. Established in 2010, Red Rooster is an organic-certified micro-roaster focusing on socially conscious coffee and high-quality coffee. Visit redroostercoffee.com or call 540-745-7338 for more information.
bottom_line: A quietly extravagant coffee: Subtle yet rich, balanced, sweet and spice-toned; an excellent value as well.
coffee_origin: San Adolfo, Acevedo, Huila Department, Colombia

title: Colombia San Agustin
blind_assessment: Richly and roundly tart. The taste of fresh coffee fruit -- think tart cherry -- and pungent grapefruit dominate in aroma and cup, with softening suggestions of cocoa, almond and caramel. Sweet-toned acidity; lightly syrupy mouthfeel. Dry, resonant finish.
notes: This coffee was grown and processed by the fifty members of La Asociación Los Naranjos de San Agustin cooperative. Equator is a specialty roaster based in the San Francisco Bay Area driven by “passion for quality and sustainability.” Visit www.equatorcoffees.com or call 800-809-7687 for more information.

title: Colombia San Agustin
blind_assessment: Deep, pungent, layered. Dark chocolate, molasses, narcissus-like flowers, peach, honeydew melon in aroma and cup. Round, gently rich acidity; lightly syrupy mouthfeel. Flowers and chocolate in particular carry into a long, sweet-toned, flavor-saturated finish.
notes: San Agustín is one of the most admired of Colombia coffee-growing regions. Chromatic prides itself in doing everything in-house and meticulously, from printing its attractive bags to modifying equipment to sourcing and roasting its exceptionally fine coffees. Visit www.chromaticcoffee.com for more information.
coffee_origin: San Agustín growing region, Huila Department, southern Colombia

title: Colombia San Agustin Arnulfo Leguizamo
blind_assessment: Crisply tart black currant and blackberry in aroma and cup, enveloped in floral sweetness and pungent fresh-cut cedar. Round, balanced acidity; syrupy mouthfeel. Impressively rich, deep, complexly flavor-saturated finish.
notes: From trees of the sturdy Caturra variety of Arabica. Processed by the classic wet or “washed” method: fruit is removed before drying using traditional ferment-and-wash methods and the beans are sun-dried. This coffee was grown and processed by the fifty members of La Asociación Los Naranjos de San Agustín cooperative. Beansmith Coffee is a small-batch roasting company located in La Vista, Nebraska that believes that coffee drinkers should know as much as they can about the coffee they drink, and that there is a story behind every cup, one worth exploring. Visit www.beansmith.com or call 866-663-5295 for more information.
coffee_origin: San Agustín growing region, Huila Department, southern Colombia

title: Colombia San Agustin
blind_assessment: Crisp, sweet, pungent. Almond, roasted cacao nib and a brightening hint of tangerine in aroma and cup, with distinct floral notes complicating the aroma. Gently rounded acidity; silky, lively mouthfeel. Flavor fades in a rich though drying finish.
notes: The San Agustín area is one of the most admired of Colombia coffee-growing regions. Mystic Monk Coffee is a small-batch roaster associated with a Carmelite monastery located in the Rocky Mountains of northern Wyoming. Roastmaster Brother Java emphasizes his artisan approach to roasting and his commitment to quality. Visit www.mysticmonkcoffee.com or call 877-751-6377 for more information.
coffee_origin: San Agustín growing region, Huila Department, southern Colombia

title: Colombia San Luís Gesha
blind_assessment: Rich-toned, elegantly sweet. Wild honey, dried apricot, lilac, myrrh, sandalwood in aroma and cup. Sweetly tart structure with juicy, bright acidity; full, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel.The finish consolidates to notes of dried apricot and myrrh with undertones of wild honey.
notes: Produced by Omar Arango Tinoco of Finca San Luís entirely from trees of the Gesha (also spelled Geisha) variety of Arabica and processed by the honey method, in which some fruit flesh (“honey”) is allowed to adhere to the beans during drying. Peach Coffee Roasters is an Atlanta, Georgia-based specialty roaster. Visit peachcoffeeroasters.com for more information.
bottom_line: A delicate, confident honey-processed Colombia Gesha: balanced, bright, floral- and fruit-toned.

title: Colombia San Martin Bourbon Aji Star Fruit Peach Honey
blind_assessment: Richly sweet-savory. Kiwi, cinnamon, white tea, gardenia, dill in aroma and cup. Tangy, juicy acidity; vibrant, silky-smooth acidity. Long-lasting, harmonious, flavor-laden and richly aromatic finish.
notes: Produced at Finca San Martin, entirely of the Bourbon Aji variety of Arabica, and processed by the co-fermented honey method, in which the whole fruit is fermented with starfruit and peaches, and then some of the fruit flesh is left on the beans during the drying process. GK Coffee is a nano-roastery in Yilan, Taiwan, that offers both retail and wholesale coffee. For more information, visit www.gkcoffee.com.tw or email gkcoffee2015@gmail.com.
bottom_line: A uniquely composed Colombia cup with wide-ranging aromas and favors, from sweet-tart fruit to savory herbs, mediated by a white-tea-like throughline.

title: Colombia San Pascual Natural
blind_assessment: Fruit-forward, richly chocolaty. Raspberry liqueur, chocolate fudge, rhododendron, molasses, cedar in aroma and cup. Sweet structure with gentle, round acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to notes of dark chocolate and cedar with hints of raspberry in the long.
notes: Produced at Finca San Pascual from the Castillo, Colombia, Bourbon, Typica and Tabi varieties of Arabica and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Magnolia Coffee is a Charlotte, North Carolina-based specialty roaster whose motto is “Craft roasted. Truly delicious. Socially conscious.” Magnolia particularly emphasizes community engagement through its Local Beans for Local Good programs.Visit www.magnoliacoffeeco.com or call 704-651-7726 for more information.
bottom_line: A sweetly fermenty and chocolaty Colombia cup that invokes a rum-cordial-like combination of intense chocolate and fruity liqueur.

title: Colombia San Pedro
blind_assessment: Crisply sweet, rich-toned, deep. Apricot, citrus blossom, Meyer lemon zest, cocoa nib, maple syrup in aroma and cup. Balanced, sweet-tart structure with juicy acidity; full, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to notes of lemon zest and cocoa nib in the short, with hints of apricot resurfacing in the long.
notes: Produced by Ciro Lugo of Finca San Pedro and processed by the wet, or washed, method. Corvus Coffee Roasters is based in Denver, Colorado and specializes in rare and exclusive coffees from some of the finest growers in the world. Corvus particularly focuses on processing methods and selective harvesting, which result in small, seasonal micro-lots of uniquely sweet, vibrant, and clean flavor profiles. For more information, visit www.corvuscoffee.com.
bottom_line: A pretty washed Colombia cup with notes of stone fruit and cocoa nib as deep, satisfying throughlines; particularly vibrant acidity.

title: Colombia San Roque
blind_assessment: Cocoa-toned, sweet-tart. Cocoa powder, Brazil nut, lemon balm, fir, dried fig in aroma and cup. Sweet, slightly astringent acidity; crisp, silky mouthfeel. Harmonious finish consolidates to notes of cocoa powder and lemon balm.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers of the Asociación San Roque, entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Founded in Philadelphia in 1994 by Todd Carmichael and JP Iberti, La Colombe is now owned by Chobani. Visit www.lacolombe.com for more information.
bottom_line: An accessible, brightly crisp, gently cocoa-toned Colombia cup.

title: Colombia Santa Monica Castillo Honey Lulo
blind_assessment: Tangy sweet, delicately fruit-toned. Dried hibiscus flower, pistachio, cannabis, fresh perique-fermented tobacco, cotton candy in aroma and cup. Bright, juicy acidity; plush but buoyant mouthfeel. Crisp, complex, bittersweet finish.
notes: Produced by Jairo Arcila of Finca Santa Monica, entirely of the Castillo variety of Arabica. Subject in the whole fruit to anaerobic fermentation for 72 hours, with lulo fruit and wine yeasts added to the fermentation, then dried on raised beds. Established in 2010, Red Rooster is an organic-certified micro-roaster focusing on socially conscious, high-quality coffee. Visit redroostercoffee.com or call 540-745-7338 for more information.
bottom_line: This Colombia Castillo fermented with lulo fruit is complex and quite original: delicately fruity, tartly floral, richly musky and enigmatically savory.

title: Colombia Santa Monica Pink Bourbon Honey Co-Ferment Strawberry
blind_assessment: Distinctly berry-toned, crisply sweet-tart. Wild strawberry, cocoa nib, lemon verbena, honey, fresh-cut fir in aroma and cup. Gently bright, juicy acidity; crisp, velvety mouthfeel. Strawberry and cocoa nib lead in the resonant finish.
notes: Produced by Jairo Arcila, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method, with the addition of wine yeast and strawberries to the fermentation. Established in 2009 by Amy and Scott Angelo, Oceana brews specialty coffees that have been roasted in small batches at its roasting house and café in Tequesta, Florida. Visit www.oceanacoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A Colombia Pink Bourbon co-fermented with strawberries for an intensely fruit-forward, cocoa-toned cup.

title: Colombia Santiago Joven
blind_assessment: Pungent and savory-sweet. Roasted cacoa nib and nut, lily, complex fruit (apricot, plum, blood orange), a hint of sweet licorice bark in aroma and cup. Rich, juicy acidity; lightly plush mouthfeel. Floral and cacao notes in particular carrying into a crisp finish.
notes: Farmer Santiago Joven of Finca La Montanita is a member of the ASPROTIMANA cooperative. Founded in 2001 by thirty-two producers, ASPROTIMANA is now comprised of nearly ninety. Spyhouse Coffee Roasting emphasizes building relationships within and around the coffee community through passion and knowledge. Visit www.spyhousecoffee.com or call 612-345-4348 for more information.
coffee_origin: Timana growing region, Huila Department, southern Colombia

title: Colombia Sebastian Ramirez Washed Pink Bourbon
blind_assessment: High-toned, lushly floral. Red currant, cocoa nib, wisteria, myrrh, pomelo in aroma and cup. Sparkling, balanced, very juicy acidity; taut, satiny mouthfeel. Long, harmonious, integrated and flavor-saturated finish.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 11 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 50 Coffees of 2025. Produced by Sebastian Ramirez, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Heady Cup is an Illinois-based specialty roaster with a focus on sustainability and sourcing traceable green coffees. Visit www.headycup.com for more information.
bottom_line: An exquisitely composed washed Colombia Pink Bourbon that’s as complex as it is satisfying, with nuances of flavor and aroma at every turn, and especially vibrant, compelling acidity.

title: Colombia Sebastian Ramirez Washed Pink Bourbon
blind_assessment: Bright, juicy, harmonious. Peach, freesia, pink grapefruit zest, marjoram, cocoa nib in aroma and cup. Balanced, high-toned acidity; crisp, delicate mouthfeel. Finish centers around notes of peach and marjoram.
notes: Produced by Sebastian Ramirez of Fincas El Placer, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Shoulders Coffee is a Chicago artisan roaster that emphasizes a fresh-roasted, no-nonsense approach to fine coffee. Visit www.bigshoulderscoffee.com or call 312-846-1439 for more information.
bottom_line: Bright, sweetly tart stone fruit is the throughline of this washed Colombia Pink Bourbon, supported by crisp cocoa nib and delicate herb notes.

title: Colombia Sebastian Ramirez White Honey Geisha
blind_assessment: Exquisitely floral and fruit-forward. Star jasmine, white peach, lemongrass basil, myrrh in aroma and cup. Sparkling acidity; vibrantly satiny mouthfeel. Exceptional long, coherent, compelling finish.
notes: Produced by Sebastian Ramirez of Fincas El Placer, entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the white honey method, in which a small amount of fruit flesh is left on the beans during the drying process. Heady Cup is an Illinois-based specialty roaster with a focus on sustainability and sourcing traceable green coffees. Visit www.headycup.com for more information.
bottom_line: An elegant and ethereal cup that seems both rare and accessible — floral notes drive everything that follows; it’s high-toned and confidently poised.

title: Colombia Sergio Roldan
blind_assessment: Sweetly tart, chocolaty. Pomegranate, baking chocolate, orange zest, almond, oak in aroma and cup. Tart-leaning structure with brisk acidity; plush, chewy mouthfeel. Crisply chocolaty finish with undertones of pomegranate and almond.
notes: Produced by Sergio Roldan, from trees of the Colombia, Caturra and Chiroso varieties of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Mostra Coffee is a women-, minority-, veteran-, and immigrant-owned micro-roaster based in north county San Diego. For more information, visit www.mostracoffee.com.
bottom_line: A crisp, fruit-centered natural Colombia with pleasing chocolate notes throughout the cup.

title: Colombia Sidra Natural Signature Selection
blind_assessment: Richly fruit-saturated, balanced, juicy. Black cherry, Bourbon barrel, cocoa nib, wisteria, candycap mushroom in aroma and small cup. Deep, sweet-savory structure with high-toned, malic acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Resonant, long, flavor-laden finish that fulfills the promise of the cup.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 10 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 30 Coffees of 2022. Produced by Rigoberto and Roberto Herrera entirely of the admired Sidra variety of Arabica, and processed by a proprietary natural-process extended fermentation method. Bird Rock Coffee Roasters is a retailer and wholesaler focused on organic and socially responsible coffees; it was awarded the “2012 Micro-Roaster of the Year” title by Roast Magazine. Visit www.birdrockcoffee.com or call 858-551-1707 for more information.
bottom_line: An exquisitely structured Colombia Sidra cup processed by an experimental method that highlights notes of rich fruit and sweet whiskey.
coffee_origin: Caicedonia, Valle de Cauca Department, Colombia

title: Colombia Sidra
blind_assessment: Floral-toned, richly sweet. Narcissus, roasted cacao nib, toffee, apricot, sandalwood in aroma and cup. Deeply sweet-tart structure with juicy, bright acidity; full, syrupy mouthfeel. Resonant finish centers around cocoa-toned narcissus and apricot.
notes: Produced at La Gallera Estate entirely from trees of the Sidra variety of Arabica, a hybrid of the old and respected varieties Red Bourbon and Typica. This is a wet-processed or “washed” coffee, meaning the fruit skin and pulp were removed from the beans immediately after harvesting and before drying. Kaffetre is a micro-roaster and cafe in central Taiwan, operated by Rex Chen, an authorized SCA trainer and Licensed Q-grader. For more information, visit https://www.facebook.com/pg/kaffetre.tw/about/?ref=page_internal or call +886916997779.
bottom_line: An engaging coffee from the unusual Sidra variety—rich, floral, balanced and bright.

title: Colombia Sierra Morena Pink Bourbon
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. This was Ken’s favorite in the tasting; he had it at 96 with a 10 for aroma. Co-taster John DiRuocco was a bit less enthusiastic at 94. The difference may have been their reading of the striking floral herb notes. Ken experienced them as exhilarating sweet lavender while John read them as a pleasant but drier eucalyptus. But both overall admired this sweetly citrusy, walnut-toned, brightly chocolaty espresso whose character resonates through the finish and retains character impressively in three parts milk.
notes: Produced by Wilson Alva of Finca Sierra Morena, entirely of the Pink Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin, pulp and flesh all removed before drying). Imported by Coffee Quest. Wonderstate Coffee, formerly Kickapoo Coffee, is an award-winning roaster based in rural Wisconsin known for its commitment to guaranteeing higher pay for farmers and operating the country’s first 100% solar-powered roastery. Visit www.wonderstate.com for more information.
bottom_line: A deeply complex, gently citrusy, crisply floral espresso that rounds gracefully without losing character in cappuccino-scaled milk.

title: Colombia Solarte
blind_assessment: Delicately rich, deeply sweet. Toffee, mulberry, cedar, roasted cacao nib, rhododendron-like flowers in aroma and cup. Balanced, sweet-tart acidity; plush, buoyantly creamy mouthfeel. The crisply cocoa-toned finish is redolent of almond and rhododendron.
notes: Produced by Don Uriel Solarte, this coffee took sixth place out of 500 coffees in the 2016 Best of Cauca competition organized by Banexport and Cafe Imports. Greater Goods was founded in 2015; its mission is to enrich the lives of coffee-drinkers through passion, creativity, innovation and a commitment to the consistency of the specialty coffee the company roasts as well as to the local causes supported by its proceeds. Visit greatergoodsroasting.com or call 512-858-2680 for more information.
bottom_line: A refined, balanced, sweetly tart Colombia cup, animated by cocoa notes throughout.
coffee_origin: Valle del Cauca Department, southwestern Colombia

title: Colombia Special Process Microlot 504 “Higher and Higher” Espresso
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Tart, rich, complex. Dark chocolate, blood orange, sandalwood, narcissus-like flowers in aroma and small cup. Lightly syrupy mouthfeel; sandalwood, citrus and flowers carry into a dry but resonant finish. Softens yet retains its tart richness in three parts milk.
notes: In addition to his retail roasting operation Aroma Roast Coffees, Simon Hsieh also operates Soaring Phoenix Trading, a business focused on purposed-built commercial espresso blends and high quality single-origin coffees. Visit www.facebook.com/4ArtsZeroDefectCoffees or call 886-0983-749876 for more information.

title: Colombia Special Process Microlot 511 “Memory Orchard” Espresso
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Sweet, deep, balanced. Dark chocolate, grapefruit, fresh-cut cedar, crisp flowers – lavender, freesia – in aroma and small cup. Heavy, syrupy, almost chewy mouthfeel; dark chocolate and cedar in a rich though drying finish. Strong presence in three parts milk: dark chocolate, cedar, flowers, anise.
notes: In addition to his retail roasting operation Aroma Roast Coffees, Simon Hsieh also operates Soaring Phoenix Trading, a business focused on purposed-built commercial espresso blends and high quality single-origin coffees. Visit www.facebook.com/4ArtsZeroDefectCoffees or call 886-0983-749876 for more information.

title: Colombia Suarez Cauca
blind_assessment: Deep and richly sweet. Mulberry, fresh-cut oak, peppermint, hazelnut, faint narcissus in aroma and cup. Juicy, vibrantly tart acidity; plump, velvety mouthfeel. Finish consolidates around a rich hazelnut- and molasses-inflected sweetness.
notes: A blend of coffees from small producers in the Valle de Cauca Department, intended to showcase the profile of the growing region. Evaluated here for brewed applications, PT’s will be offering this coffee in future as a single-origin espresso. Roasted at PT’s Coffee, where the motto is “without the love, it’s just coffee.” Visit www.ptscoffee.com or call 888-678-5282 for more information.
coffee_origin: Valle del Cauca Department, southwestern Colombia

title: Colombia Sudan Rume
blind_assessment: Multi-faceted, enticingly sweet-savory. Lychee, cardamom, cocoa nib, fennel, star jasmine in aroma and cup. Savory-sweet structure with vibrantly juicy acidity; syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Rich-toned, very long finish with leading notes of lychee and cardamom.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 15 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 30 Coffees of 2022. Comprised entirely of beans from the rare Sudan Rume, a presumably very old variety of Arabica originally selected from wild trees growing on the Boma Plateau of Sudan, close to the border with Ethiopia. Produced by Rigoberto Herrera at Granja La Esperanza in Colombia and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Nostalgia Coffee Roasters is a woman-owned specialty coffee roaster founded by Taylor Fields in 2018 as a mobile café. Nostalgia is now focused on bringing exceptional coffee to folks around the world via its online store and wholesale program. Visit www.nostalgiacoffeeroasters.com for more information.
bottom_line: An excitingly complex natural-processed Colombia Sudan Rume, layered and deep, with sweet tropical fruit notes and an umami foundation.

title: Colombia Supremo
blind_assessment: Both co-cupper Andy Newbom (90) and Ken (90) emphasized the crisp acidity and balanced structure of this aromatically rather quiet coffee. "Exquisite crisp green-apple acidity with a touch of kiwi skin" and a "nicely smooth mouthfeel with a bit of a fruit leather feeling" for Andy, who found the green apple carrying into the flavor. For Ken the gently acidy tendency in the flavor suggested dry berry and lemon; both Andy and Ken noted a hint of cocoa nib, a vegetable-toned chocolate. More green apple in the finish for Andy while Ken simply describes a pleasing tart sweetness.
notes: Designated Don Telmo Reserva Especial, this coffee is made up entirely of the heirloom Bourbon variety from the well-known Mesa de los Santos farm. This coffee is Rainforest Alliance certified, meaning it was produced following sustainable ecological and socio-economic criteria developed by the Sustainable Agricultural Network, a coalition of independent, environment-focused non-governmental organizations. Barrington Coffee is an artisan roaster dedicated to elite coffees, fresh delivery and roasting that foregrounds the coffee and not the roast. Visit www.barringtoncoffee.com or call 800-528-0998 for more information.
coffee_origin: Bucaramanga growing region, Santander Department, Colombia.

title: Colombia Supremo
blind_assessment: Rich, pronounced but sweet-toned acidity dominates aroma and cup. Milk chocolate, fresh-cut aromatic wood and a hint of fruit in the aroma. In the cup heavy body, continued aromatic wood and chocolate with a dry, pungent fruit that suggests black currant or dried apricot. Flavor outlasts astringency in the long, resonant finish.
notes: Supremo is the highest grade of Colombia coffee based on fewest physical imperfections and largest bean size. This coffee is available to consumers via Don Francisco Gourmet Coffee, the specialty line of F. Gavina & Sons, the large family-owned-and-operated roasting company in the Los Angeles area. Visit www.don-francisco.com or call 800-697-5282 for more information.

title: Colombia Supremo
blind_assessment: Richly and deeply sweet. Baker’s chocolate, raisin, Brazil nut, magnolia, oak in aroma and cup. Roundly tart acidity; plump, syrupy mouthfeel. Richly drying, quietly nut-toned finish.
notes: Supremo is the highest grade of Colombia coffee based on bean size and relative freedom from physical imperfections. Big Shoulders Coffee is a Chicago artisan roaster that emphasizes a fresh-roasted, no-nonsense approach to fine coffee. Visit www.bigshoulderscoffee.com or call 312-888-3042 for more information.

title: Colombia Supremo Pitalito Estate
blind_assessment: A tribute to the tartly sweet, invigorating sensation coffee insiders call acidity. In the aroma richly fruity and orange-toned; in the cup giddy with rich, high-toned acidity laced with fruit suggesting oranges and tart cherries. The acidity softens and sweetens voluptuously in the finish.
notes: The Roasterie is a leading, quality-oriented specialty roaster that emphasizes its commitment to "air roasting," a technology utilizing a column of hot air rather than the conventional turning drum to agitate the roasting beans. Roasterie president Danny O'Neill is an indefatigable coffee traveler and farm visitor whose travel and generous personality has facilitated this and several other well-established "relationship" coffees. Proceeds from the sale of this coffee over the past five years have helped build a community center. Visit www.theroasterie.com or call 800-376-0245 for more information.
coffee_origin: San Augustin growing region, Huila Department, Colombia

title: Colombia Supremo
blind_assessment: Very sweet-toned, intense aroma with distinctly buttery vanilla notes and hints of chocolate, honey and flowers. In the cup sweetly and richly acidy. The fundamental flavor complex is a chocolaty coffee fruit with heady complications of vanilla, flowers and honey.
notes: Supremo is the highest grade of Colombian coffee, based mainly on bean size. Don Francisco's is the upscale specialty coffee line of F. Gavina & Sons, the large, family-owned-and-operated roasting company in the Los Angeles area. Don Francisco's is named after Francisco Gavina, the Cuban-born father of the Gavina clan.Visit www.donfranciscos.com or call 800-428-4627 for more information.

title: Colombia Tabi La Roca
blind_assessment: Gently bright, deep-toned. Concord grape, sandalwood, fudgesicle, cashew, rhododendron in aroma and cup. Delicately bright, balanced acidity; very viscous, satiny mouthfeel. Finish leads with notes of Concord grape and rhododendron with fudgesicle undertones.
notes: Produced at Finca Santa Monica, entirely of the Tabi variety of Arabica, and processed by the anaerobic natural method, in which the whole fruit is fermented in tanks with limited oxygen before drying, also in the whole fruit. Big Shoulders Coffee is a Chicago artisan roaster that emphasizes a fresh-roasted, no-nonsense approach to fine coffee. Visit www.bigshoulderscoffee.com or call 312-846-1439 for more information.
bottom_line: Equal parts fruity and chocolatey, this uncommon variety is anaerobically processed to highlight intense sweet-tartness, while dessert-like chocolate notes provide the grounding undercurrent.

title: Colombia Thermal Shock Double Anaerobic Granja Paraiso Orange Gesha
blind_assessment: Elegantly berry-toned, dessert-like. Mulberry, candycap mushroom amber, apricot nectar, dark chocolate in aroma and cup. Brightly sweet-savory acidity; plush, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Harmonious, integrated, flavor-saturated finish.
notes: Produced by Wilton Benitez, entirely of the Orange Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the double-anaerobic thermal shock method, in which the coffee fruit, after having been first sanitized with ozone, undergoes two stages of fermentation. First, the whole cherries are submerged under water for 48 hours, then the beans are pulped and fermented with a strain of Lactobacillus for 24 hours. After fermentation, the beans are given a “thermal shock” using hot and cold rinses to help the beans absorb the fermentation metabolites and halt any further fermentation. Kakalove Café is a nano-roaster located in the small city of Chia-Yi in Taiwan that strives to procure and roast the finest quality coffee. Visit www.kakalovecafe.com.tw or email kahiyuho@gmail.com for more information.
bottom_line: A complex, richly sweet, deeply savory double-anaerobic Colombia with riveting berry and stone fruit notes alongside umami impulses.

title: Colombia Thermal Shock Yeast Anaerobic Natural Huila Las Flores Sidra
blind_assessment: Sweetly tart, slightly umami. Tamarind, candycap mushroom, raw cacao, watermelon candy, myrrh in aroma and cup. Sparkling acidity; full, very satiny mouthfeel. Exceptionally long, layered, rich and engaging finish.
notes: Produced by John Vergara of Finca Las Flores, entirely of the Sidra variety of Arabica, and processed by the thermal shock anaerobic method with the addition of wine yeasts to the fermentation. The thermal shock process involves first sanitizing the coffee fruit with ozone, then fermenting the whole cherries twice, giving them a “thermal shock” using hot and cold rinses to help them absorb the fermentation metabolites and halt any further fermentation. Kakalove Café is a nano-roaster located in the small city of Chia-Yi in Taiwan that strives to procure and roast the finest quality coffee. Visit www.kakalovecafe.com.tw or email kahiyuho@gmail.com for more information.
bottom_line: A uniquely composed, sweet-tart, experimentally processed Colombia with an intriguing umami detour.

title: Colombia Thermal Shock
blind_assessment: Juicy, aromatic and sweetly spice-toned. Red plum, guava, blood orange, pink peppercorn and dark chocolate in aroma and cup. Bright, fruit-toned acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. The finish is persistent, centering red plum, pink peppercorn and dark chocolate.
notes: Produced by Elkin Guzman of Finca El Mirador, entirely of the Tabi variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method, with the addition of a thermal shock step (a rapid temperature shift during the fermentation and rinsing stages). Indaba Coffee is a Spokane, Washington-based specialty coffee roaster and café founded in 2009, known for thoughtfully sourced coffees and a community-centered mission built around hospitality and social impact. Visit www.indabacoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: An intriguing thermal-shock Colombia Tabi that balances juicy tropical and stone fruit with savory spice and dark chocolate, giving the cup an appealing tension between sweet and savory impulses.
coffee_origin: Guji Zone, Oromia Region, south-central Ethiopia

title: Colombia Timana
blind_assessment: Round, rich aroma with distinct butter notes and hints of flowers and lemon. Simplifies in the cup: good body and a sweet, gently crisp structure, but little nuance.
notes: This coffee is Rainforest Alliance certified, meaning it was produced following sustainable ecological and socio-economic criteria developed by the Sustainable Agricultural Network, a coalition of independent, environment-focused non-governmental organizations. Caribou Coffee is a large (second largest after Starbucks) retail roasting chain based in the upper Middle West whose rather irreverent motto "Life is short. Stay awake for it" belies a serious approach to coffee. Visit www.cariboucoffee.com or call 888-227-4268 for more information.

title: Colombia Tio Conejo Sudan Rume
blind_assessment: Deeply sweet, fruit-forward, and complex. Pomegranate, red grape, cocoa nib, tamarind, lavender in aroma and cup. Bright, winey acidity; full, velvety-smooth mouthfeel. The finish leads with tart fruit and floral notes that resolve gracefully into deep cocoa sweetness.
notes: Produced by Angela Suarez of Finca Tío Conejo from trees of the Sudan Rume variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Utopian Coffee is a specialty roaster based in Fort Wayne, Indiana. Visit www.utopiancoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A plush, fruit-saturated natural-process Sudan Rume from Colombia’s Tío Conejo, offering layered fruit and floral tones grounded by chocolate richness.
coffee_origin: Vereda Santa Rita, Manizales, Caldas, Colombia

title: Colombia Toledo Labateca
blind_assessment: A complex and interesting coffee rather than a perfect one. The aroma is subdued but round and sweet with a distinct cherry-toned milk chocolate. In the cup the acidity is soft but the fruit turns bracing and tartly sweet -- think the pleasantly sour sweetness of pie cherries. As the cup cools the fruit softens once again, revealing a refined but almost candyish chocolate character.
notes: CC's Coffee is the upscale specialty line of Community Coffee, a distinguished family-owned coffee company founded in 1919. This coffee is facilitated by a sustainable coffee partnership between Community Coffee and the Toledo and Labateca community first established in 2001. Community puts ten cents per pound of coffee purchased into a local endowment for social development projects, including a new technical school for high-school-age children. Visit www.communitycoffee.com or call 800-525-5583 for more information.

title: Colombia Tolima
blind_assessment: Apple-toned, richly herbal. Red apple, sage blossom, panela, anise, walnut in aroma and cup. Briskly sweet acidity; rounded, buttery-smooth mouthfeel. The finish leads with red apple and walnut tones.
notes: Produced by 379 smallholding farmers organized around the Cooperativa Multiactiva de Asociaciones Agropecuarias del Tolima (MULTICOOP), from trees of the Castillo, Caturra, Catimor, Colombia, Geisha and Tabi varieties of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). SkyTop Coffee is a USDA-certified organic specialty coffee roaster based in Manlius, New York. For more information, visit skytopcoffee.com.
bottom_line: A crisp and herbaceous Colombia with sweet apple brightness, subtle floral accents, and a warm, nutty finish.
coffee_origin: lanadas, Rio Blanco, and Chaparral, Tolima, Colombia

title: Colombia Tolima Cup of Excellence Presidential Award Winner El Placer
blind_assessment: Sweet-toned and alive with a dense, shifting complexity. Cedar, orange, distinct butterscotch, tomato, perhaps chocolate in the aroma. In the cup low-toned acidity and lightly syrupy in mouthfeel, with an almost sugary sweetness and tight-knit notes of butterscotch, caramel, honey, ripe but slightly tart orange. Rich and sweet in the short finish, though a slight hint of astringency surfaces in the long.
notes: A prize winner in the 2006 Colombia Second Harvest Cup of Excellence competition, where as a green (unroasted) coffee it placed third out of hundreds of entries, attracting a score of 92.38 from an international jury. Produced from trees of the caturra variety at an elevation of approximately 5,100 feet by farmer Cesar Julio Munoz Calderon. Terroir is a microroaster selling only elite single-origin coffees, no blends. It specializes in medium roast styles designed to foreground the character of the green coffee. Terroir is the creation of George Howell, one of the world's leading coffee visionaries. Visit www.terroircoffee.com or call 866-444-5282 for more information.

title: Colombia Tolima Finca El Mirador Washed Anaerobic
blind_assessment: Delicately fruit-toned. Guava, ginger blossom, cocoa nib, cedar, agave syrup in aroma and cup. Sweet-toned structure with juicy acidity; crisp, satiny mouthfeel. Cocoa-toned finish, supported by notes of cedar and agave.
notes: Produced by Victor Gutiérrez of Finca Mirador entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica. Processed by the anaerobic washed method, in which the fermentation step occurs in a hermetically sealed vessel before the beans are washed and dried. With more than 10 years of roasting experience, Regent strives to deliver coffee with care and purpose. Visit regentcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: An appealing washed anaerobic cup: deep-toned, nuanced, richly sweet.

title: Colombia Tolima Finca El Vergel Rebel Geisha
blind_assessment: Complex, multi-layered. Green oolong, rosehips, sandalwood, gingko, Meyer lemon zest in aroma and and cup. Exceptionally sweet with elegant acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Richly resonant, sweetly tart finish.
notes: Produced by Marta Bayter and her sons, Shady and Elias, of Vergel Estate. Composed entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica, and processed by the honey or semi-washed method, in which the skins are removed from the fruit but some of the fruit flesh is allowed to dry on the beans. Bargain Cafe is a specialty coffee roaster in Taitung, Taiwan. Visit https://shopee.tw/iamjiter for more information.
bottom_line: An enticingly rich Colombia Geisha aromatic fireworks whose promise is fulfilled in the cup with deep oolong-like impulses and sweet citrus zest.

title: Colombia Tolima Finca Las Florestales
blind_assessment: Juicy but bittersweet, slightly savory cup. Red grape, cantaloupe, grapefruit, lavender-like flowers in quiet aroma and crisp cup. Richly round acidity. Lightly syrupy mouthfeel turns juicy as the cup cools. Citrus and floral notes linger in a dry finish.
notes: From trees of the Caturra variety, a compact growing selection of Bourbon, this coffee was grown by Maximino Gutierrez and the adjacent farms of his brothers and sons, who collectively market their coffee under the name Finca Las Florestales. Portland Roasting emphasizes sustainable environmental and social practices throughout its business, including its "Farm Friendly Direct" sourcing program involving partnership projects with coffee producers in several origin countries. Visit www.portlandroasting.com or call 800-949-3898 for more information.

title: Colombia Tolima Geisha
blind_assessment: Delicate, fruit- and floral-toned. Apricot, honeysuckle, cocoa nib, white peppercorn, myrrh in aroma and cup. Deeply sweet structure with gently bright acidity; silky-smooth mouthfeel. Quiet but pretty finish with notes of apricot and white peppercorn and a hint of honeysuckle in the long.
notes: Produced by Israel Hernandez of Finca Buenos Aires entirely of the Geisha variety of Arabica and processed by the washed method. Available as part of a Geisha sampler of three coffees. Paradise Roasters specializes in micro-lot Arabica and Robusta coffees from Asia and other emerging origins. The company prides itself on quality and freshness, craft-roasting coffees in small batches only after orders are placed. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.
bottom_line: A complex, original washed-process Colombia Geisha that hits all of the celebrated Geisha notes: stonefruit, sweet flowers, gentle spice notes, crisp cocoa.

title: Colombia Tolima Genius
blind_assessment: High-toned, sweetly tart. Pomegranate, red wine, milk chocolate, cedar, agave syrup in aroma and cup. Sparkling acidity; satiny, viscous mouthfeel. Fruity finish with undertones of milk chocolate.
notes: Produced by Marta Bayter and her sons, Shady and Elias, of Vergel Estate, entirely of the Red Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the carbonic maceration method, which involves fermenting whole coffee fruit inside a sealed container that has been flushed with CO2, then drying the coffee in the whole fruit. Big Shoulders Coffee is a Chicago artisan roaster that emphasizes a fresh-roasted, no-nonsense approach to fine coffee. Visit www.bigshoulderscoffee.com or call 312-846-1439 for more information.
bottom_line: This carbonic-macerated Colombia is tart-leaning and also very sweet; notes of milk chocolate provide richness as ballast.

title: Colombia Tolima Honey Organic Fair Trade
blind_assessment: Sweetly rounded, gently fruit-toned. Baked apple, milk chocolate, roasted almond, mandarin zest and honey in aroma and cup. Briskly sweet acidity; smooth, lightly creamy mouthfeel. The finish is clean and lingering, with notes of cocoa, toasted nut and soft citrus.
notes: Produced by Jairo Aviles of Finca La Cumbre and processed by the honey method, in which some of the fruit flesh is left on the beans during the drying process. Certified USDA Organic and Fair Trade. Fair Mountain Coffee Roasters, based in New Jersey, specializes in organic-certified, fair trade coffees. Visit www.fairmountaincoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A comforting, approachable honey-process Colombia that offers pleasing sweetness, balanced structure and everyday drinkability while reflecting Fair Mountain's commitment to responsibly sourced coffee.

title: Colombia Tolima Jairo Guiterrez Micro-Lot 07
blind_assessment: Intense, balanced aroma: cedar, cherry, flowers, orange. In the cup syrupy body with an almost bouillon-like richness, deeply but quietly acidy, with floral high notes and a wonderfully deep cherry- and cedar-toned chocolate. The pungent chocolate/fruit notes carry into a long, flavor-saturated finish.
notes: This is a very micro micro-lot, weighing only 350 pounds, selected from the 15-acre farm of Jairo Guiterrez. Paradise Roasters prides itself on roasting and shipping coffee only after orders are placed. Its metaphoric mission is to bring some paradisiacal warmth from the coffee-growing south to the cool environs of Minnesota. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.

title: Colombia Tolima La Aldea
blind_assessment: Delicate, soft, silky. Honey, night-blooming flowers, cocoa butter, vanilla in aroma and cup. Gentle but lively, floral-toned acidity; buoyant, silky mouthfeel. Vanilla in particular carries into a quietly flavor-saturated finish.
notes: This coffee has benefited from the “million-pesos” program, which guarantees farmers a significant premium for coffees rated 90 points and above. Papa Lin's Coffee Roasting is a “nano” roaster located in Yorktown Heights, New York, that focuses on carefully sourced, extremely high-quality specialty coffees that are custom-roasted to the preference of every customer. Visit www.papalins.com for more information.

title: Colombia Tolima La Gallera Honey Process
blind_assessment: Crisply sweet, spice-toned. Pie cherry, oak, baking chocolate, freesia-like flowers, sandalwood in aroma and cup. Sweet in structure with citrusy acidity; syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. The finish centers around tart stone fruit and aromatic wood notes, with a hint of spicy florals underneath.
notes: Produced at Finca La Gallera and processed by the honey method, in which the skins are removed from the fruit but some of the fruit flesh (mucilage) is allowed to dry on the beans. Buon Caffe is a specialty coffee roaster and cafe in Taipei, Taiwan. Visit www.buoncaffe.com.tw for more information.
bottom_line: A cleanly fruit-driven honey-processed Colombia with pleasingly spicy floral undertones.

title: Colombia Tolima Monteverde Estate Natural Wush Wush
blind_assessment: Unorthodox but coherent and compelling. Pungent rose, fresh fennel frond, ripe cantaloupe, walnut, marshmallow in aroma and cup. Roundly sweet-savory in structure, with an impressively smooth, plush mouthfeel. Rose-like flowers prevail in a deeply rich finish.
notes: Produced on Monteverde Estate in Colombia by the Gilardo Gutierrez family from trees of the rare Ethiopia Wush Wush variety of Arabica. Processed by fermenting the fresh coffee fruit in an oxygen-free environment before drying it in the whole fruit. Dou Zhai Coffee is a café and roastery on a quiet lane in Taoyuan City, Taiwan, that offers a wide range of exceptional coffees. Visit www.douzhaicafe.com.tw for more information.
bottom_line: An extraordinary coffee, difficult to characterize in typical coffee language, yet deeply satisfying, ringing with quiet, resonant authority.

title: Colombia Tolima Planadas Lot 3
blind_assessment: Delicate, pure, balanced. Honey, flowers, fresh-cut fir in aroma and cup. Gentle, juicy acidity; smooth, lively, almost effervescent mouthfeel. A hint of chocolate surfaces in a sweet finish.
notes: Produced from trees of the Caturra variety, a compact-growing selection of Bourbon, from Las Hermosa farm and surrounding El Eden hamlets. Thirty-Thirty is a small-batch coffee roasting company located in Peoria Illinois that is committed to sourcing the finest green coffees and to expressing the individuality and character of those coffees through the roasting process all the way to the cup. Visit www.thirty-thirtycoffee.com or call 309-713-2983 for more information.

title: Colombia Tolima Reynel Perez Micro-Lot
blind_assessment: Exhilaratingly intense but roundly sweet-toned aroma: black cherry, flowers, milk chocolate, with an underlying cedar-toned crispness. Sweet flowers and cherry dominate in the cup with an almost symphonic richness of tone. Medium bodied but silky mouthfeel. The floral notes linger into the farthest reaches of the finish.
notes: Produced by farmer Reynel Perez at an elevation of approximately 5,500 feet. This 2006 crop, less than 1,000 pounds, was purchased in its entirety by Paradise Roasters. Paradise prides itself on roasting and shipping coffee only after orders are placed. Its metaphoric mission is to bring some paradisiacal warmth from the coffee-growing south to the cool environs of Minnesota. Visit www.paradiseroasters.com or call 763-433-0626 for more information.

title: Colombia Tolima SOE
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Balanced, fruity, sweetly nutty. Notes of red apple, caramel, roasted almond, cocoa and plum in aroma and small cup. Crisp, satiny mouthfeel; resonant, cocoa-toned finish. In cappuccino format, apple and caramel notes become dessert-like, reminiscent of tarte tatin.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers, from trees of the Caturra, Colombia, Castillo and Bourbon varieties of Arabica, and processed by the washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Buon Caffe is a specialty coffee roaster and cafe in Taipei, Taiwan. Visit www.buoncaffe.com.tw for more information.
bottom_line: A classic Colombia Tolima espresso: fruit-toned and sweetly nutty in the straight show, indulgently dessert-like in milk.

title: Colombia Tolima Villa Karina Bourbon Naranja Honey
blind_assessment: Deeply sweet-savory. Yellow plum, almond, pink peppercorn, narcissus, cedar in aroma and cup. Complex, bittersweet acidity; crisp, lightly satiny mouthfeel. Yellow plum and pink peppercorn notes carry the delicate finish.
notes: Produced by José Amir Garzon of Villa Karina, entirely of the Orange Bourbon variety of Arabica, and processed by the honey method, in which some of the fruit flesh is left on the beans during the drying process. Buon Caffe is a specialty coffee roaster and cafe in Taipei, Taiwan. Visit www.buoncaffe.com.tw for more information.
bottom_line: A pretty honey-processed Colombia Bourbon with notes of stone fruit, floral-toned spices and rich aromatic wood.

title: Colombia Tolima
blind_assessment: Sweetly tart, delicately fermenty. Notes suggesting Jolly Rancher, chocolate fudge, rum barrel, baking spices, sandalwood in aroma and cup. Sweet structure with gentle, round acidity; velvety mouthfeel. Sweetly fermenty finish with crisp chocolate fudge notes throughout.
notes: Produced by Katerinne Gutierrez and family entirely from trees of the Yellow Wush Wush variety of Arabica and processed by the natural method. Jaunt Coffee Roasters is a San Diego-based roaster and café with an extensive coffee and food menu. Visit www.jauntcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A heady Colombia cup from the admired Ethiopian Wush Wush variety, processed by the natural method to bring out sweet but distinctive alcohol-ferment notes.

title: Colombia Tolimas
blind_assessment: Classically pure, brightly balanced profile. Honey, flowers, ripe lemon, with a rounding hint of cocoa in aroma and cup. Sweet, juicy acidity; syrupy mouthfeel. Flavor may fade a bit in the finish but the poised, complete structure of the coffee rings on.
notes: A classic Colombia from one of the lesser known but respected Colombia growing regions. Turnstile Coffee Bar brings the city coffee experience to the Jersey Shore in Belmar, New Jersey.Visit www.turnstilecoffee.com or call 732-894-9012 for more information.

title: Colombia Tres Dragones
