title: SpeedGoatKarl’s 100-Mile Blend
blind_assessment: Nutty, cocoa-nib-like chocolate dominates in aroma and cup, with complicating hints of cedar, honeyish flowers and molasses. Backgrounded acidity; light, slightly leanish mouthfeel. Some cocoa-nib chocolate carries into a richly balanced finish.
notes: This blend was created in partnership with ‘ultrarunner’ Karl Meltzer, who at this date has won thirty-two (and counting) 100-mile mountain runs. Jameson Coffee is a small-batch roaster in Greencastle Indiana. Their mission is to “Offer exceptional tasting coffee, provide unequaled service, treat people well and have fun.” Visit www.jamesoncoffee.com or call 800-694-9559 for more information.

title: Sphere Coffee Club Guatemala
blind_assessment: Richly sweet-savory. Toffee, dried persimmon, almond butter, mandarin orange, cedar in aroma and cup. Sweet structure with gentle acidity; full, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to notes of persimmon and almond.
notes: Produced by Javier Cabrera of Finca San Isidro Chacaya, entirely of the Pacamara variety of Arabica, and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). City Boy Coffee is a specialty roaster based in Long Island City, New York. Visit www.cityboycoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A rich-toned Guatemala Pacamara, complex and deep, with notes of persimmon and sweet almond front and center.

title: Spice Island Blend
blind_assessment: Sweetly roast-rounded. Cocoa powder, Brazil nut, singed oak, raisin, hint of thyme in aroma and cup. Bittersweet structure with gentle, round acidity; thin, velvety mouthfeel. Roast-forward finish with notes of cocoa powder and singed oak.
notes: Metropolis Coffee’s motto is “Great coffee for everyone.” The Chicago-based roaster specializes in affordable, high-quality single-origins and blends. Visit www.metropoliscoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A blend with a developed roast profile, slightly roasty and nicely cocoa-toned.

title: Spinelli Blend
blind_assessment: A gently roasty, light-bodied blend: sweet, balanced, with fresh leather, grapefruit and sweet herb notes, lemon thyme perhaps. Slightly astringent in the finish.
notes: Tully's is a large quality-oriented specialty roasting company and cafe chain that now appears to be the only large-scale competitor to Starbucks left standing in Seattle. Visit www.tullys.com or call 206-233-2070 for more information.

title: Splendid Espresso Blend
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Rich, sweet-toned aroma: toast, nut, flowers, apricot. In the small cup rather lean in mouthfeel but pleasing in flavor: sandalwood, apricot-like or perhaps mango-like fruit, dark chocolate, a hint of flowers. Rich, flavor-saturated finish. Crisply chocolaty in milk with continued complications of apricot and sandalwood.
notes: Based in Thailand, P&F Coffee is a roaster that offers training, brewing equipment in addition to retail and wholesale coffee. Visit www.pnfcoffee.com or call +668-6789-2699 for more information.

title: Splendid Espresso Blend
blind_assessment: Sweet, deep, crisp aroma: aromatic wood, toast, hints of flowers and tropical fruit. In the small cup big body, slightly rough but deeply syrupy mouthfeel, notes of flowers, dark chocolate, banana- or coconut-toned fruit. Sweet, rich, flavor-saturated finish. Crisply chocolaty in milk, though it does not completely open and bloom.
notes: Based in Thailand, P&F Coffee is a roaster that offers training and brewing equipment in addition to retail and wholesale coffee. Visit www.pnfcoffee.com or call 886-86789-2699 for more information.

title: Spring Blend
blind_assessment: Sweetly nut-toned, delicately bright. Pistachio, cocoa powder, red grape, cedar, hint of tarragon in aroma and cup. Brislky sweet acidity; full, satiny mouthfeel. Cocoa-toned finish supported by notes of pistachio and red grape.
notes: A blend of coffees from two origins: a washed Guatemala and a natural-processed Ethiopia. Buon Caffe is a specialty coffee roaster and cafe in Taipei, Taiwan. Visit www.buoncaffe.com.tw for more information.
bottom_line: A quietly confident blend of washed Guatemala and natural-processed Ethiopia, the former contributing complex nut tones, and the latter, structured fruit.

title: Spring Blend
blind_assessment: Elegant, balanced dark roast: Comfortably sweet with a shimmer of acidity and a hint of roastiness. The bittersweet chocolate and pineapple notes in the aroma deepen and round congenially in the cup.
notes: Served at Spring, a Chicago-area restaurant that serves much-praised Asian-influenced new American cuisine designed by chef Shawn McClain. Intelligentsia is a leading, award-winning Chicago-area roaster with a commitment to quality epitomized by the practice of printing roast dates on coffee packaging. Visit www.intelligentsiacoffee.com or call 888-945-9786 for more information.

title: Spring Dawn
blind_assessment: Sweetly tart, fruit-toned. Raspberry, almond, dark chocolate, narcissus, oak in aroma and cup. Sweet structure with brisk acidity; very full, syrupy mouthfeel. Chocolaty finish with undertones of crisply sweet almond.
notes: A blend comprised of coffees from Ethiopia, Rwanda and Panama. Luv Moshi is a Taiwan-based specialty coffee roaster. Visit https://www.facebook.com/luvMoshi for more information.
bottom_line: A harmonious blend with chocolate and nut anchors and pleasingly bright fruit and spicy floral complications.

title: Spring Loop Espresso Blend
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Chocolaty and sweet-toned. Baking chocolate, cashew, molasses, raisin, oak in aroma and cup. Syrupy-smooth mouthfeel; crisp, chocolaty finish. In three parts milk, notes of baking chocolate take front and center, with undertones of molasses and cashew.
notes: A blend of coffees from Colombia and El Salvador designed to be brewed as espresso. Buon Caffe is a specialty coffee roaster and cafe in Taipei, Taiwan. Visit www.buoncaffe.com.tw for more information.
bottom_line: A very sweet espresso blend, richly nutty and crisply chocolaty, with the chocolate particularly prominent in cappuccino format.

title: Spring Revival Blend
blind_assessment: Sweet-toned, fresh aroma, with hints of orangy fruit, dry berry, dark chocolate. In the cup very soft acidity, plush mouthfeel, and an almost sugary sweetness with continued hints of dry berry. The sweetness carries into the finish, where a suggestion of the chocolate revives.
notes: Evaluated pre-ground. A seasonal blend of coffees only available for a limited time. Certified Fair Trade, meaning all coffees in the blend were purchased from small-holding farmers at a "fair" or economically sustainable price. Green Mountain Coffee Roasters is one of the country's leading specialty roasters, offering a particularly wide-ranging variety of origins and roast styles, including this blend. Visit www.GreenMountainCoffee.com or call 888-879-4627 for more information.

title: Spring Revival Blend
blind_assessment: Lovely balance. Crisply sweet-toned aroma: lemon, flowers, and a deepening hint of pungent dried fruit. In the cup gently bright, with a continued delicate sweetness and complex cherryish fruit completely free of bitter or astringent imbalances. Cleanly simple finish.
notes: Evaluated pre-ground. A seasonal blend of coffees from Rwanda, Mexico and Colombia, available only for a limited time. Certified Fair Trade, meaning these coffees were purchased from small-holding farmers at a "fair" or economically sustainable price. Keurig/Green Mountain, formerly Green Mountain Coffee Roasters, pioneered single-serve capsule brewing in the United States with its Keurig brewing system, and remains one of the country’s leading large specialty roasters, offering a particularly wide-ranging variety of origins and roast styles. Visit www.GreenMountainCoffee.com or call 888-879-4627 for more information.

title: St. Helena Bamboo Hedge Estate Peaberry
blind_assessment: Delicate, sweetly tart and intriguingly savory. Red currant, dried apricot, Meyer lemon, black tea and cocoa nib in aroma and cup. Softly brisk acidity; light, silky mouthfeel. The finish is persistent and nuanced, with notes of dried apricot, black tea and cocoa nib.
notes: A rare coffee grown on the island of St. Helena, a British territory in the South Atlantic Ocean — a Bourbon processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). This coffee consists entirely of peaberries, a kind of bean that results when the coffee fruit develops a single, oval bean rather than the usual pair of flat-sided beans. Sea Island Coffee is a London-based roaster specializing in rare origins and varieties. Visit Seaislandcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A distinctive St. Helena peaberry with an appealing tension between tart fruit, tea-like delicacy and chocolaty sweetness, expressed in a light-bodied but quite persistent cup.

title: St. Helena Bamboo Hedge Estate
blind_assessment: Crisply sweet, chocolaty. Baking chocolate, hazelnut, lemon balm, cedar, lily in aroma and cup. Brisk, sweet-toned acidity; velvety-smooth mouthfeel. Finish consolidates to notes of baking chocolate and lily.
notes: A rare coffee grown on the island of St. Helena, a British territory in the South Atlantic Ocean — a green-tipped Bourbon processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Sea Island Coffee is a London-based roaster specializing in rare origins and varieties. Visit seaislandcoffee.com.
bottom_line: A coffee as interesting for its rare origin (the island of St. Helena) as its friendly, chocolaty and nut-toned cup.

title: St. Helena Wranghams Estate Peaberry
blind_assessment: Restrained, crisp and gently sweet. Baked pear, mandarin zest, dried cherry, almond brittle and cocoa powder in aroma and cup. Softly bright acidity; light-bodied, smooth mouthfeel. The finish is sweet and persistent, with baked pear, almond brittle and cocoa powder tones.
notes: A rare coffee grown on the island of St. Helena, a British territory in the South Atlantic Ocean — a Bourbon processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). This coffee consists entirely of peaberries, a kind of bean that results when the coffee fruit develops a single, oval bean rather than the usual pair of flat-sided beans. Sea Island Coffee is a London-based roaster specializing in rare origins and varieties. Visit Seaislandcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A subtle St. Helena peaberry that emphasizes quiet fruit, citrus and cocoa-nut sweetness over intensity, with a light-footed structure and pleasing balance.

title: Starlight Blend
blind_assessment: Intense sweetness suggesting honey and dried dates supports an impressive, layered complexity: cedar, ripe orange, roasted nut, hints of rose and strawberry. Juicy acidity; lively, syrupy mouthfeel. Rich, long, flavor-saturated finish.
notes: This blend is 100% Rainforest Alliance certified, meaning all component coffees were produced following sustainable ecological and socio-economic criteria developed by the Sustainable Agricultural Network, a coalition of independent, environment-focused non-governmental organizations. Caribou Coffee is a retail roasting chain based in the upper Middle West whose rather irreverent motto "Life is short. Stay awake for it" belies a serious approach to coffee. Visit www.cariboucoffee.com or call 888-227-4268 for more information.

title: Stars of Africa Blend
blind_assessment: Intense aroma: fresh-cut fir, brandy, cherry, a hint of nut. Rich, deep-toned acidity; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. Continued intensity in a complex and juicily sweet cup: lush dusk flowers, berry, brandied fruit, a hint of dark chocolate and a continued hint of fir. In the finish the opulent sweetness fades but flavor persists nicely.
notes: Cherry Smile is a brand of coffee established by Wei-Ming Zhuo, a leader in the Taiwan coffee community who is dedicated improving coffee knowledge and culture in Taiwan. Visit www.cherry-smile.com or call 886-938-362-368 for more information.

title: Stars of Formosa Blend
blind_assessment: Delicate hints of orange, flowers and roasted nut in the aroma. Gently bright-toned acidity, lightly syrupy mouthfeel with juicy suggestions of lemon, orange, stone fruit and more flowers with a pungent hint of fresh-cut fir. Superb finish: Long, sweet, complex, fruit-toned.
notes: Cherry Smile is a brand of coffee established by Wei-Ming Zhuo, a leader in the Taiwan coffee community who is dedicated to improving coffee knowledge and culture in Taiwan. Visit http://www.cherry-smile.com or call 886-938-362-368 for more information.

title: Stars of Italy Espresso
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Opulent, complex and big-bodied. Night flowers and a pronounced brandy-like fruit dominate aroma and the small cup, with a crisp, drying hint of cedar. Plump, syrupy mouthfeel. Long, flavor-saturated finish. Two parts milk turns the brandied fruit toward a minty dark chocolate with a continuing floral complication.
notes: Cherry Smile is a brand of coffee established by Wei-Ming Zhuo, a leader in the Taiwan coffee community who is dedicated improving coffee knowledge and culture in Taiwan. Visit http://www.cherry-smile.com or call 886 938 362 368 for more information.

title: Static Adado Shara
blind_assessment: Delicate, sweetly musk-toned. Singed sandalwood, dried lemon zest, malty chocolate, almond, gardenia in aroma and cup. Spice-toned in structure, crisply perfumy; buoyant, lean mouthfeel. The gently drying finish centers on citrus and chocolate in the short modulating to bittersweet aromatic wood in the long.
notes: Yirgacheffe is a coffee region in southern Ethiopia that produces distinctive coffees from traditional varieties of Arabica long grown in the region. Yirgacheffe coffees like this one processed by the wet or washed method (fruit skin and pulp are removed before drying) typically express great aromatic complexity and intensity with a particular emphasis on floral notes. Like virtually all Ethiopia coffees, this coffee is produced by villagers on small, garden plots interplanted with food and other subsistence crops. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: An interesting choice for those who prefer to find the sweetness in their cup expressed in floral and aromatic wood notes rather than in the more typical fruit.

title: Static Amaro Gayo Natural Ethiopia
blind_assessment: Crisply sweet, fruit-forward. Ripe strawberry, aromatic orchid, honey, toasted pine nut, a hint of sumac spice in aroma and cup. Lavish, elegant structure, with sweet-tart-savory in harmonious balance. Syrupy mouthfeel. The finish is resonant, long and flavor-saturated, maintaining the promise of the complex flavor notes from the cup.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 24 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 30 Coffees of 2017. Yirgacheffe is a coffee region in southern Ethiopia that produces distinctive coffees from traditional varieties of Arabica long grown in the region. This is a “natural” or dry-processed version, meaning the beans were dried inside the fruit, encouraging a flavor profile that is less predictable and deeper than the more familiar wet-processed floral- and citrus-toned Yirgacheffe profile. Like virtually all southern Ethiopia coffees, this coffee is produced by villagers on small, garden plots interplanted with food and other subsistence crops. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: A thrill of a natural-processed Ethiopia: fruit, florals and savory notes in intricate, lively harmony.

title: Static Colombia Decaf Midnight
blind_assessment: Deeply sweet, chocolate-toned. Dark chocolate, Brazil nut, gardenia, baked apple, cedar in aroma and cup. Roundly sweet in structure; lean, lightly syrupy body. The gently drying finish is characterized by notes of dark chocolate throughout, supported by gardenia and apple tones in the short and cedar in the long.
notes: Decaffeinated at the Descamex plant in Mexico by the “Mountain Water Process” which does not involve use of solvents. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: A solid, chocolate-toned decaf with inviting fruit and floral tones.

title: Static Cali Classic Espresso
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Deeply and richly sweet-tart, spice-toned. Dark chocolate, blood orange zest, licorice root, dried mango, caraway seed in aroma and small cup. Full, creamy mouthfeel; the finish moves from crisp, sweet cocoa tones in the short to caraway and licorice root in the long. In cappuccino-scaled milk, floral, fruit and savory spice tones richly converge.
notes: A blend of Arabica coffees from Ethiopia and Colombia, all processed by the wet-processed or “washed” method, meaning the fruit skin and pulp were removed from the beans immediately after harvesting and before drying. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: A deeply sweet, richly pungent espresso blend, compelling in its confident spice tones (caraway, licorice root) and balanced sweet-savory-tart structure.

title: Static Chirinos Peru
blind_assessment: Richly low-toned, gently zesty. Cedar, baker’s chocolate, grapefruit zest, apple, a hint of magnolia-like flowers in aroma and cup. Sweetly and quietly tart in structure, with a brisk edge. Plump mouthfeel. Flavor consolidates in a sweet, though rather drying, finish.
notes: Produced by some of the over 700 small-holding farmers of the La Prosperidad de Chirinos cooperative in northern Peru from trees of the Bourbon and Caturra varieties of Arabica. Processed by the wet or “washed” method, in which skin and fruit flesh are removed from the beans or seeds before they are dried. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: A quietly rich Peru, sweet yet briskly zesty.

title: Static Dark Star Mexico Espresso
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Baker’s chocolate, plum blossom, molasses, grapefruit zest, cedar in aroma and small cup. Crisp, lightly satiny mouthfeel; the finish consolidates around grapefruit zest and baker’s chocolate in the short, with notes of cedar returning in the long. In three parts milk, baker’s chocolate envelopes citrus zest and stone fruit notes in pleasing balance.
notes: A blend of Arabica coffees from Chiapas State, Mexico, all processed by the wet-processed or “washed” method, meaning the fruit skin and pulp were removed from the beans immediately after harvesting and before drying. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: An impressively balanced, energetic chocolate- and stonefruit-toned espresso from Mexico, an origin seldom show-cased in single-origin espressos.

title: Static Don Eli La Pastora Tarrazu Costa Rica
blind_assessment: Deeply rich, bittersweet, herbaceous. Almond brittle, date, mace, honeysuckle, eucalyptus leaf in aroma and cup. Crisply bittersweet structure; satiny, full mouthfeel. The finish consolidates to gently drying notes of date and almond.
notes: Produced by Don Eli of the Caturra and Catuai varieties of Arabica. Processed by the white honey method. With all honey processing methods, some sweet pulp or fruit flesh (“honey”) is allowed to adhere to the beans during drying. In the white honey variation, an extremely thin layer of pulp is allowed to dry on the beans, less than with yellow honey, and much less than is the case with red or black honey. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: A honey-processed Costa Rica cup, enticing for its high-toned, vivacious herb notes enveloped in suggestions of rich florals and sweet nuts.

title: Static El Salvador Finca Maria Luisa
blind_assessment: Brisk and subtly layered. Almond butter, dried apricot, fresh-cut fir, hints of dark chocolate and clover in aroma and cup. Sweetly brisk and dry in structure; lightly syrupy mouthfeel. The drying structure sweetens and smoothes a bit in the finish, and chocolate and clover-like flowers move forward.
notes: Processed by the wet or “washed” method, in which skin and fruit flesh are removed from the beans or seeds before they are dried. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: Those who value brisk, dry beverages should enjoy this coffee and its quiet, unorthodox aromatic intrigue.
coffee_origin: Santa Rosa, La Unión Department, El Salvador

title: Static Ethiopia Koke
blind_assessment: Sweetly roast-rounded. Baker’s chocolate, singed cedar, dried cherry, lily, Brazil nut in aroma and cup. Gently bittersweet structure with a hint of acidity; lightly creamy mouthfeel. The resonant finish is flavor-saturated, if short.
notes: Yirgacheffe is a coffee region in southern Ethiopia that produces distinctive coffees from traditional varieties of Arabica long grown in the region. This Yirgacheffe is processed by the honey method, an atypical process for Ethiopia, involving removing the outer skin as it is in the wet or "washed" method, but leaving at least some of the sticky fruit residue, or honey, to dry on the bean. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: An inviting honey-processed Ethiopia, with cocoa, fruit and floral notes both rounded and turned gently crisp by a tactful medium-dark roast.

title: Static Ethiopia Konga Washed
blind_assessment: Sweetly roast-toned. Dark chocolate, cinnamon, gently scorched cedar, roasted cashew, dried apricot in aroma and cup. Round, backgrounded acidity; impressively plump, velvety mouthfeel. The cocoa-toned finish is gently drying, with a spice-driven aromatic wood throughline.
notes: Yirgacheffe is a coffee region in southern Ethiopia that produces distinctive coffees from traditional varieties of Arabica long grown in the region. Yirgacheffe coffees like this one processed by the wet or washed method (fruit skin and pulp are removed before drying) typically express great aromatic complexity and intensity with a particular emphasis on floral notes. Like virtually all Ethiopia coffees, this coffee is produced by villagers on small, garden plots interplanted with food and other subsistence crops. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: A medium-dark roast nicely develops this wet-processed Ethiopia’s chocolate and spice notes. A good choice for those who enjoy strongly stated profiles.

title: Static Hacienda Sonora Costa Rica
blind_assessment: Subtle, engaging, deeply sweet-savory. Orange blossom, baker’s chocolate, cantaloupe, fresh pine, a hint of cinnamon in aroma and cup. Round, sweetly savory structure; taut, velvety body. The finish consolidates around quiet chocolate and almond notes.
notes: Produced from trees of the Caturra and Catuai varieties of Arabica by farmers Alberto and Diego Guardia of Sonora Estate in Costa Rica. Processed by the honey method (sometimes referred to as “semi-washed”), which means that the outer skin of the coffee fruit is removed as it is in the wet or “washed” process, but at least some of the sticky fruit residue is allowed to dry on the bean and later removed by machine along with the parchment skin. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: A simultaneously savory-leaning yet floral- and sweet-toned honey-processed coffee.

title: Static Indonesia Toarco Sulawesi
blind_assessment: Crisp, sweetly savory. Butterscotch, mesquite, cocoa powder, cooked acorn squash, fine musk in aroma and cup. Sweet-savory in structure with brisk acidity; lightly syrupy mouthfeel. The finish is carried, both short and long, by notes of cocoa and rich aromatic wood.
notes: Toarco (TOraja ARabica COffee) is a coffee project in the famous Sulawesi coffee growing region of Toraja developed and financed by Japan’s Key Coffee Company and its Indonesian partners. Toarco coffees are processed by variants of the orthodox wet or washed method, giving them a brighter and cleaner profile than Sulawesi coffees processed by the locally traditional wet-hulling method. Until recently Toarco sold its entire production to the Japanese market, making this coffee rare in the United States. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: A sweet, richly savory Sulawesi cup with a cocoa and mesquite throughline nuanced by butterscotch and fine musk.
coffee_origin: Toraja growing region, south-central Sulawesi, Indonesia

title: Static Kenya Kavutiri
blind_assessment: Delicate, sweetly spice-toned. Red currant, lemon verbena, baker’s chocolate, rose hips, a hint of cannabis in aroma and cup. Crisply sweet-savory structure; crisp, velvety mouthfeel. The finish is sweetly herb-toned, leading with notes of lemon verbena and red currant in the short and a sweet muskiness akin to cannabis in the long, with a throughline of baker’s chocolate.
notes: Produced by smallholding farmers from trees of the Ruiru 11, Batian, SL28 and SL34 varieties of Arabica. Despite grower discontent and urban encroachment on prime coffee lands, Kenya continues to produce some of the world’s most elegant and distinctive coffees. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: A delicate, spice-driven Kenya cup with engaging undercurrents of fruit, floral and chocolate.

title: Static Kenya Kirimahiga
blind_assessment: Richly sweet-savory. Brown sugar, baker’s chocolate, black currant, rye grain or flour, fine musk in aroma and cup. Balanced, sweet-savory structure; plush, syrupy mouthfeel. The resonant finish consolidates to notes of chocolate and black currant.
notes: Despite grower discontent and urban encroachment on prime coffee lands, Kenya continues to produce some of the world’s most elegant and distinctive coffees. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: An engaging, classic Kenya cup, with sweet and savory notes in balance, including an intriguing undertone suggesting the flavor of Russian rye bread.

title: Static Peaberry Cerrado Brazil
blind_assessment: Delicately earth-toned, floral. Toffee, violet, fresh-cut cedar, lime zest, a hint of apricot in aroma and cup. Round, sweetly savory structure; satiny-smooth mouthfeel. The short finish is resonant with notes of bittersweet aromatic wood and florals.
notes: A traditional Brazil dry-processed or "natural" coffee, meaning the beans were dried inside the fruit rather than after the fruit has been removed, as is the case with wet-processed or "washed" coffees. From the admired Cerrado growing region. This sample consists entirely of peaberries, a kind of bean that results when the coffee fruit develops only a single, oval bean rather than the usual pair of flat-sided beans. Peaberries produce a somewhat different (often better) cup than normal beans from the same crop, from which they may or may not be separated during grading. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: An aromatic-wood-framed Brazil peaberry with pretty floral undertones.
coffee_origin: Cerrado growing region, Minas Gerais State, Brazil

title: Static Peru Cajamarca
blind_assessment: Quietly and delicately crisp. Candied walnut, peach, honeysuckle, cedar, ripe banana in aroma and cup. Gently and sweetly brisk in structure; light, very silky in mouthfeel. Walnut, peach and cedar in particular carry into a sweet though drying finish.
notes: From Cenfrocafe Cooperative in northern Peru. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: A delicately brisk, sweetly nut-toned variation on the classically gentle Peru profile.

title: Static Peru Valle de Chingama Peru
blind_assessment: Deeply pungent and richly sweet. Lavender, baker’s chocolate, oak, ripe fig, a hint of ginger in aroma and cup. Roundly sweet-tart and juicy in structure; full and satiny in mouthfeel. Baker’s chocolate carries distinctly and pleasingly into an otherwise short finish.
notes: Produced by small-holding farmers in northern Peru from trees of the Bourbon, Caturra and Typica varieties of Arabica. Processed by the wet or “washed” method, in which skin and fruit flesh are removed from the beans or seeds before they are dried. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: A fine Peru, with the round, pungently chocolaty character of the type supported by crisp floral top notes and a plump, smooth mouthfeel.

title: Static Ravens Dark Roast Mexico
blind_assessment: Richly aromatic, wood-framed, bittersweet. Rhododendron, fresh mulch, dried apricot, saltwater taffy, molasses in aroma and cup. Bitter-leaning in structure; lean, silky mouthfeel. The finish is gently drying, with sweet mulch notes and vanilla-like florals.
notes: A blend of Arabica coffees from Chiapas State, Mexico, all processed by the wet-processed or “washed” method, meaning the fruit skin and pulp were removed from the beans immediately after harvesting and before drying. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: The bittersweet structure, dried fruit notes and vanilla-toned flowers pleasantly nudge this coffee toward a darker roast profile, even though this is a medium-roasted bean.

title: Static Rio Negro Colombia
blind_assessment: Delicate; crisply sweet-savory. Lemon blossom, roasted cacao nib, pink peppercorn, fresh fennel, plum in aroma and cup. Brisk, sweet-tart acidity; satiny-smooth mouthfeel. The quiet finish consolidates to cocoa-toned citrus notes in the short with suggestions of fresh fennel in the long.
notes: Produced from trees of the Bourbon, Caturra and Typica varieties of Arabica by multiple family farmers in the remote village of Rio Negro. This is a wet-processed or “washed” coffee, meaning the fruit skin and pulp were removed from the beans immediately after harvesting and before drying. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: A sweetly herbaceous, crisp, cocoa-toned Colombia cup.

title: Static Rio Negro Huila Supremo
blind_assessment: Delicate yet deep; sweetly spice-toned. Baker’s chocolate, cinnamon, black cherry, narcissus-like flowers, caraway seed in aroma and cup. Savory-sweet in structure; crisp, satiny mouthfeel. The finish consolidates around spice-framed wood and rich black cherry suggestions.
notes: Like almost all Colombia coffees, this coffee is wet-processed or “washed,” meaning the fruit skin and pulp were removed from the beans immediately after harvesting and before drying. Huila is one of Colombia’s most respected coffee-growing regions. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: A big-bodied Colombia that leads unapologetically and impressively with sweet-toned spice notes.

title: Static San Augustin Guatemala
blind_assessment: Deeply rich, sweetly smoky. Ripe banana, black peppercorn, singed clove, pipe tobacco, gardenia-like flowers in aroma and cup. The structure is dominated by a smoke-toned sweetness with spice undertones. Velvety smooth mouthfeel. Fruit tones carry the short finish, while gently drying pipe tobacco and clove re-emerge in the long.
notes: Produced by Ricardo Zelaya entirely of the Caturra variety of Arabica. This is a wet-processed or “washed” coffee, meaning the fruit skin and pulp were removed from the beans immediately after harvesting and before drying. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: A roast at the edge between medium and medium-dark promotes pleasant smoke notes in this Guatemala, while still allowing spice, fruit and floral notes to exert their presence and authority.

title: Static Santa Luzia Brazil
blind_assessment: Sweetly spice-toned. Gardenia, baker’s chocolate, green grape, pecan, black peppercorn in aroma and cup. Brisk, sweet-tart acidity; delicate, silky mouthfeel. The gently drying finish consolidates to notes of pecan and baker’s chocolate with hints of gardenia.
notes: This is a wet-processed or “washed” coffee, meaning the fruit skin and pulp were removed from the beans immediately after harvesting and before drying. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: An accessible, sweetly nut- and spice-toned Brazil cup.

title: Static Tio Emilio Pichincha Ecuador
blind_assessment: Crisply sweet, balanced. Maple syrup, rhododendron-like flowers, pear, hazelnut, cedar in aroma and cup. Briskly sweet acidity; silky mouthfeel. The flavor-saturated finish is resonant, if short.
notes: This is a wet-processed or “washed” coffee, meaning the fruit skin and pulp were removed from the beans immediately after harvesting and before drying. Espresso Republic, founded in 2010, specializes in sourcing quality coffees and roasting them in small batches for both retail and wholesale customers. Visit www.espressorepublic.com for more information.
bottom_line: An accessible, high-toned coffee with inviting pear, vanilla-like florals and aromatic wood notes.

title: Steep ‘N Deep Brew Bag
blind_assessment: Evaluated in brew bag format with a steeping time of 5 minutes in 8 ounces of water. Crisply sweet, nut-toned. Cocoa powder, pomegranate, almond, orange zest, magnolia in aroma and cup. Sweet-toned with brisk acidity; plush, creamy mouthfeel. Cocoa-toned finish supported by notes of orange zest and almond.
notes: Produced by Juana Delgado and processed by the traditional washed method (fruit skin and pulp removed before drying). Packaged in brew bag format by Steeped Coffee. Rick and Randy Evans founded Evans Brothers Coffee in 2009 focused on sourcing and roasting the finest small lots of seasonally available coffees in a context of sustainability and responsibility. Visit www.evansbrotherscoffee.com or call 208-265-5553 for more information.
bottom_line: A sweetly nut-toned single-origin Guatemala brew bag, crisply chocolaty with tart fruit and bittersweet citrus complications.

title: Stella Espresso
blind_assessment: Reviewed as espresso. Tart, raspberry-like fruit balanced by a dark chocolate and almond sweetness in aroma and small cup. Gently syrupy mouthfeel; crisply chocolaty finish. In two parts milk the tart fruit character turns rich and deep, supported by a chocolate predictably milk-sweetened.
notes: Caldi Coffee is a small coffeehouse located in Tao-yuan City, Taiwan that devotes itself to providing “splendid coffee” at affordable prices. Visit http://www.caldicafe.url.tw/caldi/module.php or call +886-3-3364965 for more information.

title: Strawberry Chloris Coffee Blend
blind_assessment: Delicately sweet-tart, fruity. Strawberry, magnolia, almond, cedar, dark chocolate. Briskly sweet structure; lightly syrupy mouthfeel. Sweetly wood-framed finish supported by strawberry and almond.
notes: A blend of two coffees, a double-anaerobic enzyme-washed Colombia and an anaerobic natural Yunnan, China. Entrebox is a specialty coffee roaster based in Hong Kong. Visit www.entreboxhk.com for more information.
bottom_line: A distinctly strawberry-toned blend with supporting notes of sweet nut, dark chocolate and rich aromatic wood.

title: Strawberry Forest
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Chocolaty and fruit-toned. Ripe blueberry, baking chocolate, gardenia, fir, caramel in aroma and small cup. Full, syrupy mouthfeel; gently drying, wood-framed finish. In three parts milk, balanced, chocolate-toned and fruity.
notes: A blend comprised of a natural-processed Ethiopia and a washed-process Nicaragua, roasted for espresso applications. David's Nose Coffee is a specialty coffee roaster based in Taipei, Taiwan whose founder studied agronomy and has a deep interest in crop quality. For more information, visit www.davidsnosecoffee.com.
bottom_line: A half-natural, half-washed blend of coffees from Ethiopia and Nicaragua, respectively, that net a chocolaty, fruit-driven espresso.

title: Strawberry Meets Lemon
blind_assessment: Deeply sweet, crisply fruit-toned, richly aromatic. Strawberry jam, pink grapefruit, cocoa nib, and jasmine, lemon verbena in aroma and cup. florals lead in a cup that is both intensely expressive and surprisingly composed. Bright, sweetly tart acidity; lightly syrupy mouthfeel. The finish has lingering notes of berry preserves, citrus candy, and delicate fermented fruit.
notes: A blend of coffees from Thailand (double-anaerobic coferment), Colombia (both washed and cofermented) and Ethiopia (washed). Bargain Cafe is a specialty coffee roaster in Taitung, Taiwan. Visit www.bargain-cafe.com for more information.
bottom_line: An unabashedly contemporary, fruit-driven blend that layers cofermented coffees with finesse and clarity, delivering a cup that is playful and aromatic without tipping into excess.

title: Strawberry Shadow
blind_assessment: Juicy, playful, deeply aromatic. Strawberry jam, dark chocolate, blood orange, hibiscus, sugarcane in aroma and cup. Gently fruity acidity; lush, creamy mouthfeel. The finish is long and flavor-saturated, led by strawberry and dark chocolate notes.
notes: Produced from two Colombia coffees — a washed process from Huila Department and a honey mossto carbonic maceration from Quindío Department. Founded in 2013, modcup focuses on fresh roasting and distinctive natural-processed coffees. This special release is available to members of modcup’s Deepcuts list. Visit modcup.com for more information.
bottom_line: A distinctive two-region Colombia blend that marries the origin’s classic sweetness with contemporary fermentation-driven fruit intensity.

title: Stubble Man Espresso
blind_assessment: Evaluated as espresso. Crisply cocoa-toned, quietly complex. Baker’s chocolate, fresh-cut cedar, apricot jam, anise in aroma and small cup. Satiny mouthfeel. Chocolate and cedar carry into a resonant though drying finish. Surprisingly buttery and fat in three parts milk, with continued apricot and cedar notes.
notes: Kevin Lin, the owner of HuZaZa Café, likes to relax and enjoy good coffees, and the coffees he serves at his Shanghai café are designed to provide that experience to customers. Located in a very competitive business area, HuZaZa Café offers an opportunity to slow down and enjoy life. Email panda.taipei@gmail.com or call +86-1306-160-8697 for more information.

title: Stuck in the Middle
blind_assessment: Lightly scorched cedar dominates in aroma and cup, complicated by dark chocolate, cardamom-like spice and hints of flowers and lemon. Roast-muted acidity. Leanish though smooth mouthfeel. Chocolate moves forward in a simple but sweet finish.
notes: This coffee has been treated to reduce acids and the acidy sensation that may create gastric discomfort in some people. The acid-reduction procedure is applied to the coffee in its green state, before roasting, and is entirely “natural,” meaning only hot water and steam are used. The acidy sensation is further reduced by a relatively dark roast. TruCup is a Seattle, Washington based roaster that differentiates itself by specializing in low-acid coffee. Visit www.trucup.com or call 855-287-8287 for more information.

title: Subrosa Ethiopia Kayon Mountain Organic Natural
blind_assessment: Gently sweet-tart, cocoa-toned. Cocoa nib, orange, narcissus, mango, cedar in aroma and cup. Intricately sweet, bright, with brisk acidity; full, syrupy mouthfeel. The quietly sweet finish consolidates to cocoa-toned mango and cedar.
notes: Produced by Ato Esmael and his friends and family at their estate farm in the Guji Zone of southern Ethiopia. Certified organic and produced from distinctive, largely indigenous landrace varieties of Arabica long grown in the region. Processed by the dry or “natural” method, meaning the beans were dried inside the fruit rather than after the fruit has been removed, as is the case with wet-processed or “washed” coffees. Available at any States Coffee café location in the San Francisco East Bay area. States Coffee, established in 2015, is a small-batch roastery and bakery that offers coffee, bread and baked goods. For more information on locations and hours visit www.statescoffee.com.
bottom_line: A natural-processed Ethiopia cup driven by tropical fruit and floral tones, with a throughline of cocoa nib.
coffee_origin: Odo Shakiso District, Guji Zone, Oromia region, southern Ethiopia

title: Sudan Rume
blind_assessment: Rich-toned, deeply sweet-savory. Black cherry, almond nougat, hop flowers, cedar, marjoram in aroma and cup. Richly bittersweet structure with gentle, round acidity; very full, syrupy mouthfeel. The finish leads with bittersweet floral notes that suggest hop flowers, with undertones of stone fruit and almond nougat.
notes: Produced from trees of the ancient Sudan Rume variety of Arabica and processed by the washed method with a cold ferment. Lina Premium Coffee is a Bogota-based specialty coffee roaster that works with and supports Colombian farms and farmers. Visit www.linapremiumcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A compelling version of the rare Sudan Rume variety — complex, multi-layered, richly savory-leaning.

title: Sudan Rume
blind_assessment: Complex, sweetly and intricately herbaceous, citrusy. Lemon verbena, cardamom, cocoa nib, ginger, aromatic orchid in aroma and cup. Sweetly savory with delicately juicy acidity; crisp, silky mouthfeel. Long, resonant, flavor-saturated finish.
notes: Comprised entirely of beans from the rare Sudan Rume, a presumably very old variety of Arabica originally selected from wild trees growing on the Boma Plateau of Sudan, close to the border with Ethiopia. Produced by Rigoberto Herrera at Granja La Esperanza in Colombia. Fermented in the whole fruit, then fermented again after the skins are removed. JBC Coffee Roasters’ vision is simple: “let the coffee lead the way” through sourcing and roasting the best and most unique coffees available and rewarding the farmers who grow those coffees with substantial premiums. Visit www.jbccoffeeroasters.com or call 608-256-5282 for more information.
bottom_line: A striking and original version of the rare Sudan Rume variety of Arabica: all spice, herbs and cocoa.

title: Sudan Rume
blind_assessment: Spice-toned, delicate and deep. Cardamom, black tea, bergamot, honeysuckle, sandalwood in aroma and cup. Sweet-savory structure with juicy acidity; full, syrupy-smooth mouthfeel. Flavor-saturated finish leads with cardamom and bergamot, rounding to honeysuckle-toned sandalwood in the long.
notes: Comprised entirely of beans from the rare Sudan Rume, a presumably very old variety of Arabica originally selected from wild trees growing on the Boma Plateau of Sudan, close to the border with Ethiopia. Produced by Rigoberto Herrera at Granja La Esperanza in Colombia and processed by the wet, or washed, method. Founded in 2013, modcup coffee focuses on fresh roasting and distinctive natural-processed coffees. Visit modcup.com for more information.
bottom_line: An exciting cup from a rare varietal that, in this incarnation, is richly cocoa-toned and spice-laden, complex and multi-layered.
coffee_origin: Valle del Cauca growing region, Colombia

title: Sulawesi
blind_assessment: Replete with earth, leather, and vaguely animal and forest notes. In structure leans more toward the bitter side of bittersweet, but blooms with chocolate opulence for a moment toward the finish.
notes: "Develop a nose for coffee," declares Plantation Coffee 's website, over a fisheye-lens photo of owner Dan Davis 's own personal facial appendage. Plantation is a quality-oriented wholesale roaster founded in 1994 in the Sacramento, California suburb of Elk Grove.

title: Sulawesi
blind_assessment: Lushly high-toned, remarkably complex aroma: flowers (tea-rose?), temperate fruit (pear perhaps), milk chocolate. Slumps toward a lower-key bittersweet character in the cup with only occasional glimpses of chocolate, but the giddy floral top notes persist. Slightly shallow finish.
notes: Sulawesi coffee, grown in the mountains at the southwestern-reaching tip of the Indonesian island of Sulawesi (formerly Celebes) near the port of Ujung Pandang (formerly Makassar), typically offers a more extreme version of the traditional Sumatra Mandheling cup, heavier, more pungent, more ambiguous. Dazbog is a specialty coffee company founded by two brothers who immigrated from Saint Petersburg (then Leningrad) in the old Soviet Union. The Dazbog package carries the retro bold red and black geometry of Russian Constructivist design. Visit www.dazbog.com or call 888-932-9264 for more info.
coffee_origin: Toraja (also Kalosi) growing region, southwestern Sulawesi, Indonesia

title: Sulawesi
blind_assessment: Aroma of cedary wood and roasty chocolate, with a faint hint of earthiness. In the cup, medium body, leanish mouthfeel and flavor dominated by sweet-toned aromatic wood that lingers into a long, dry, mildly roasty finish.
notes: Coffee from the Toraja region of Sulawesi, once Celebes, typically displays a wild and often earth-toned character, the result of unorthodox methods of fruit removal and drying. Tully's is a large quality-oriented specialty roasting company and caf? chain based in Seattle. Visit www.tullys.com or call 800-968-8559 for more information.

title: Sulawesi Bolokan
blind_assessment: Earth-toned, subtly floral. Plum, fresh-cut cedar, muscovado sugar, coriander seed, dark molasses in aroma and cup. Gently tart structure with balanced, winey acidity; dense, satiny mouthfeel. The finish emphasizes plum and molasses, with a faint echo of spice and floral wood.
notes: This exceptional coffee was selected as the No. 38 coffee on Coffee Review’s list of the Top 50 Coffees of 2025. Produced at Rantekarua Estate, entirely of the S795 variety of Arabica, and processed by the natural method (dried in the whole fruit). Certified USDA Organic. Rusty Dog Coffee is a Madison, Wisconsin-based specialty coffee roaster. Visit www.rustydogcoffee.com for more information.
bottom_line: A deep and resonant Sulawesi profile, this cup leans into rich fruit and spice, grounded by sweet earth tones and a whisper of floral complexity.
coffee_origin: Bolokan Valley, Tana Toraja Regency, Sulawesi, Indonesia

title: Sulawesi (Celebes) Medium Roast
blind_assessment: Reader Ben Anderson calls this coffee "fantastic." That familiar adjectivefreshens up when applied to Sulawesi coffees, whose unexpected forest and fruit notes often doseem to express a sort of adventurous coffee fantasy. When hot, this Sulawesi displayed a richcup with a fine balance of acidity, sweetness and roastiness plus - the Sulawesi factor - carnally rich fruit notes reminiscent of cantaloupe. I started with a rating of over 90, but as the cup cooleda slight salty astringency in the finish lowered my assessment.
notes: The rugged mountains north of the port city of Makasar on the Indonesian island ofSulawesi are the coffee equivalent of Islay in the world of scotch whiskeys, producing coffeesthat are often startling in their quirky, earth-toned variety. Green Mountain Coffee Roasters isone of the country's leading specialty roasters, offering a particularly wide-ranging variety oforigins and roast styles, including a comprehensive selection of Fair-Trade/organic coffees. Visit www.greenmountaincoffee.com or call 800-223-6768 for more information.
coffee_origin: Toraja/Kalossi growing district, southwestern Sulawesi, Indonesia.

title: Sulawesi Kalossi DP
blind_assessment: Another coffee in which the hard tones characteristic of many traditionally processed Indonesian coffees are precariously mellowed by an ingratiating sweetness. The combination of (perhaps musty) sharpness and sweetness hints at chocolate, particularly in the finish.
notes: As in many traditionally processed Indonesian coffees, hard tones are precariously mellowed by ingratiating sweetness, with hints of chocolate, particularly in the finish. Processed by traditional Indonesian methods. Celebes is the old, Dutch name for the island of Sulawesi and Kalossi the Dutch name for the region the Indonesians now call Toraja.

title: Sulawesi PT Toarco
blind_assessment: Quietly distinctive; resonant. Honey, dark chocolate, hazelnut, sweetly pungent fruit (cherimoya?) in aroma and cup. Round but juicy acidity; lively, syrupy mouthfeel. Chocolate sweetness dominates in a long, gently persistent finish.
notes: Toarco (TOraja ARabica COffee) is a coffee project in the famous Sulawesi coffee growing region of Toraja developed and financed by Japan's Key Coffee Company and its Indonesian partners. Toarco coffees are processed by variants of the orthodox wet or washed method, giving them a brighter and cleaner profile than Sulawesi coffees processed by the locally traditional wet-hulling method. Until recently Toarco sold its entire production to the Japanese market, making this coffee rare in the United States. Propeller is a relatively new Toronto-based micro-roaster with a dedication to careful selection and exceptional craft roasting of high-end coffees, the outgrowth of five years of successful business as the three-location Crema Coffee café chain. Visit www.propellercoffee.com or call 416-479-3771 for more information.
coffee_origin: Toraja growing region, southwestern Sulawesi, Indonesia

title: Sulawesi Pulupulu Toraja
blind_assessment: Deep-toned, balanced coffee. Gently tart acidity, lean but silky mouthfeel. Cherryish fruit with a hint of lemon and a lean toward chocolate dominate aroma and cup, coasting into a long, sweet finish.
notes: Coffee from the Toraja region of the Indonesian island of Sulawesi, once Celebes, typically displays a wild and often earth-toned character, the result of the unorthodox "wet-hulled" method of fruit removal and drying. However, the clean sweetness and balance of this particular Sulawesi suggests it is a more conventional wet-processed or "washed" coffee. With two locations in Southern California's Orange County, Kean Coffee is an in-house coffee roaster and retailer established by Martin Diedrich of the famous Diedrich coffee family. The Kean slogan, "Martin knows his beans" should be true, considering Martin grew up in Guatemala where the family owned a coffee farm.Visit www.keancoffee.com or call 949-933-9164 for more information.
coffee_origin: Toraja growing region, southwestern Sulawesi, Indonesia

title: Sulawesi Tana Toraja
blind_assessment: Deep, round, gently bright. Aprium, malt, lily-like flowers, baker’s chocolate, a hint of moist fallen leaves in aroma and cup. Sweet-toned, softly tart acidity; light, buoyant mouthfeel. Flavor consolidates in a long, sweet, very slightly drying finish.
notes: This coffee originates from the Toarco (TOraja ARabica COffee) project in the famous Sulawesi coffee growing region of Toraja, a project developed and financed by Japan’s Key Coffee Company and its Indonesian partners.
